$r>2^{2d+1}(2qu+v)$ into the first term gives (HG).
\src{BIB, thm:v75-high-gap}
\end{proof}
\begin{warning}[Hypothesis, restated]
Warning~\ref{warn:highgap} applies verbatim: the hypothesis is
\emph{Exact-D pair failure}, not CRD failure. Using $h^2>4m_0$ under canonical
failure alone is an error.
\end{warning}

\begin{corollary}[Quadratic canonical gap filter]\label{cor:quadgapfilter}
\PROVEDs. With
$\Lambda:=4^dgv^2+2^{2d-1}\frac{gv^3}{qu}+\frac{v}{2u}$ and $h<G$,
\[
\boxed{\ p_0<2G+\frac{G^2}{\Lambda}<2G+\frac{G^2}{4^dgv^2}\le2G+\frac{G^2}4.\ }
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{statusbox}{cComp}
\textbf{Finite check of the quadratic filter.} \VERIFCOMP\ \emph{as reported by
the source}. An exact check to $p_0\le10^9$ found no canonical failure
satisfying the filter $p_0<2G+G^2/4$; of the candidates only $p_0=11$ passed,
and it admits no permissible pair of distinct roots. This is a finite
verification, not a global proof. --- \emph{reported computational result, not
reproduced in this document.}
\end{statusbox}

\subsection{The branch $k=1$}

For $k=1$ one has $g=v=1$, so $t=q+r$, $m_0=qru$ with $u\ge3$ odd, and exactly
$D_q=r$, $M_q=2qu+1$, $D_r=q$, $M_r=2ru+1$.

\begin{theorem}[$k=1$ high-gap strengthening]\label{thm:k1gap}
\PROVEDs. For $k=1$ every pair failure satisfies
\[
\boxed{\ r>4^{d+1}qu^2,\qquad \frac{h^2}{m_0}>4^du,\ }
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
\boxed{\ p_0<2G+\frac{G^2}{4^du}\le2G+\frac{G^2}{12}.\ }
\]
The only non-automatic SMOOTH condition on the larger row is
$\boxed{\PFp(2ru+1)<qu}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Failure gives $(2qu+1)(2ru+1)\le(r-q)^2/4^d<r^2/4^d$; the lower bounds on both
factors give $r>4^{d+1}qu^2$. Then
$\frac{h^2}{m_0}=\frac{(q+r)^2}{4qru}>\frac{r}{4qu}>4^du$, and the filter for
$p_0$ follows from $h<G$. The condition $u\ge3$ is necessary: at $u=1$ the
factor $r=D_q=B_q$ breaks the strict SMOOTH threshold.
\src{BIB, thm:v75-k1-gap}
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[$k=1$ quotient normal form]\label{thm:k1quotient}
\PROVEDs. With $A:=2qu+1$, $B:=2ru+1$ one has exactly
\[
q=\frac{A-1}{2u},\qquad r=\frac{B-1}{2u},\qquad A\equiv B\equiv3\pmod4,
\]
\[
\boxed{4um_0=(A-1)(B-1)},\quad
\boxed{4uh=A+B-2},\quad
\boxed{4ux=AB-1},\quad
\boxed{4up_0=AB+A+B-3},
\]
\[
\boxed{\ up_0+1=\frac{(A+1)(B+1)}4=(qu+1)(ru+1).\ }
\]
Moreover $d=v_2(B-A)-1$ and $\delta=\frac{B-A}{2^{d+1}u}$; pair failure is
equivalent to
\[
\boxed{\ 4^{d+1}u^2AB\le(B-A)^2,\ }
\]
SMOOTH of the larger row reads $\boxed{\PFp(B)<\frac{A-1}2}$, and canonicity
reads
\[
\boxed{\ \Bigl[\frac{AB-1}{4u},\ \frac{AB+A+B-3}{4u}\Bigr)\cap\PP=\varnothing\ }
\]
with prime endpoint $p_0=\frac{AB+A+B-3}{4u}$.
\src{BIB, thm:v75-k1-quotient}
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[The continued-fraction relation, and why it is not a descent]
\label{rem:k1cf}
With $a:=qu+1=\frac{A+1}2$ and $b:=ru+1=\frac{B+1}2$ one has
$\boxed{ab-up_0=1}$, and the Euclidean algorithm gives explicitly
\[
\boxed{\ \frac a{p_0}=[0;r,u,q],\qquad \frac ub=[0;r,u].\ }
\]
The modular-inverse relation is therefore an exact relation between consecutive
convergents --- but by itself it supplies no descent. Compare the
\emph{Matched Euclidean Gluing Lemma} recorded as missing in
\S\ref{sec:litverdicts}.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Structured composite coverage in the prime-free interval]
\label{prop:k1coverage}
\PROVEDs. For odd $s$ with $\frac{r-q}{2q}<s<\frac rq$, the number $z=r-sq$
satisfies $0<z<h$ and
\[
\boxed{\ p_0-z=q(ru+s+1).\ }
\]
Moreover for every prime $\ell\mid B$,
$\boxed{2up_0\equiv qu-1\pmod\ell}$, hence $\boxed{\gcd(B,qu-1)=1}$. Each such
$\ell$ covers exactly one residue class among the shifts $p_0-2j$, and under
pair failure the number of its hits in $0<2j<h$ is at least $4^du$.
\src{BIB, prop:v75-k1-coverage}
\end{proposition}

\begin{target}[Canonical $k=1$ gap/covering barrier]\label{tgt:k1barrier}
\OPENs. The canonical branch $k=1$ has \emph{not} been eliminated. The present
apparatus produces a gap filter, a smooth-shift condition and a covering
requirement, but no contradiction. This is the sharpest surviving remnant of
the Exact-D programme and is a self-contained problem: exhibit a canonical
$k=1$ Exact-D pair failure, or prove none exists.
\src{BIB, Canonical $k=1$ Gap/Covering Barrier}
\end{target}

\section{Sparse geometric core locks (FFS layer)}\label{sec:ffslocks}

\begin{summarybox}
The factor-flow-system (FFS) layer of the Biblia proves that \emph{collision
compression must be paid for with geometry}. These results are stated for a
finite factor-closed core $C$ of a prime affine FFS; the Goldbach
specialisations take $\delta=2$ because all active primes are odd. Statuses are
the source's own: \tid{tagN} = source claim ``new, proved'' and \tid{tagG} =
Goldbach specialisation, both imported as \PENDINGRT.
\end{summarybox}

\begin{definition}[Collision multiplexing ratio]\label{def:kappacol}
For a finite factor-closed core $C$ let $\eta(C)=\Om(J_C)>0$, let $\chi(C)$ be
the minimal number of distinct parent-pairs in a collision witness forest, and
put
\[
\boxed{\ \kappa_{\mathrm{col}}(C):=\frac{\eta(C)}{\chi(C)}\ge1.\ }
\]
$\kappa_{\mathrm{col}}=1$ means no multiplexing: each unit of collision excess
needs its own pair. A value above $1$ means some witness pairs carry several
distinct prime labels at once.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Multiplex collision rigidity, \tid{B-MULTIPLEX-RIGID}]
\label{thm:multiplexrigid}
\PENDINGRT. With $m=\min C$, $D=\max C-\min C$, $\eta=\Om(J_C)>0$ and
$\chi=\chi(C)$,
\[
\boxed{\ D\ \ge\ \delta\,m^{\eta/\chi}=\delta\,m^{\kappa_{\mathrm{col}}(C)}.\ }
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Closure puts every child in $C$, so every prime label occurring in $J_C$ is at
least $m$ and $J_C\ge m^\eta$. Choose a collision witness forest realising
$\chi$; lattice collision divisibility bounds each of its $\chi$ aggregated
labels by $D/\delta$, and the product of the aggregated labels is exactly
$J_C$, so $J_C\le(D/\delta)^\chi$. Combine and take $\chi$-th roots.
\src{BIB, Multiplex Collision Rigidity}
\end{proof}
\emph{Reading.} If many independent collision-excess labels are packed into few
parent-pairs, those pairs must be extremely far apart: at
$\kappa_{\mathrm{col}}=2$ the diameter grows at least quadratically in the
minimal atom, at $3$ at least cubically. Topological excess is converted into a
power lower bound for the diameter.

\begin{corollary}[Goldbach collision-compression barrier]\label{cor:compbarrier}
\PENDINGRT. Let $C$ be a terminal bad SCC of the graph for even $N$ that is not
a pure support cycle, $m=\min C$, $D=\max C-\min C$. Then
$\boxed{D\ge2m^{\eta/\chi}}$, and since $\max C<N/3$,
\[
\boxed{\ m<\Bigl(\frac N6\Bigr)^{\chi/\eta}.\ }
\]
In particular for every integer $t\ge2$:
$\boxed{\eta\ge t\chi\Rightarrow m<(N/6)^{1/t}}$; equivalently a hypothetical
core with $m>N^{1/t}$ must satisfy $\boxed{\eta<t\chi}$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
All active primes are odd, so $\delta=2$; apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:multiplexrigid} and $\max C<N/3$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:highroot}).
\end{proof}
\emph{Reading.} This converts a structural question into a very concrete one:
instead of killing all large cores directly, it suffices to exhibit
\emph{triple} collision multiplexing in the relevant class. It does not solve
Goldbach --- $\chi$ may be close to $\eta$, recovering only a linear diameter
barrier.

\begin{corollary}[Sparse Geometric Core Lock, \tid{B-SPARSE-CORE-LOCK}]
\label{cor:sparsecorelock}
\PENDINGRT. Under the same hypotheses, for every collision witness forest with
$\chi_\tau$ distinct parent-pairs,
\[
\boxed{\ N-1\ \le\ U_CJ_C\ \le\ U_C\Bigl(\frac D2\Bigr)^{\chi_\tau},\ }
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
\boxed{\ D\ \ge\ 2\Bigl(\frac{N-1}{U_C}\Bigr)^{1/\chi_\tau}.\ }
\]
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
For a terminal bad SCC the unit-slope product lock gives $T_C=U_CJ_C\ge N-1$,
and lattice collision divisibility with $\delta=2$ gives
$J_C\le(D/2)^{\chi_\tau}$. \src{BIB, Sparse Geometric Core Lock}
\end{proof}
\begin{remark}
Unlike the older bound $U_CG_C\ge N-1$, the right-hand side here uses only the
\emph{sparse} family of parent-pairs needed to realise the collision fibres.
It is a geometric version of exact-$J$, not a product over all pairwise gcds of
rows.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Quantitative support explosion]\label{thm:supportexplosion}
\PENDINGRT. Let $S$ be a finite subsystem of an exact prime affine FFS and
$K_\tau(S)$ any collision witness product. Put
\[
\mathcal M(S)=P_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\frac{\prod_{p\in S}R(p)}{\prod_{p\in S}p},
\qquad B_S=\max_{p\in S}R(p).
\]
If $A_S:=\mathcal M(S)/\bigl(U_SK_\tau(S)\bigr)>1$ then the number of distinct
boundary atoms satisfies
\[
\boxed{\ |\partial S|\ \ge\ \Bigl\lceil\frac{\log A_S}{\log B_S}\Bigr\rceil,\ }
\]
and more generally
$\mathcal M(S)>U_SK_\tau(S)B_S^r\Rightarrow|\partial S|\ge r+1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The geometric escape criterion gives $R_\partial(S)\ge A_S$. Every boundary atom
divides some $R(p)$, hence is at most $B_S$, and $R_\partial$ is a product of
$|\partial S|$ distinct primes, so $R_\partial(S)\le B_S^{|\partial S|}$. Take
logarithms and use integrality. \src{BIB, Quantitative Support Explosion}
\end{proof}
\emph{Reading.} The escape criterion is not merely ``$R_\partial>1$''; the same
computation can force \emph{many} new boundary atoms. Together with
Corollary~\ref{cor:sparsecorelock} the FFS layer therefore has two independent
elimination mechanisms, one for existence of escape and one for its
multiplicity.

% =====================================================================
\chapter{Canonical Root Dynamics (CRD)}\label{ch:crd}
% =====================================================================

\section{Epistemic convention}\label{sec:crdconv}

\begin{navbox}
CRD is a \emph{reformulation}, not a mechanism. Its content is:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the failed world is a closed bad set with a unique source
(Lemma~\ref{lem:closure});
\item the union of all closed bad sets below $N/3$ is computable by a
decreasing filtration (Definition~\ref{def:crdfilt});
\item canonical failure is exactly membership of $\PF(N-p_0)$ in that fixed
point (Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedpoint}).
\end{enumerate}
Anything beyond that --- capacity arguments, container arguments, spectral
arguments --- belongs to the successor theories of \S\ref{sec:successors} and
is \KILLED. When reading older CRD material, keep this boundary in mind: the
three items above survived every audit; the rest did not.
\end{navbox}

\section{The architecture wall}\label{sec:crdwall}

\begin{theorem}[Finite Affine Canonical Programmability]\label{thm:facp}
\PROVEDs\ in \src{PCRD} (proof not reproduced here), class A as a statement
about canonicity. For any finite family of affine forms $L_j(P)=a_jP+b_j$ and
any prescribed finite valuation and compositeness conditions, under the
standard coprimality conditions there exist --- by the Chinese remainder
theorem and Dirichlet's theorem --- infinitely many primes $P$ realising the
whole pattern. Setting $N=2(P-1)$ gives canonical $p_0=P$, $h=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Partial BAD-transcript programmability; scope-corrected]\label{thm:fbtu}
\SCOPECORR. Compatible prescribed finite BAD edges and edge valuations can be
programmed in canonical $h=1$ worlds by CRT/Dirichlet methods, as formalised by
\tid{CRT-TRANSCRIPT-EXACT-SCOPE-20260905}. The theorem controls the selected
requirements only. It does \emph{not} assert that every unprescribed prime
factor of an expanded row is BAD, nor that a complete BFS neighbourhood of a
prescribed depth is BAD. The earlier blanket reading of FBTU is withdrawn.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Partial-transcript no-go; not a complete-BFS wall]\label{cor:wall}
\SCOPECORR. A contradiction cannot follow merely from the existence of a
finite compatible \emph{selected} divisibility/valuation transcript, because
such a transcript may be realised in canonical worlds with extra cofactors.
This corollary does \textbf{not} rule out a theorem controlling a complete
bounded-depth BFS frontier. The exact $N=92$ certificate in
\S\ref{sec:post481-fbtu} shows why the quantifiers differ: a selected BAD cycle
coexists with a depth-$1$ GOOD child.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[Link to the phase diagram]\label{rem:h1typeI}
All $h=1$ worlds with $G\ge4$ lie in phase Type~I
(Theorem~\ref{thm:phase}), hence have $m_0$ composite and $\rho_0=0$. The whole
$h=1$ programme of \src{PCRD} therefore lives \emph{inside a single phase} ---
the one in which the reflection gate gives no guarantee. Two reported
witnesses, verified here:
\[
\begin{array}{r|r|r|l|l}
N & p_0 & G & m_0 & \text{type, depth}\\\hline
103\,344 & 51\,673 & 14 & 51\,671=163\cdot317 & \text{Type I},\ d=4\\
364\,844 & 182\,423 & 6 & 182\,421=3^2\cdot20\,269 & \text{Type I},\ d=6
\end{array}
\]
\VERIFCOMP.
\end{remark}

\section{C0a --- the small-gap canonical obligation}\label{sec:C0a}

\begin{theorem}[Small-gap residual closure, \texttt{C0a}]\label{thm:c0a}
\PROVEDs, class C. \emph{Hypotheses:} canonical failure, $h\le2$. Then
$h\in\{1,2\}$, $m_0$ is odd composite, $Q\ne\varnothing$, and
\[
\boxed{\ \max\{U_R,J_R,B_{\mathrm{abs}}\}>
\Bigl[\bigl(\tfrac53\bigr)^{|Q|}\rad(m_0)\Bigr]^{1/3}>1.\ }
\]
\src{CORE, C0a-RESIDUAL-CLOSURE}
\end{theorem}
\emph{Reading.} For $h\le2$ the reflected block is empty, so boundary geometry
gives nothing; the theorem replaces it by a nonzero obligation on the row side.
\emph{Limitation:} it yields neither a path to GOOD nor a capacity
contradiction.

\section{C0b --- the exact canonical reflection-defect ledger}\label{sec:C0b}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{C0b-RD}]\label{thm:c0brd}
\PROVEDs, class A\,+\,C. \emph{Hypotheses:} canonical failure, $N\ge50$,
$h\ge3$. With $t=\lfloor(h-1)/2\rfloor$ and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal I&=\{j:\PF(c_j)\cap R\ne\varnothing,\ a_j\in\Aset\}, &
\mathcal D&=\{j:\PF(c_j)\cap R\ne\varnothing,\ a_j\notin\Aset\},\\
\mathcal S&=\{j:\PF(c_j)\cap R=\varnothing,\ \PFp(c_j)<h\}, &
\mathcal F&=\{j:\PF(c_j)\cap R=\varnothing,\ \PFp(c_j)\ge h\},
\end{aligned}
\]
one has
\[
\boxed{\ \mathcal J_h=\mathcal I\uplus\mathcal D\uplus
\mathcal S\uplus\mathcal F\ }
\]
and for $j\in\mathcal F$ the number $\ell_j=\PFp(c_j)$ is active, lies outside
$R$, and occurs in exactly one element of $\mathfrak B(p_0)$. Moreover, if
$\mathcal I=\varnothing$ and $k=\lceil t/3\rceil$, then at least one of
\[
\sum_{j\in\mathcal D}\Om(a_j)\ge2k,\qquad
\sum_{j\in\mathcal S}\Om(c_j)>k\frac{\log x}{\log h},\qquad
\prod_{\ell\in\Lambda_{\mathcal F}}\ell\ge h^k
\]
holds. With $Q_\le=\{q\in Q:q\le t+1\}\ne\varnothing$ and $j(q)\equiv h\pmod q$,
$1\le j(q)\le q-1$, one has $q\mid c_{j(q)}$,
$j(q)\in\mathcal I\cup\mathcal D$ and
$B_\le<h^{|\mathscr J_\le|}$; and if $Q_\le=\varnothing$ then
$\mathfrak F_Q>\bigl(5(t+1)/3\bigr)^{|Q|}$.
\src{CORE, C0b-RD}
\end{theorem}
\emph{Reading.} This is the strongest \emph{quantitative} obligation that
canonical boundary geometry issues at all: every coordinate of the reflected
block must land in one of the four classes.
\emph{Known limitation:} \texttt{C0b-RD} supplies neither a path to GOOD nor a
capacity bound.

\begin{scopenote}[Why the hypothesis $Q_\le\ne\varnothing$ is needed]
\label{scope:qle}
\SCOPECORR. In version v1 this condition was omitted; with
$Q_\le=\varnothing$ the inequality would read $1<1$. The configuration is not
rare: among canonical instances with $h\ge3$ and $N<2\cdot10^{5}$, $47\,551$ of
$72\,446$ have $Q_\le=\varnothing$; the smallest case is $N=50$, $p_0=29$,
$h=4$, $t=1$, $m_0=21$, $Q=\{3,7\}$.
\src{CORE, C0b-RD audit repair} --- \emph{reported computational result, not
reproduced in this document}.
\end{scopenote}

\section{The C0b branch targets: TI, TD, TS, TF}\label{sec:branchtargets}

\begin{summarybox}
\texttt{C0b-RD} says one of four classes must carry the obligation. The four
branch targets are the statements ``if the obligation lands in class $X$, then
the dynamics must realise it''. All four are \OPENs. They are the entry point
to the frontier; full frontier entries with obstructions and success criteria
are in Chapter~\ref{ch:frontier}.
\end{summarybox}

\begin{longtable}{p{0.09\textwidth}p{0.24\textwidth}p{0.61\textwidth}}
\toprule
ID & Branch & Obligation to be discharged\\
\midrule
\endhead
\bottomrule
\endfoot
\tid{TI} & $\mathcal I$ (incident, active mirror) &
Turn an active reflected row into realised production: the mirror $a_j$ is an
active parent of $c_j$, so it \emph{could} feed the world; TI asks that it must
feed it \emph{measurably}.\\
\tid{TD} & $\mathcal D$ (incident, inactive mirror) &
The root-anchored dominance obligation. The mirror is not active, so the mass
must be recovered from $\Om(a_j)$; TD asks for a lower bound on realised
production anchored at the root. \textbf{This is the smallest missing bridge}
(\S\ref{sec:frontieropen}).\\
\tid{TS} & $\mathcal S$ ($h$-smooth mirror) &
The coordinate is smooth, so its factors are small and lie in the low range;
TS asks that smooth coordinates cannot all be absorbed.\\
\tid{TF} & $\mathcal F$ (fresh large factor) &
$\ell_j=\PFp(c_j)\ge h$ is active and outside $R$; TF asks that a fresh
external atom forces an escape or a coupling.\\
\tid{TD-DENSITY} & density form of TD & \SUPERSEDEDs: replaced by the
root-anchored form after the density version was found to require a bound of
the same strength as its conclusion.\\
\end{longtable}

\begin{scopenote}[TF is local, and locality is not enough]\label{scope:tf}
\SCOPECORR. ``A local $\mathcal F$ certificate together with $h<G$ forces
routing'' is false: at $N=128$, $\ell=13$ the certificate holds, but $p_0$
wins and $R=\varnothing$. \tid{FAIL-TF-LOCAL-SCOPE-001}
\end{scopenote}


% =====================================================================
\chapter{Current Proof Frontier}\label{ch:frontier}
% =====================================================================

\begin{summarybox}
\textbf{This is the only chapter where new work should start.} Everything
before it is either settled or dead. Each target below carries seven fields:
exact statement, why it matters, what is already proved, the exact remaining
obligation, known obstructions, what would count as success, and the
failure-log entries that constrain it.

\textbf{Before reading further, internalise the shape of the problem.} The
chain is
\[
\underbrace{\texttt{C0a}}_{\PROVEDs}\Rightarrow
\underbrace{\texttt{C0b-RD}}_{\PROVEDs}\Rightarrow
\underbrace{\{\texttt{TI},\texttt{TD},\texttt{TS},\texttt{TF}\}}_{\OPENs}
\Rightarrow
\underbrace{\texttt{P1}^{\mathrm{br}}}_{\OPENs}\Rightarrow
\underbrace{\{\texttt{L1},\texttt{E1},\texttt{W1},\texttt{K1}\}}_{\OPENs}
\Rightarrow
\underbrace{\texttt{X1}}_{\OPENs}.
\]
The chain does \emph{not} end at Goldbach even if every link is proved: it ends
at ``the canonical traversal succeeds'', which is strictly stronger than
Goldbach for each $N$ but is not implied by it. The architecture wall
(\S\ref{sec:crdwall}) says the chain cannot be closed by finite local data
alone, so at least one link must import global input.

\medskip
\textbf{Read \S\ref{sec:v481} first.} That chain is the historical frontier.
The project's \emph{current} frontier is the canonical threshold programme of
v4.79--v4.81 (\S\ref{sec:v481}), whose target is deliberately weaker than X1
--- an asymptotic $N_0^{p_0}$ rather than all $N$ --- and which has already
converted two of its own demanded outputs into proved impossibilities. The two
live targets are named there. The older chain is retained because its
statements are correct and its obstructions are real, and because
\texttt{C0b-RD} still feeds it.
\end{summarybox}

\section{The exact Goldbach boundary}\label{sec:boundary}

\begin{statusbox}{cAudit}
\textbf{What is proved.} For every even $N$ in the non-diagonal case:
the canonical root is well defined and unique; if it fails, the failed world is
closed, all-BAD, has $p_0$ as its unique source, and lies below $N/3$; the
reflected boundary is defect-free and its ledger has exactly four classes; and
the row side satisfies \texttt{C0a} when $h\le2$ and \texttt{C0b-RD} when
$h\ge3$.

\textbf{What would imply Goldbach.} If for every $N$ the canonical traversal
succeeded, then in particular $\Good_N\ne\varnothing$ for every $N$, which is
binary Goldbach. So a proof of universal canonical success is \emph{sufficient}.

\textbf{What does not follow.} Goldbach does \emph{not} imply universal
canonical success; the six $N$ of \S\ref{sec:six} have $\Blow\ne\varnothing$
while satisfying Goldbach comfortably, and $301$ non-canonical upper roots fail
while their $N$ satisfy Goldbach. Every statement conditioned on
$\Good_N=\varnothing$ is class D and is unusable under canonical failure alone.
\tid{FAIL-UPPERHALF-SCOPE-001}

\textbf{The current smallest missing bridge.} The root-anchored \texttt{TD}
obligation feeding \texttt{P1}$^{\mathrm{br}}$. Everything upstream is proved;
everything downstream is blocked on it or on the same defect in another guise.
\end{statusbox}


\section{The canonical threshold programme (post-v4.79/4.80/4.81)}
\label{sec:v481}

\begin{summarybox}
\textbf{This is the project's actual current frontier, and it is newer than the
TI/TD/TS/TF/P1BR/K1/X1 chain of \S\ref{sec:frontier-branch}--\S\ref{sec:X1}.}
The older chain is not wrong; it is simply not where the work is. A model
starting fresh should read this section first.

The target here is deliberately weaker than X1 and therefore more attackable:
\[
\boxed{\ \exists\,N_0^{p_0}<\infty\ \ \forall\text{ even }N\ge N_0^{p_0}:\quad
p_0(N)\text{ succeeds}.\ }
\]
The verdict after v4.81 is: \emph{yes in architecture, not in closure}. Two of
the four demanded outputs of the previous frontier were \emph{proved
impossible}; exactly three routes remain, and the preferred one is named.
\end{summarybox}

\subsection{The v4.79/v4.80 engine}\label{sec:v479engine}

Throughout: $N=2x$, $p_0=x+h$, $m=N-p_0$, $Q=\PF(m)$, $R=R_N(p_0)$, canonical
failure, $N\ge50$.

\begin{proposition}[Nagura window]\label{prop:nagura}
\PROVEDs. For $N\ge50$, Nagura's explicit interval theorem together with
canonical minimality gives
\[
\boxed{\ p_0<\frac{3N}5,\qquad m>\frac{2N}5.\ }
\]
\src{CORE, v4.79 (V79.2); Nagura \cite{Nagura1952}}
\end{proposition}
\emph{Reading.} This is why the two-sheet argument
(Theorem~\ref{thm:collision}) may use $m_0>2N/5$; it is the only place an
external prime-counting input enters the canonical layer, and it is completely
explicit.

\begin{theorem}[Root-row vertical compensation and weighted residual floor]
\label{thm:v79floor}
\PROVEDs. The root row itself contributes $V_0:=m/\rad(m)$ to the canonical
vertical defect $U_R$. Combined with full-$Q$ residual production
(Theorem~\ref{thm:fullqprod}) and the rooted residual--absorption split,
\[
\boxed{\ U_R^2J_RB_{\mathrm{abs}}>m\Bigl(\frac53\Bigr)^{|Q|}>\frac{2N}3.\ }
\tag{V79.4}
\]
\src{CORE, vNEXT4.79}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[First-front coefficient dichotomy]\label{thm:coeffdich}
\PROVEDs. With the exact first-front coefficient defect
\[
F_Q^{\mathrm{coeff}}
=\frac{m}{\rad(m)}\prod_{\substack{q\mid m\\ \kappa_R(q)\ge2}}q ,
\]
one has the sharp dichotomy
\[
\boxed{\ F_Q^{\mathrm{coeff}}=1\iff m\text{ squarefree and }\kappa_R(q)=1
\ (q\mid m),\ }
\]
while
\[
\boxed{\ F_Q^{\mathrm{coeff}}>1\ \Longrightarrow\ T_R>\tfrac52N,\ }
\]
which forces a half-power $U/J$ channel. Nonprimitive first-front failure is
therefore already coefficient-heavy.
\src{CORE, vNEXT4.79--4.80}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Primitive branch]\label{def:primitive}
The canonical failed world is \emph{primitive} when
$F_Q^{\mathrm{coeff}}=1$, i.e.\ $m$ is squarefree and every first-front label
has load one. Otherwise it is \emph{nonprimitive}.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Primitive load-one and selected first-front production]
\label{thm:primloadone}
\PROVEDs. On the primitive branch the load-one condition is exactly
\[
\boxed{\ D_q=\gcd(m,N-q)=1\qquad(q\in Q),\ }
\]
so the selected first-front product is exactly
\[
\boxed{\ U_F(J_FB_{\mathrm{re}})B_{\mathrm{abs}}=\prod_{q\in Q}(N-q).\ }
\]
With the adaptive least non-dividing prime
$\lambda_N=\min\{\ell\in\PP:\ell\ge3,\ \ell\nmid N\}$ one has $q<N/(2\lambda_N)$
for every $q\in Q$, hence
\[
\boxed{\ \prod_{q\in Q}(N-q)>\Bigl(1-\frac1{2\lambda_N}\Bigr)^{|Q|}N^{|Q|}
\ \ge\ \frac{25}{36}N^2.\ }
\]
The primitive selected production therefore has leading logarithmic coefficient
$|Q|\ge2$, not merely one.
\src{CORE, vNEXT4.80}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Owner-preserving quadratic $U\!J\!D$ charge,
\tid{C-P0-PRIMITIVE-OWNERPRESERVING-QUADRATIC-UJD-CHARGE}]
\label{thm:ownercharge}
\PROVEDs. The adaptive high range forms a unique-parent acyclic forest. Each
absorbed high atom is replaced by a selected terminal descendant whose support
lies in $C_{\lambda_N}\setminus Q$; low absorbed support and selected terminal
support are disjoint, so vertical, horizontal and denominator support can each
be single-charged. The resulting owner-preserving selected divisor
$\mathscr C_Q$ satisfies
\[
\boxed{\ \mathscr C_Q\ \Big|\ U_RJ_RD_{\lambda_N}.\ }
\]
\src{CORE, vNEXT4.80}
\end{theorem}

\begin{statusbox}{cSup}
\textbf{Consequences recorded by v4.80.}
\tid{C-P0-PRIMITIVE-BASEABS-ESCAPE-OR-REUSE-CHARGE} is \SUPERSEDEDs: no
external-parent escape/reuse theorem is needed to charge primitive base
absorption.
\tid{C-P0-PRIMITIVE-FIRSTFRONT-UNITMARGIN-PRODUCTION}
($U_F(J_FB_{\mathrm{re}})B_{\mathrm{abs}}>\tfrac{10N}9$, \PROVEDs\ in v4.79) is
\emph{retained} but superseded \emph{as the binding primitive floor}.
\tid{C-P0-PRIMITIVE-SELECTEDFAMILY-CAPACITY} is refined to
\tid{C-P0-PRIMITIVE-SELECTED-UJD-CAPACITY}, which remains \OPENs.
\tid{G-CONDITIONAL-EFFECTIVE-P0-N0} is \PROVEDs\ \emph{only as a conditional
theorem}: no numerical $N_0^{p_0}$, no universal $p_0$-success theorem and no
Goldbach proof is claimed.
\end{statusbox}

\subsection{The v4.81 container theorem and what it kills}\label{sec:v481kill}

The v4.80 preferred frontier
\tid{C-P0-PRIMITIVE-FIRSTFRONT-REFLECTION-DISJOINT-CAPACITY} asked for one of
four outputs: (1) reflected production disjoint from $\mathscr C_Q$ at fixed
positive logarithmic scale; (2) same-label overlap forcing an additional exact
$J/U$ layer; (3) a GOOD event; (4) strict scale descent. v4.81 proves that
\textbf{(1) and (2) cannot exist}, by exact identity rather than heuristic.

\begin{theorem}[Exact rooted container identity]\label{thm:container}
\PROVEDs. On the primitive canonical failed branch,
\[
\boxed{\ U_RJ_RD_{\lambda_N}
=\frac{\prod_{u\in R}(N-u)}{m\prod_{r\in H_\lambda}r}.\ }\tag{V81.1}
\]
So the ``container'' of the v4.80 selected charge is, up to an explicit
denominator, \emph{the row product of the world itself}.
\src{CRD v4.81, Thm.\ container}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Container slack for $\mathscr C_Q$]\label{thm:slack}
\PROVEDs. For every $N\ge500$,
\[
\boxed{\ \frac{U_RJ_RD_{\lambda_N}}{\mathscr C_Q}
=\frac{\prod_{r\in C_\lambda\setminus Q}(N-r)\ \prod_{r\in H_\lambda\setminus Z}(N-r)}
{\prod_{r\in H_\lambda\setminus A_H}r}\ >\ \frac{5N}6 .\ }\tag{V81.2}
\]
The selected charge therefore \emph{never} approaches its container: the gap is
at least one full logarithmic unit, and grows by one further unit for every low
non-front state.
\src{CRD v4.81, Thm.\ slackCQ}
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Death of the size route]\label{cor:sizedeath}
\PROVEDs. Two consequences close the archimedean size route completely.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Trivially}: a divisor never exceeds what it divides. Once
$\mathscr C_Q\mid U_RJ_RD_{\lambda_N}$ is a theorem
(Theorem~\ref{thm:ownercharge}), no lower bound for $\mathscr C_Q$ can
contradict any true upper capacity for the container.
\item \emph{Quantitatively}: any adjoined production $P$ with
$\mathscr C_QP\mid U_RJ_RD_{\lambda_N}$ is priced exactly by (V81.2) --- it
must supply one factor $\ge\tfrac56N$ for every low non-front state before it
can begin to bite.
\end{enumerate}
Hence ``new selected storage disjoint from $\mathscr C_Q$ at fixed positive
logarithmic scale'' --- the frontier's own demanded output (1) --- is
\emph{insufficient by construction}, not merely unproved.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Exact overlap normal form: overlaps are charge-free]
\label{thm:overlapfree}
\PROVEDs. If a prime $\ell$ divides a selected row $N-u$ ($u\in Q\cup Z$) and a
strict reflected carrier $c_j=p_0-2j$, then the entire content of that
coincidence is
\[
\boxed{\ \ell\mid a_j-u,\qquad 0<a_j-u<x,\ }\tag{V81.3}
\]
which is \emph{equivalent} to the already-counted divisibility $\ell\mid N-u$
together with the residue condition $2j\equiv p_0\pmod\ell$. Because
$a_j\notin R$, the coincidence creates no rooted parent, no $\kappa_R$
increment, no $J$-layer and no $U$-layer.
\end{theorem}
\begin{corollary}
Alternative (2) of the v4.80 frontier is \emph{empty}.
\end{corollary}
\emph{Reading.} This is the sharpened, final form of the reflection-gate
warning: not only does the prime-free boundary fail to \emph{activate} a
reflected row (Warning~\ref{warn:gate}, $N=242$), an overlap between the
reflected block and the selected family carries \emph{no charge at all}.

\subsection{New positive structure surviving the attack}\label{sec:v481positive}

All of the following is owner-preserving and reconstructible from the rooted
CRD definitions.

\begin{theorem}[C1: gap-scale shadow normal form]\label{thm:v81shadow}
\PROVEDs. $D_q=\gcd(m,2h-q)$, and primitive load-one is \emph{equivalent} to
\[
\boxed{\ \gcd\bigl(m,\ 2h-u\bigr)=1\qquad(u\in R\setminus\{p_0\}).\ }
\tag{V81.11}
\]
This puts the first front and the reflected block on a single scale
$\delta=2h$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{remark}
This is the Prime-Gap Shadow Identity (Theorem~\ref{thm:shadow}) re-proved from
the v4.80 definitions and used for the first time in the v4.79/v4.80 chain. The
v4.81 salvage audit records it as \emph{the one genuinely missing tool} the
older corpus contributed to the current frontier.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[C2: primitive residual world]\label{thm:v81residual}
\PROVEDs. $R':=R\setminus(\{p_0\}\cup Q)$ is child-closed, nonempty, satisfies
$\Src(R')\subseteq\Gamma_N(Q)$ and $\min R'<\sqrt N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[C3: owner-preserving capacity factorisation]\label{thm:v81factor}
\PROVEDs. With $\Sigma'=\prod_{d\in\Src(R')}d$,
\[
\boxed{\ T_R\,\Sigma'=\Bigl(\prod_{q\in Q}(N-q)\Bigr)T_{R'}.\ }
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[C4: selected residue lock]\label{thm:v81reslock}
\PROVEDs.
\[
\boxed{\ \mathscr C_QB_H\equiv(-1)^{|Q|+|Z|}\,m\prod_{z\in Z}z\pmod N.\ }
\tag{V81.13}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[C5: adaptive fringe cofactor alphabet]\label{thm:v81alphabet}
\PROVEDs. Every edge into $H_\lambda$ has cofactor a \emph{prime} in
$[\lambda,2\lambda)$ coprime to $N$, and that prime is itself a low state. The
alphabet is the full prime range $\mathcal L_N\subseteq[\lambda,2\lambda)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{warning}
This is \emph{not} the rejected two-letter claim $\{\lambda,2\lambda-1\}$,
which is \KILLED\ as \tid{FAIL-FRINGE-ALPHABET-TRANSFER-001}.
Theorem~\ref{thm:v81alphabet} is precisely the ``what survives'' clause of that
failure entry.
\end{warning}

\subsection{The minimal hostile survivor and the surviving routes}
\label{sec:v481routes}

\begin{theorem}[Product-comparison immunity]\label{thm:immunity}
\PROVEDs. A primitive canonical failed world survives every \emph{archimedean
product comparison} between a single-charged selected family and the rooted
$U/J/D$ container. The reason is now exactly quantified: a selected family can
beat its container only if it leaves fewer than $|H_\lambda|$ rows unselected,
whereas $\mathscr C_Q$ leaves at least
$|C_\lambda\setminus Q|+|H_\lambda|-k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Trichotomy of surviving routes]\label{thm:trichotomy}
\PROVEDs. Any proof that the minimal hostile survivor class is empty must
proceed through at least one of
\[
\boxed{\ \textbf{(A) population capacity}\ \vee\
\textbf{(B) residue/congruence obstruction}\ \vee\
\textbf{(C) a GOOD witness}.\ }
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item[\textbf{(A)}] an upper bound for $|C_\lambda|$ (or $|R|$) contradicting a
lower bound for the same quantity. \emph{This is the only archimedean route
left}, because by (V81.1) every product container scales with $|R|$.
\item[\textbf{(B)}] an obstruction inside a container of \emph{bounded} size.
The only such containers in the corpus are the residue class modulo $N$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:v81reslock}, Theorem~\ref{thm:rootlock}) and the gap-scale
divisors $h-j<h$ of \texttt{C0b-RD}(3).
\item[\textbf{(C)}] an actual reachable $g\in R$ with $N-g$ prime.
\end{itemize}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Immediate from Theorem~\ref{thm:immunity} together with the observation that
every capacity object in the corpus ($T_R$, $U_R$, $J_R$, $D_\lambda$, the FC
and LCAP envelopes) is a product over rows or labels of $R$, hence has
logarithm $\Theta(|R|\log N)$, whereas any selected subfamily has logarithm at
most $|\mathcal S|\log N$ with $\mathcal S\subseteq R$.
\end{proof}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{C-P0-PRIMITIVE-LOWCORE-SMOOTHROW-POPULATION-CAPACITY}
--- the current preferred target}
\textbf{Status.} \OPENs.

\textbf{Statement.} Primitive canonical failed world, $N\ge500$, with the
partition $R=\{p_0\}\uplus C_\lambda\uplus H_\lambda$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:v81alphabet} exactly $|H_\lambda|$ rows carry a high factor,
each of the form $L\ell$ with $L\in\mathcal L_N$. Hence
\[
\boxed{\ \text{exactly }|R|-|H_\lambda|\text{ distinct integers }N-u\ (u\in R)
\text{ are }C_\lambda\text{-smooth and lie in }[m,N),\ }
\]
all of them $>(1-\tfrac1{2\lambda})N$ except the root row $m>2N/5$. Wanted: an
effective upper bound
\[
|C_\lambda|\ \le\ \Psi^*(N,\lambda_N)
\]
for the number of integers in the window
$\bigl((1-\tfrac1{2\lambda})N,\ N\bigr)$ all of whose prime factors lie in a
prescribed set of $|C_\lambda|$ primes below $N/(2\lambda)$, contradicting the
matching lower bound $|C_\lambda|\ge|R|-|H_\lambda|-1$ forced by child-closure.

\textbf{Why it matters.} By Theorem~\ref{thm:trichotomy} route (A) is the only
archimedean route left; by Theorem~\ref{thm:v81alphabet} the high band is
completely described, so the whole unknown is the low core; and by (V81.1) a
bound on $|C_\lambda|$ is exactly what converts every existing product capacity
into a finite quantity.

\textbf{Already proved.} The container identity (V81.1), the slack bound
(V81.2), the fringe alphabet, the shadow normal form (V81.11), the residual
world $R'$, and the capacity factorisation.

\textbf{Honest difficulty statement.} This is an analytic question about
$S$-smooth integers in a short interval with prescribed \emph{sparse} support.
$\Psi(x,y)$ technology does not apply directly, because the support set is not
an initial segment of the primes.

\textbf{Known obstruction.} Evertse's $S$-unit bound is \emph{vacuous} here:
the equation $u+w=N$ with $u\in S$, $w$ $S$-smooth, $S=R\setminus\{p_0\}$ has
$|R|-1$ solutions, while the bound is $3\cdot7^{2|S'|+3}$ with
$|S'|\le|S|+\omega(N)$ --- exponential in the very quantity to be bounded.
Recorded as \tid{FAIL-SUNIT-COUNT-BOUNDS-THE-LOWCORE-001}.

\textbf{Success criterion.} The effective bound $\Psi^*$ above, or a proof that
no such bound can exist at this scale.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{C-P0-PRIMITIVE-SELECTED-RESIDUE-LOCK-CAPACITY}
--- the secondary target}
\textbf{Status.} \OPENs.

\textbf{Statement.} Produce a second, \emph{independent} determination of
$\mathscr C_Q\bmod N$ (or of $T_{R'}\bmod N$) from the reflection-complete
boundary, incompatible with (V81.13) above a computable threshold.

\textbf{Input.} (V81.13), \tid{G-ROOT-LOCK} (Theorem~\ref{thm:rootlock}), the
capacity factorisation (Theorem~\ref{thm:v81factor}), and the gap-scale normal
form (V81.11). Reflected carriers entering the exact lock are the natural
source of a second determination.

\textbf{Guard --- read before attempting.} A congruence that is a formal
consequence of the \emph{same} factorisation is vacuous. The check performed in
Theorem~\ref{thm:v81reslock} shows that combining (V81.12), (V81.13) and
\tid{G-ROOT-LOCK} reproduces only $m\equiv-p_0$. Any candidate must import an
\emph{independent} evaluation.

\textbf{Why it is route (B).} It lives inside a container of bounded size (the
residue class modulo $N$), which is the only kind of container
Theorem~\ref{thm:trichotomy} leaves for a non-archimedean argument.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{statusbox}{cKill}
\textbf{The nonprimitive branch.} Separately alive but without a consumer. The
coefficient lock gives $T_R>\tfrac52N$; a large $F_Q^{\mathrm{coeff}}$ yields a
superlinear amplifier, while cheap nonprimitive defect bases localise below a
small power and into a Baker-accessible reduction. \emph{These are reductions,
not a capacity theorem}, and the same container degeneracy
(Corollary~\ref{cor:sizedeath}) forbids the scalar route there too. The exact
Baker requirement recorded in v4.81 is \emph{not} met by the available
effective machinery.
\end{statusbox}

\begin{statusbox}{cOpen}
\textbf{Status line, verbatim from the source.} Binary Goldbach remains
\OPENs; universal canonical $p_0$-success remains \OPENs; $N_0^{p_0}$ is
\textbf{not proved}, neither effectively nor ineffectively; no status of
\tid{G-CONDITIONAL-EFFECTIVE-P0-N0} is changed.
\end{statusbox}

\subsection{Updated proof DAG}\label{sec:v481dag}

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&p_0(N)\text{ fails},\qquad N\ge500\\
&\Downarrow\\
&F_Q^{\mathrm{coeff}}>1\ \vee\ F_Q^{\mathrm{coeff}}=1\\
&\Downarrow\\
&\begin{cases}
\textbf{nonprimitive: } T_R>\tfrac52N,\ \text{split at }N^{3/40}
&\text{(no consumer; the scalar route is forbidden)}\\[1mm]
\textbf{primitive: } m\text{ squarefree},\ \kappa_R(q)=1
\end{cases}\\
&\Downarrow\quad\text{(primitive)}\\
&D_q=1\iff\gcd(m,2h-q)=1
\iff\gcd(m,2h-u)=1\ \ \forall u\in R\setminus\{p_0\}
\quad\text{(V81.11)}\\
&\Downarrow\\
&U_F(J_FB_{\mathrm{re}})B_{\mathrm{abs}}=\prod_{q\in Q}(N-q)
>\Bigl(\tfrac{5N}6\Bigr)^{|Q|}\\
&\Downarrow\\
&\mathscr C_Q\mid U_RJ_RD_{\lambda_N}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{U_RJ_RD_{\lambda_N}}{\mathscr C_Q}>\frac{5N}6
\quad\text{(V81.1, V81.2)}\\
&\Downarrow\\
&\text{archimedean product comparison is immune}\
\Longrightarrow\ \text{routes (A), (B), (C) only}
\end{aligned}}
\]

\section{The C0b branch targets}\label{sec:frontier-branch}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{TI} --- injective branch obligation}
\textbf{Statement.} If the \texttt{C0b-RD} obligation is carried by the class
$\mathcal I$ (incident coordinates with an \emph{active} lower mirror), then the
map $j\mapsto(a_j,\PF(c_j))$ realises production in the world: the active
mirrors inject into distinct parent--child incidences, and the number of such
incidences is bounded below by $|\mathcal I|$ up to an explicit constant.

\textbf{Why it matters.} $\mathcal I$ is the only class whose coordinates are
already \emph{active graph rows}. If the obligation lands there and TI holds,
the boundary obligation converts directly into world structure with no further
input. It is the cheapest of the four branches.

\textbf{Already proved.} The reflection gate (Lemma~\ref{lem:gate}): for
$j\in\mathcal I$ the edge $a_j\to\PF(c_j)$ exists and
$\Gamma_N(\{a_j\})=\PF(c_j)$. Strict non-reuse (Lemma~\ref{lem:nonreuse}):
every prime $\ell\ge h$ occurs in at most one block element, so distinct
$j\in\mathcal I$ with a large factor give distinct incidences.

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} Injectivity for the \emph{small} factors, i.e.\
for primes $\ell<h$, where strict non-reuse gives nothing. Equivalently: bound
$\#\{j\in\mathcal I: \PF(c_j)\subseteq[2,h)\}$ from above by a fraction of
$|\mathcal I|$.

\textbf{Obstructions.} (i) The class $\mathcal I$ can be empty --- $N=242$ has
no active reflected row at all (Warning~\ref{warn:gate}); TI is then vacuous
and the obligation moves to $\mathcal D$, $\mathcal S$, $\mathcal F$. (ii) The
guaranteed active mirror exists only in phase Type~III
(Corollary~\ref{cor:gatephase}), so TI can only be the operative branch on
$\theta>1/2$. (iii) Small-factor collisions are exactly what the widened block
would have controlled, and the widened block is refuted
(Warning~\ref{warn:broadblock}).

\textbf{Success criterion.} An unconditional inequality of the form
$\#\{\text{distinct incidences from }\mathcal I\}\ \ge\ c\,|\mathcal I|$ with
$c>0$ absolute, valid in all phases where $\mathcal I\ne\varnothing$, and
\emph{stated in the same functional} that P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$ consumes.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-REFLECTION-ACTIVATION-001},
\tid{FAIL-BROADBLOCK-ENDPOINT}, \tid{FAIL-TF-LOCAL-SCOPE-001}.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{TD} --- root-anchored dominance obligation}
\textbf{Statement.} If the obligation is carried by $\mathcal D$ (incident
coordinates whose lower mirror is \emph{inactive}), then the recovered mass
$\sum_{j\in\mathcal D}\Om(a_j)\ge2\lceil t/3\rceil$ of \texttt{C0b-RD}
translates into a lower bound on \emph{realised production in the world},
anchored at the root, measured by the same functional that bounds capacity.

\textbf{Why it matters.} This is \textbf{the smallest missing bridge in the
whole project}. \texttt{C0b-RD} is proved and hands over a genuine quantitative
obligation; TD is the first step that turns a boundary count into a dynamical
count. Every downstream target (P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$, L1, W1, K1, X1) either
depends on TD or fails for the same reason TD fails.

\textbf{Already proved.} \texttt{C0b-RD} (Theorem~\ref{thm:c0brd}) including
the $\mathcal D$-branch inequality $\sum_{j\in\mathcal D}\Om(a_j)\ge2k$ under
$\mathcal I=\varnothing$; the closed-world and unique-source structure
(Lemma~\ref{lem:closure}); no-bad-return (Theorem~\ref{thm:norereturn}); the
exact factorization $T_S=U_SJ_S$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:tuj}).

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} Produce a lower bound
\[
\text{(realised production of the world)}\ \ge\ \gamma\bigl(\text{obligation
mass of }\mathcal D\bigr)
\]
in which $\gamma$ is \emph{the same} functional as the one appearing on the
capacity side of P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$ and K1. Not a comparable functional, not a
functional that dominates it on average: the same one.

\textbf{Obstructions.}
(i) $a_j$ inactive means $a_j$ is composite or divides $N$; the mass
$\Om(a_j)$ is therefore not attached to any graph vertex, and there is no
proved route from it to an incidence.
(ii) The density formulation \tid{TD-DENSITY} is \SUPERSEDEDs\ precisely
because it needed a bound of the same strength as its own conclusion.
(iii) The scope-corrected partial-transcript wall (Corollary~\ref{cor:wall})
forbids inferring the bound from selected programmed edges alone; a theorem
controlling the complete frontier is not excluded.
(iv) Every recorded attempt to substitute a different but ``morally
equivalent'' functional is in the log as a scope error.

\textbf{Success criterion.} A proof of the displayed inequality with an
explicit $\gamma$, plus a verification that the $\gamma$ used is literally the
one in \S\ref{sec:P1BR}. A proof with a different functional is \emph{not}
partial progress; it is a new open problem.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-ETA-GAMMA-IDENTIFY-001},
\tid{FAIL-POTENTIAL-CAPACITY-001}, \tid{FAIL-CAB-001},
\tid{FAIL-CAB-INTERNAL-001}, \tid{FAIL-BABS-PRODUCTION-001}.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{TS} --- smooth branch obligation}
\textbf{Statement.} If the obligation is carried by $\mathcal S$ (coordinates
with $\PFp(c_j)<h$ and $\PF(c_j)\cap R=\varnothing$), then the smooth mass
$\sum_{j\in\mathcal S}\Om(c_j)>k\log x/\log h$ cannot be entirely absorbed
inside the world: some smooth coordinate must contribute an escape or a
coupling.

\textbf{Why it matters.} $\mathcal S$ is the branch where the mass bound is
largest (it grows like $\log x/\log h$ per unit), so if the obligation lands
there the quantitative margin is greatest. It is the branch most likely to be
provable by elementary means.

\textbf{Already proved.} The $\mathcal S$-branch inequality of
\texttt{C0b-RD}; minimum-factor escape (Corollary~\ref{cor:minfactor}); shadow
cycle localisation (Theorem~\ref{thm:cycleloc}), which confines a terminal
core inside $Q$ to $(0,2h/3)$ --- exactly the range in which smooth
coordinates live.

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} Convert ``$c_j$ is $h$-smooth and its factors
avoid $R$'' into a statement about the world. The factors of $c_j$ are active
primes outside $R$; they are candidate escape targets, but their rows have not
been shown to reach GOOD.

\textbf{Obstructions.} (i) A factor outside $Q$ or outside $R$ does not mean
success --- only that the current alphabet was left (warning after
Corollary~\ref{cor:minfactor}). (ii) Smoothness bounds \emph{numbers}, not
\emph{vertices}; the passage from $\Om(c_j)$ to distinct active vertices needs
the same injectivity that TI lacks.

\textbf{Success criterion.} An unconditional statement: if
$\mathcal I=\varnothing$ and the $\mathcal S$ inequality is the operative one,
then $G_{\mathrm{esc}}(N)>0$. That alone would be a real theorem, since it
would give Goldbach for every $N$ in that regime.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-HALL-SUPPORT-001},
\tid{FAIL-DIRECT-ADJACENCY-001}.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{TF} --- fresh branch obligation}
\textbf{Statement.} If the obligation is carried by $\mathcal F$ (coordinates
with $\ell_j=\PFp(c_j)\ge h$, active and outside $R$), then the product bound
$\prod_{\ell\in\Lambda_{\mathcal F}}\ell\ge h^k$ forces an escape edge or an
external coupling.

\textbf{Why it matters.} $\mathcal F$ is the only branch that hands over
\emph{named active primes outside the world}. Those are exactly the objects an
escape argument needs.

\textbf{Already proved.} The $\mathcal F$-branch product inequality; that each
$\ell_j$ is active, outside $R$, and occurs in exactly one block element
(Theorem~\ref{thm:c0brd} combined with Lemma~\ref{lem:nonreuse}).

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} Show that an active prime outside $R$ occurring
as a large factor of a reflected coordinate must be, or must lead to, a GOOD
vertex.

\textbf{Obstructions.} (i) \textbf{Locality is not enough}: at $N=128$,
$\ell=13$, the local $\mathcal F$ certificate holds but the canonical root wins
outright and $R=\varnothing$, so the certificate constrains nothing.
\tid{FAIL-TF-LOCAL-SCOPE-001} (ii) An external parent need not be a success
root: $(6142,877,3511)$ has $3511$ active and above $p_0$, yet its own
traversal fails. \tid{FAIL-EXTERNAL-SUCCESS-001} (iii) External reuse is not
local: $(N,\ell)=(1\,825\,372,52\,153)$ at distance $53\,750$.
\tid{FAIL-LOCAL-REUSE-001}

\textbf{Success criterion.} A theorem of the form: under canonical failure with
$\mathcal I=\mathcal D=\mathcal S=\varnothing$, some $\ell\in\Lambda_{\mathcal F}$
has $N-\ell$ prime, or has an active parent outside $R$ whose row meets
$\Good_N$. The second alternative must be included --- it is provably necessary.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-TF-LOCAL-SCOPE-001},
\tid{FAIL-EXTERNAL-SUCCESS-001}, \tid{FAIL-LOCAL-REUSE-001}.
\end{frontierbox}

\section{P1\texorpdfstring{$^{\mathrm{br}}$}{br} --- branchwise production upgrade}
\label{sec:P1BR}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{P1BR}}
\textbf{Statement.} Let $\gamma$ be the capacity functional of the canonical
world. P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$ asserts that the production realised branchwise ---
summed over the branches of the first front, each measured on its own subtree
--- admits a lower bound in $\gamma$ that exceeds the capacity bound in the
same $\gamma$:
\[
\sum_{\text{branches }\beta}\gamma\bigl(\text{production}(\beta)\bigr)\ >\
\gamma\bigl(\mathcal C_N(R)\bigr).
\]

\textbf{Why it matters.} P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$ is the node where the boundary
obligations become a contradiction. Everything downstream (L1, E1, W1, K1, X1)
consumes its conclusion.

\textbf{Already proved.} The branchwise decomposition itself is legitimate:
the world is closed with a unique source, so the first front partitions it into
branches. The exact ledger $T_S=U_SJ_S$ holds on every branch separately. The
capacity side $\mathcal C_N(R)$ is well defined.

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} A \emph{positive external packet} feeding the
\emph{same} P1 capacity --- the corpus target
\texttt{C-POSITIVE-EXTERNAL-PACKET-TO-SAME-P1-CAPACITY}. Concretely: exhibit a
quantity that (a) is provably positive under canonical failure, (b) is
external to the world (so it is not already counted in $\mathcal C_N(R)$), and
(c) is measured in $\gamma$ rather than in a functional that merely
correlates with $\gamma$.

\textbf{Obstructions.}
(i) The status of P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$ was overridden several times in the
corpus (\src{CORE, vNEXT4.25--4.33}) as successive candidate packets were found
to be either non-positive or already internal.
(ii) $\mathcal C_S<\mathcal D_S$ from the first front is \KILLED\ by $N=4736$
($\mathcal C_S\approx22.60>\mathcal D_S\approx20.16$).
\tid{FAIL-POTENTIAL-CAPACITY-001}
(iii) Unconditional CAB is \KILLED\ by $N=322$ and $N=858$.
(iv) The naive support expansion of all sources is \KILLED\ by Hall
compression $456\to17$ at $N=51\,032$. \tid{FAIL-HALL-SUPPORT-001}

\textbf{Success criterion.} A packet satisfying (a), (b), (c) above, with the
positivity proved and the functional identity checked symbol by symbol. Any
proof that silently changes $\gamma$ between the production and capacity sides
is invalid; that substitution is the single most repeated error in the log.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-POTENTIAL-CAPACITY-001},
\tid{FAIL-CAB-001}, \tid{FAIL-CAB-INTERNAL-001},
\tid{FAIL-HALL-SUPPORT-001}, \tid{FAIL-ETA-GAMMA-IDENTIFY-001},
\tid{FAIL-CHILD-C1-001}.
\end{frontierbox}

\section{L1 --- actual layer realisation}\label{sec:L1}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{L1}}
\textbf{Statement.} The layer part $J_R$ of the canonical world is realised by
\emph{actual} distinct layers of the internal filtration, i.e.\ the support
reuse counted by $J_R$ corresponds to genuinely distinct BFS levels rather than
to repeated incidences inside one level.

\textbf{Why it matters.} Every capacity argument that uses $J_R$ implicitly
assumes this. Without L1, $J_R$ is a bookkeeping quantity with no dynamical
meaning, and the Euler-defect route collapses --- as the computation in
\S\ref{sec:euler} shows it does under the naive normalisations.

\textbf{Already proved.} $T_S=U_SJ_S$ exactly (Theorem~\ref{thm:tuj}); the
world is closed with a unique source, so the BFS filtration is well defined and
canonical.

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} A lower bound on the number of layers in terms
of $\log J_R$, or a counterexample. Note that the two false normalisations
(N1) and (N2) of \S\ref{sec:euler} are exactly failed attempts at L1 in
disguise.

\textbf{Obstructions.} The measured data go the wrong way:
$3\,804$ of $21\,093$ canonical worlds violate the (N2) inequality, so support
reuse is systematically \emph{larger} than the layer count can absorb.

\textbf{Success criterion.} Either a proof of $\nu(R)\ge c\log J_R$ for some
$c>0$, or an explicit family showing $\nu(R)=O(1)$ with $J_R$ unbounded (which
would kill L1 and, with it, every capacity route that passes through $J$).
The second is probably easier and is listed as an experiment in
Chapter~\ref{ch:handoff}.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-ETA-GAMMA-IDENTIFY-001} and the
computational refutations of (N1), (N2) recorded in \S\ref{sec:euler}.
\end{frontierbox}

\section{E1 --- escape or coupling}\label{sec:E1}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{E1}}
\textbf{Statement.} Under canonical failure, every internal base atom
$\ell\in B_{\mathrm{abs,int}}$ either has a GOOD edge reachable inside one of
its first-front branches, or has an active parent outside $R$. (This is the
\emph{escape-or-reuse} alternative promoted to a theorem.)

\textbf{Why it matters.} E1 is the only frontier target with overwhelming
computational support and a completely explicit statement: $61\,452$ instances
with $0$ orphans, plus an independent red team over $60\,413$ atoms with $0$
orphans. If any target is true, this one is.

\textbf{Already proved.} Retention--escape (Theorem~\ref{thm:retention});
minimum-factor escape (Corollary~\ref{cor:minfactor}); the prime-power witness
(Proposition~\ref{prop:ppwitness}); $B_{\mathrm{abs,int}}=B_{\mathrm{abs}}$
without vacuity \src{CORE, ARS-BABS-INTERNAL}.

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} The disjunction itself, unconditionally. Both
alternatives are provably necessary: $(6142,877,3511)$ shows the second cannot
be dropped.

\textbf{Obstructions.} (i) External reuse is not local
(\tid{FAIL-LOCAL-REUSE-001}), so the ``active parent outside $R$'' cannot be
found by bounded search. (ii) The external parent need not itself be a success
root (\tid{FAIL-EXTERNAL-SUCCESS-001}). (iii) Escape need not be directly
adjacent (\tid{FAIL-DIRECT-ADJACENCY-001}: at $N=14198$ the atoms $19$ and
$167$ escape at distances $8$ and $7$). (iv) Charging multiplicity is observed
to be $1$ but is \emph{not} proved bounded, and the constant-$C=1$ charging
scheme is \KILLED\ ($53$ violations, maximum $9.42243$,
\tid{FAIL-CHILD-C1-001}).

\textbf{Success criterion.} A proof of the disjunction, or a bounded-charging
lemma (multiplicity $\le C$ for an absolute $C$) which the corpus identifies as
the missing ingredient.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-LOCAL-REUSE-001},
\tid{FAIL-EXTERNAL-SUCCESS-001}, \tid{FAIL-DIRECT-ADJACENCY-001},
\tid{FAIL-CHILD-C1-001}.
\end{frontierbox}

\section{W1 --- simultaneous clean witnesses}\label{sec:W1}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{W1} --- corrected}
\textbf{Statement.} Several clean witnesses can be selected simultaneously at
the \emph{actual} layer scale of the world: a selection of parents, one per
branch, simultaneously clean (no shared support, no double charging), covering
the layers that really occur in $R$ rather than only the polylogarithmic ones.

\textbf{Correction to an earlier reading.} \SCOPECORR. Earlier compressions
listed \tid{G-CLEAN-POLYLOG-PARENT-SELECTION} as W1's open target. It is
\emph{not} open: it is a \PROVEDs\ theorem of the CRD Core
(Theorem~\ref{thm:cleanpoly}), giving exactly such a clean selection for every
finite layer family with $\ell^k\le(\log N)^A$, with global support load at
most $\rho(\mathcal L)$ --- and load one when the base primes are distinct. See
Warning~\ref{warn:w1corr}.

\textbf{Why it matters.} Capacity arguments need many witnesses at once, and
the selection problem is \emph{solved} in the polylogarithmic range. What is
missing is the range, not the selection.

\textbf{Already proved.} Theorem~\ref{thm:cleanpoly} (the selection itself);
strict non-reuse (Lemma~\ref{lem:nonreuse}) for primes $\ell\ge h$; the global
two-sheet collision budget (Theorem~\ref{thm:collision}).

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} Extend the selection from
$\ell^k\le(\log N)^A$ to the actual layers of $R$. That is precisely the
content of L1 (\S\ref{sec:L1}): \textbf{W1 is blocked on L1, not on a
selection lemma.} If L1 is refuted --- and \S\ref{sec:euler} suggests it may be
--- then W1 is not merely open but misconceived, and the correct object is the
polylogarithmic family alone.

\textbf{Obstructions.} Hall-type compression destroys naive selections outside
the proved range: at $N=51\,032$ the naive support expansion of all sources
compresses $456\to17$ (\tid{FAIL-HALL-SUPPORT-001}). This is not a technical
nuisance --- it says the bipartite incidence structure has small vertex covers,
which is exactly what a simultaneous selection must avoid, and it is why
Theorem~\ref{thm:cleanpoly} needs Siegel--Walfisz and a lower-bound sieve
rather than a combinatorial argument.

\textbf{Success criterion.} Either a clean selection at the actual layer scale,
or a proof that the polylogarithmic range is the maximum possible --- which
would close W1 negatively and remove it from the frontier.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-HALL-SUPPORT-001},
\tid{FAIL-CHILD-C1-001}.
\end{frontierbox}

\section{K1 --- source-sensitive capacity}\label{sec:K1}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{K1}}
\textbf{Statement.}
\[
\boxed{\ K_\times(R,\mathcal P)+K(\mathcal P)\ \le\ \mathcal C_N(R)\ }
\]
where $K_\times$ is the cross term between the world $R$ and the selected
parent set $\mathcal P$, $K(\mathcal P)$ the internal term of $\mathcal P$, and
$\mathcal C_N(R)$ the capacity of the world --- all three measured in the
\emph{same} functional as P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$.

\textbf{Why it matters.} K1 is the quantitative closure: with P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$
above and K1 below, the two bounds cross and canonical failure is excluded.

\textbf{Already proved.} The capacity side $\mathcal C_N(R)$ is well defined and
computable; the world's ledger identities (IL1--IL6) hold on
$Q_{\mathrm{smooth}}$.

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} \emph{Exactly the same defect as TD.} K1 needs
the cross term and the capacity to be expressed in one functional. Every
recorded attempt produced two functionals with a comparison that holds
on average and fails pointwise. The corpus's vertical-origin overrides
(\src{CORE, vNEXT4.8--4.13}) end at the target
\texttt{C-NATURAL-SCALE-WEIGHTED-CONSUMER}: a consumer of the packet weighted
by a natural scale, which has never been produced.

\textbf{Obstructions.} (i) The same-functional obstruction, shared with TD and
P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$ --- these three are not independent problems.
(ii) $N=4736$ kills the first-front form of the capacity inequality.
(iii) $N=322$ and $N=858$ kill the unconditional CAB form.

\textbf{Success criterion.} The displayed inequality with all three terms
written in one explicit functional and proved unconditionally under canonical
failure. Equivalently: solve TD and K1 together, since a solution to one in the
correct functional very likely gives the other.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-POTENTIAL-CAPACITY-001},
\tid{FAIL-CAB-001}, \tid{FAIL-CAB-INTERNAL-001},
\tid{FAIL-ETA-GAMMA-IDENTIFY-001}.
\end{frontierbox}

\section{X1 --- canonical failure exclusion}\label{sec:X1}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{X1}}
\textbf{Statement.} For every even $N$ in the non-diagonal case, the canonical
traversal from $p_0$ terminates in \textsc{success}. Equivalently:
$\PF(N-p_0)\not\subseteq\Blow$ whenever $N-p_0$ is composite
(Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedpoint}).

\textbf{Why it matters.} X1 is the terminal node. It implies binary Goldbach.
It is the central hypothesis of the whole project, written here as
\textbf{(H-$p_0$)}.

\textbf{Already proved.} Nothing towards X1 itself. The fixed-point
reformulation (Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedpoint}) is exact but not progress.

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} Everything above, plus the passage from
``the capacity inequality fails'' to ``the traversal succeeds''.

\textbf{Obstructions.} The architecture wall
(\S\ref{sec:crdwall}) --- no finite local certificate can do it; the parity
barrier (\S\ref{sec:parity}) --- no purely sieve-theoretic route reaches a
prime complement; and the fact that X1 is \emph{strictly stronger} than
Goldbach for each $N$, so any proof strategy that would also prove Goldbach
must be at least as hard as Goldbach.

\textbf{Success criterion.} A proof. Nothing weaker counts; in particular no
finite scan, however large, changes the status of X1.

\textbf{Computational status.} \VERIFCOMP: no canonical failure for even
$N\le10^{7}$ (this project, exhaustive). Independent Goldbach verification
reaches $4\cdot10^{18}$ \cite{OHP2014} but says nothing about X1.
\end{frontierbox}

\section{RPD --- repeated prime-power redundancy}\label{sec:RPD}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{RPD}}
\textbf{Statement.} The repeated external prime-power layer redundancy is
bounded:
\[
D_{\mathrm{high}}(H_Q)\ \le\ C\log\log N\cdot
\sum_{\text{layers}}(\kappa-1)_+\ +\ o(M),
\]
equivalently
$D_{\mathrm{high}}(H_Q)\le O(\log\log N)\cdot\eta_{\mathrm{high}}+o(M)$, where
$M$ is the total mass and $\eta_{\mathrm{high}}$ the high-range excess
valuation.

\textbf{Why it matters.} If RPD is true then $\Delta_J\gg M$: the layer defect
dominates the mass, which is exactly the quantitative separation that the
capacity route needs. RPD is the one open target that would supply the
\emph{margin} rather than merely the structure.

\textbf{Already proved.} $T_S=U_SJ_S$; the high/low decomposition of the
valuation mass; the prime-power witness (Proposition~\ref{prop:ppwitness}).

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} The $\log\log N$ bound. The natural approach is
a divisor-type bound on how often a fixed prime power can recur across layers,
which is where $\log\log N$ would come from.

\textbf{Obstructions.} (i) The bound is asserted for the \emph{external}
redundancy; the internal part is already controlled and is not the difficulty.
(ii) The $o(M)$ term hides the interaction between layers, and no proof
technique in the corpus separates layers without losing a factor of the size
that RPD is supposed to save.

\textbf{Success criterion.} A proof of the displayed inequality with an
explicit $C$, or a family of $N$ showing $D_{\mathrm{high}}$ can exceed
$\eta_{\mathrm{high}}\log\log N$ by an unbounded factor.

\textbf{Provenance note.} RPD is recorded in the corpus as a v4.45 open target
inside a commented archive block of the CRD failure log; it is reproduced here
because it is the only surviving open target that carries an explicit
quantitative margin. Its exact original phrasing should be checked against the
source before it is used as a hypothesis.
\end{frontierbox}

\section{Open targets specific to \texorpdfstring{$p_0$}{p0} alone}
\label{sec:frontieropen}

These are stated \emph{without} reference to a Goldbach proof and each is a
self-contained problem.

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{C-SAMEFUNC-BRIDGE} --- global same-functional margin bridge}
\textbf{Statement.} There is a single functional $\gamma$ in which both the
production lower bound (TD, P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$) and the capacity upper bound
(K1) can be stated, with a positive margin between them.

\textbf{Why it matters.} This is the abstract form of the obstruction shared by
TD, P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$ and K1. Solving it solves all three; failing to solve it
blocks all three. Anyone attacking one of them individually should first decide
whether they are really attacking this.

\textbf{Already proved.} Nothing. Several \emph{pairs} of functionals are known
in which one side is provable; no pair is known in which both are.

\textbf{Remaining obligation / obstruction / success criterion.} As for TD; see
\S\ref{sec:frontier-branch}.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-ETA-GAMMA-IDENTIFY-001} and every
entry filed under capacity.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{C-GENEALFREE-DYN} --- boundary to dynamic escape}
\textbf{Statement.} Does the absence of any genealogical boundary defect
($\kappa_{\mathrm{gen}}=0$) force the whole \texttt{C0b-RD} obligation into
\emph{actual} dynamical channels?

\textbf{Why it matters.} This is the single missing implication between
Chapter~\ref{ch:p0prog} (exact boundary structure) and any dynamical statement.
The entire ``why $p_0$ works'' question reduces to it.

\textbf{Already proved.} The boundary side completely
(Theorems~\ref{thm:kappa}--\ref{thm:ledgercomplete}); the obligation side
completely (Theorem~\ref{thm:c0brd}). The implication between them: nothing.

\textbf{Minimum acceptable form.} A theorem whose conclusion \emph{actually
fails}, or acquires an explicit leakage term, when the defect rank is one.
Anything that also holds at rank one is not progress --- it is a class-B result
in disguise.

\textbf{Obstruction.} Warning~\ref{warn:ledger}(2): the statement
$\kappa_{\mathrm{gen}}(r)=0$ may be informationally equivalent to ``$r$ is the
first upper prime''. If so, no theorem can extract more from it than from the
ordering of the primes, and the target should be restated.

\textbf{Constraining log entries.} \tid{FAIL-P0-ZEROHOLE-ESSENTIAL-001},
\tid{FAIL-P0-INFORMATION-SELECTOR-001}.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{frontierbox}{\tid{C-P0P1-SEP} --- one-defect dynamic separation}
\textbf{Statement.} Prove a dynamical difference between $p_0$ and $p_1$ that
is caused by the single embedded channel of the earlier root, not by aggregate
size.

\textbf{Why it matters.} This is the sharpest available test of
\tid{C-GENEALFREE-DYN} and the one with the best data.

\textbf{Already proved.} The categorical separation on the boundary
($\kappa_{\mathrm{gen}}$: $0$ versus $0.9041$ mean, maximum $1$) and the
aggregate near-identity of every other observable (\S\ref{sec:ablation}).

\textbf{Remaining obligation.} Isolate causality. The aggregate observables
differ by $6$--$24\%$, which is consistent with pure size effects; the defect
rank differs categorically but has negligible logarithmic mass.

\textbf{Obstruction.} \tid{FAIL-P0-ZEROHOLE-ESSENTIAL-001}: the mass of the
hole is $O(\log N)$, so any argument that routes the separation through mass
is dead before it starts.

\textbf{Success criterion.} A statement true for $p_0$ and false for $p_1$
whose proof uses the hole \emph{structurally} (as absence of a multiplicative
carrier, \src{CORE, V71.44}) and not quantitatively.
\end{frontierbox}

\section{Smaller open questions about \texorpdfstring{$p_0$}{p0}}
\label{sec:smallopen}

Each of the following is a self-contained problem that does not mention
Goldbach.

\begin{description}
\item[\normalfont Q1. Does $\rho_0$ have dynamical consequences?] \OPENs. The
signature $(\kappa^+,\kappa^-)=(0,\rho_0)$ is the first boundary invariant that
varies nontrivially between canonical worlds. Does $\rho_0\ge1$ (Type~III,
where a guaranteed active reflected row exists) correlate with, or imply,
anything about the traversal? Preliminary data: immediate success occurs in
$18.4\%$ of Type~III cases and is \emph{impossible} in Type~I --- but that is a
consequence of the definition, not of dynamics.
\item[\normalfont Q2. Does the escape margin grow?] \OPENs. Is
$G_{\mathrm{esc}}(N)\to\infty$? Data (\S\ref{sec:margin}): the per-dyadic-block
minimum runs $1,1,1,1,1,1,2,2,3,3,3$ up to $2\cdot10^{5}$. A theorem
``$G_{\mathrm{esc}}(N)\ge f(N)$ for increasing $f$'' would be strictly stronger
than the existence of a Goldbach pair and is, as far as is known, untouched.
\item[\normalfont Q3. Is there a missing state variable?] \OPENs. Four pairs of
structural twins survived enrichment by all global-source information; they are
separated only by the \emph{internal witness signature} (localisation, nearest
escape distance in the same branch, external-reuse flag) \src{F3}. Is there a
scalar invariant, or is the system state intrinsically a profile?
\item[\normalfont Q4. A second canonical anchor?] \OPENs. Let
$p^\star=\max\{p\in\PP:p<N\}$ and $g=N-p^\star$. Then $g\le N-p\le m_0$ for
upper sources, $p^\star-p_0=m_0-g$, and
$\gcd(m_0,g)=\gcd(m_0,p^\star-p_0)=\gcd(g,p^\star-p_0)$ \PROVEDs\ \src{BIB}.
Does $p^\star$ have its own rigidity? Evidence against: $p^\star$ finances on
average only $25.07\%$ of the $B_{\mathrm{abs}}$ atoms against $81.44\%$ for
the whole ensemble of upper sources; priority assessed as low
\src{D4, q.\ 11, 21}.
\item[\normalfont Q5. Is $p_0$ exceptional outside this one graph?] \OPENs. An
analogous selector appears in the Erd\H os--Straus model and in the Schinzel
model \src{BIB}. Does ``the least element above the midpoint, chosen
unconditionally'' have the same reflection-completeness property there? The
definition of the reflected block transfers verbatim, so the question is well
posed.
\item[\normalfont Q6. Diagonal closure.] \OPENs\ (Scope
note~\ref{scope:diag}). What is the right formulation of the genealogical layer
covering $x\in\PP$? Replacing $[x,r)$ by $(x,r)$ makes the theorem
unconditionally true, but then $p_0$ is no longer uniquely characterised. Is
there a simultaneous formulation?
\item[\normalfont Q7. Invariants of the boundary filtration.] \OPENs. The
filtration $\mathfrak B_0\subset\mathfrak B_1\subset\cdots$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:filtration}) with the coupling-matrix embedding
(Corollary~\ref{cor:gcdembed}) is a purely combinatorial structure independent
of Goldbach. Does the sequence $(M^{(k)})_k$ have invariants --- rank,
spectrum, zero pattern --- that do not reduce to the gap sequence
$g_1,g_2,\dots$?
\item[\normalfont Q8. Prove the active-mass Euler bound.] \OPENs. Normalisation
(N3) of \S\ref{sec:euler}, $\sum_qd_R(q)\ge|R|+1$, held in all $21\,093$
canonical worlds tested. It is the only nontrivial surviving form; a proof
would be small but real, and would repair the part of the corpus that used the
false normalisations.
\end{description}

% =====================================================================

\begin{summarybox}
\textbf{Historical binding waypoint through 2026-09-07C.} This chapter
integrates the lossless 2026-09-05--06B archive and the 2026-09-07C checkpoint.

\section{Binding FBTU scope correction}\label{sec:post481-fbtu}
The audit \tid{AUDIT-FBTU-PARTIAL-VERSUS-COMPLETE-20260905} is binding.
Prescribed CRT constraints force selected edges; they do not force the entire
factorisation of an expanded row. At
\[
N=92,\qquad p_0=47,\qquad 92-47=3^2\cdot5,
\]
the selected walk $47\to5\to29\to7$ and the BAD cycle
$5\to29\to7\to5$ are real, while $92-3=89$ is prime, so the complete BFS
succeeds at depth $1$. This kills the blanket implication
``programmable selected BAD transcript $\Rightarrow$ programmable complete
BAD neighbourhood''. The repaired theorem \tid{CRT-TRANSCRIPT-EXACT-SCOPE-
20260905} survives.

\section{Closed-support counting, height and forced envelope escape}\label{sec:post481-support}
The September 5 continuation produced a coherent fixed-/bounded-support layer.
For a fixed prime alphabet $S$ of size $s$, coprime $S$-smooth solutions of a
fixed affine equation are bounded by $2^{9s+16}$ via the verified
Beukers--Schlickewei input. This yields both
\tid{COMPLETE-H1-TWO-ROW-FINITENESS-20260905} and
\tid{CLOSED-ALPHABET-COUNT-20260905}: one fixed finite alphabet cannot support
infinitely many complete closed active BAD worlds.

The Matveev route was then repaired to remove the old branching/pure-row
hypothesis. If $C$ is any nonempty closed active BAD set, $s=|C|$ and
$M=\max C$, then
\[
 \log\frac{N-M}{M}
 < 1.4\,30^{s+3}s^{9/2}\!\prod_{q\in C}\log q\,
   \left(1+\log\frac{\log N}{\log3}\right).
\]
Consequences retained as proved are the explicit bounded-core threshold and
the pointwise lower growth
\[
 M\ge(1-o(1))\frac{(\log\log N)(\log\log\log N)}
                         {\log\log\log\log N}
\]
along any sequence carrying a closed active BAD set. These are necessary
conditions, not contradictions: moving support remains possible.

In the canonical $h=1$ family, bounded first support also forces complete-row
escape from a fixed envelope: beyond the explicit threshold $F_2(y)$ every
first child row has a prime factor $>y$, and the large factors arising from
distinct first children are pairwise disjoint. The inference that this
automatically iterates was explicitly killed by
\tid{ENVELOPE-ESCAPE-AUTOMATIC-ITERATION-20260905}.

\section{Shallow asymptotics and same-$N$ no-gos}\label{sec:post481-asymptotic}
The September 6/06B continuation establishes several asymptotic traversal
constraints, all with novelty still unaudited externally.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \tid{COMPLETE-H1-RADIUS-TWO-RARE-SUCCESS-20260906}: for almost every
prime $P\in[X,2X]$, the canonical $h=1$ start has complete BADness through
radius two; the exceptional relative proportion has an explicit decaying
bound.
\item \tid{SAME-N-GROWING-ROOTS-COMPLETE-RADIUS-TWO-20260906B}: the same
complete radius-two BADness holds simultaneously for a growing prefix of
nearby same-$N$ roots. Thus shallow BADness is not a $p_0$-only signature.
\item \tid{SAME-N-GROWING-DEPTH-DUAL-PRODUCT-BARRIER-20260906B}: for fixed
$c+\kappa<1$, almost every prime start and every same-$N$ root
$k\le(\log X)^\kappa$ has no short successful simple path whose label product
or cofactor product is $\le X^{1-\varepsilon}$, up to depth
$c\log\log X/\log\log\log X$.
\item Exact non-dominance survives hostile checking: at $N=2180$, $p_1$ is
directly GOOD while $p_0$ is BAD through radius two; at $N=2024$, $p_0$
succeeds earlier while $p_1$ is BAD through radius two.
\end{enumerate}
The product barriers quantify over \emph{successful paths}. They are vacuous
inside a completely closed failed core, so the attempted inference from those
barriers to closed-core height was correctly killed by
\tid{SUCCESS-PRODUCT-BARRIER-TO-CLOSED-CORE-HEIGHT-20260906B}.

\section{Exact $h=1$ conjugacy, cycle realisation and canonical embedding}\label{sec:post481-exact}
\paragraph{Prime-lift full-BFS conjugacy.}
Let $N=dx$, let $m=x-1\ge2$, and suppose
$R=(d-1)x+1$ is prime. In the composite-$m$ case the complete BFS from the
inactive prime divisor $d$ and from $R$ have identical ordered transcripts
after replacing the initial root. For $d=2$ this gives the exact all-generation
normal form
\[
 N=2(P-1),\quad P=p_0(N)\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
 \text{BFS from }P\ \equiv\ \text{BFS from }2
\]
for every non-direct $h=1$ case. The tempting general implication
``prime lift $\Rightarrow$ success'' is false: $(N,d,R)=(1862,7,1597)$ gives a
complete failed 22-test conjugate pair.

\paragraph{Canonical first-support cycles.}
For every prescribed ordered list of distinct odd primes there is a fixed gap
$h$ and infinitely many canonical worlds whose complete first support contains
a directed BAD cycle through those primes. Extra factors and GOOD branches are
uncontrolled. Hence canonical first-support acyclicity and any uniform bound on
cycle length are false outside the special $h=1$ situation.

\paragraph{Fixed-gap canonical valuation embedding.}
Take any actual upper BAD root $(N_0,R_0)$ with composite first complement and
gap $h_0$. Its complete induced first-support graph on
$S=\PF(N_0-R_0)$, including root valuations and all internal row valuations,
embeds exactly into infinitely many canonical BAD-root first-support graphs
with the same numerical gap $h_0$. Additional support outside $S$ is forced and
remains uncontrolled. Therefore every hereditary property of this labelled
induced graph that holds for all canonical BAD roots must also hold for every
upper BAD root. This is the rigorous replacement for the old overbroad
finite-local wall: finite hereditary first-support graph/valuation invariants
cannot universally separate $p_0$, while complete support and later
reachability remain outside the theorem.

\section{Low-gap complete-support restrictions}\label{sec:post481-lowgap}
Let $r=N/2+h$ be an upper prime root, $m=N-r$ composite and
$q=\min\PF(m)$ with $0<h<q$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item If no GOOD vertex occurs through depth $2$, then at least three distinct
nonroot primes have been discovered by depth $3$
(\tid{LOW-GAP-COMPLETE-THREE-LABEL-ALTERNATIVE-20260907}).
\item If $q$ participates in a reciprocal BAD two-cycle $q\to b\to q$, then
\[
 b=2h+(2j+1)q\quad(j\ge1),\qquad b\ge3q+2h,
\]
and this numerical bound is sharp for both canonical and noncanonical roots.
\item If the complete row is a prime square, $N-q=b^2$, then $q\nmid N-b$ and
$(b-1)^2<N-b<b^2$. In the $h=1$ singleton-square subcase, necessarily
$u$ is odd, $u\ge3$, and $q\equiv23\pmod{24}$ when $m=q^u$.
\item If $m=q^u$, $N-q=b^v$ is a complete prime-power row and the reciprocal
return occurs, then
\[
 3\le v\le u-1.
\]
Thus $u=2,3$ exclude this immediate monomial return.
\end{enumerate}

The attempted universal FIVE-label strengthening was refuted exactly at
$N=44670$, root rank $12$, where the depth-three nonroot labels are precisely
$\{149,211,23,1933\}$. The proved lower bound THREE survives. The final exact
reduction \tid{LOW-GAP-THREE-LABEL-EXACT-OBSTRUCTION-SPLIT-20260907C} says
that a genuine three-label case must be either (A) a complete closed active
BAD world on exactly three primes, or (B) an explicit prime-power system
\[
 m=q^u,\qquad N-q=b^v,\qquad N-b=q^a c^w,
\]
with the restrictions recorded in the raw theorem. In the singleton square
branch the remaining equations can be written
\[
 2q^u+2h=q+b^2=b+c^w,\qquad w\ge3\ \text{odd};
\]
for $h=1$, also $u$ is odd and $q\equiv23\pmod{24}$.

\section{Negative structural diagnostics}\label{sec:post481-negative}
The multiplicative subgroup generated modulo $N$ by a closed BAD support
necessarily contains $-1$, and contains any upper root whose complete first
support lies in that closed set. As a general explanation of $p_0$ this route
fails: at five of the six historical hosts the maximal closed low BAD support
generates the entire unit group. At $N=2200$ the generated subgroup is proper,
but membership is still not sufficient for failure. This kills simple
multiplicative-character separation as a general $p_0$ mechanism while leaving
more structured valuation/additive residue arguments open.

\section{07C frontier waypoint (superseded by 07H)}\label{sec:post481-frontier}
\begin{frontierbox}{Global exact question: the $h=1$ closed-support obstruction}
Can complete factor search from $2$ fail when
\[
 N=2(P-1),\qquad P\ge5\ \text{prime},\qquad P-2\ \text{composite}?
\]
Equivalently, can there exist a finite set $C$ of odd active primes below
$2(P-1)/3$ such that $\PF(P-2)\subseteq C$ and, for every $q\in C$,
$2(P-1)-q$ is composite with its \emph{entire} prime support contained in
$C$? By the full-BFS conjugacy this is exactly the unresolved non-direct
canonical $h=1$ failure question. Selected cycles, finite internal valuations
and support-height lower bounds do not answer it.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{frontierbox}{Local exact question: three-label obstruction}
Can either branch of
\tid{LOW-GAP-THREE-LABEL-EXACT-OBSTRUCTION-SPLIT-20260907C} actually occur?
The singleton-square branch reduces to the displayed exponential/prime-power
system above. A proof of impossibility would strengthen the current THREE-label
theorem to FOUR in the stated low-gap domain; an exact example would kill that
strengthening cleanly.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{frontierbox}{Asymptotic radius-three question}
The previous 2026-09-06B frontier remains open: control the canonical depth-3
successful-path system in the region where \emph{both} the label product and
the cofactor product exceed $X^{9/10}$. A suitable $o(X/\log X)$ count would
give almost-everywhere complete radius-three BADness in the $h=1$ family, not
a Goldbach proof.
\end{frontierbox}

\section{$p_0$ status at the 07C waypoint}\label{sec:post481-p0status}
The empirical eventual reliability of $p_0$ remains unexplained. Several
simple candidate explanations are now rigorously unavailable: shallow BADness
and product barriers are shared by nearby roots; finite first-support
acyclicity can reverse between $p_0$ and $p_1$; arbitrary first-support BAD
cycles occur in canonical worlds; and hereditary first-support
label/valuation invariants cannot separate all canonical BAD roots from all
upper BAD roots. What may still distinguish $p_0$ must use information outside
that hereditary local class --- complete support, leakage/external cofactors,
absolute root location/size, or truly multigeneration reachability.
