\section{Run D: low-gap complete-support strengthening}
\label{sec:postDH-lowgap}

Run D extends the 07C low-gap branch but does not become the global frontier.

\begin{theorem}[No proper power in $2\cdot3^u-1$]
\label{thm:postDH-3power}
\PROVEDs. For every integer $u\ge1$, the integer $2\cdot3^u-1$ is not a
proper integer power $A^k$ with $A\ge2$ and $k\ge2$.
\end{theorem}
The proof is the elementary factorisation argument recorded in the run-D
source and in the delta registry \S\ref{sec:postDH-registry}.  It excludes
proper powers, not compositeness.

\begin{theorem}[Low-gap singleton upward four-label alternative]
\label{thm:postDH-fourlabel}
\PROVEDs. Let
\[
 r=q^u+2h\ \text{prime},\quad u\ge2,\quad q\ \text{odd prime},\quad
 0<h<q,\quad N=2q^u+2h.
\]
Assume $N-q$ is composite, has at least two distinct prime factors, and
\emph{every} prime factor of $N-q$ exceeds $q$.  Then either a GOOD vertex
is reached by depth $2$ from $r$, or at least four distinct nonroot prime
labels occur by depth $3$ in the complete stopped search.
\end{theorem}

The complete-factor hypothesis is essential.  In the special canonical
family $q=3,h=1$, Theorem~\ref{thm:postDH-3power} supplies it after the
depth-$1$ GOOD case is removed.  Hence for $P=3^u+2$ prime and
$N=2(P-1)$, the canonical search either succeeds by depth $2$ or has at
least four nonroot labels by depth $3$.  The explicit source witness
$u=14$, $P=4782971$, $N=9565940$ shows the BAD-through-depth-$2$ branch is
nonvacuous.

The companion run-D monomial-return theorem proves that a monomial return
\[
 N-q=b^v,\qquad q\mid N-b
\]
in the same low-gap setup satisfies
\[
 d=\operatorname{ord}_q(b)=\operatorname{ord}_q(2h)\ge3,\qquad
 d\mid(v-1),\quad d\mid(q-1),
\]
and consequently
\[
 4\le v\le u-1,\qquad u\ge5.
\]
Later D carryover in the 07G source records stronger $h=1$ filters for
special parity/exponent branches; these are preserved verbatim in the raw
delta and are not promoted here into a global closure theorem.

\section{All-upper-root fixed point and exact rank spectrum}
\label{sec:postDH-spectrum}

For this chapter write
\[
 B_N:=\Blow,
\]
the largest active closed BAD subset below $N/3$ from
Definition~\ref{def:crdfilt}.  The canonical fixed-point theorem extends
without difficulty to every upper root.

\begin{theorem}[All-upper-root fixed point]
\label{thm:postDH-allroot}
\PROVEDs. Let $N$ be even and let $r\ge N/2$ be prime with composite
mirror $m=N-r>1$. Then
\[
 \boxed{\,r\text{ fails}\iff \PF(m)\subseteq B_N\, }.
\]
\end{theorem}

Indeed every child of an odd composite row lies below $N/3$; a failing
reachable set therefore feeds a closed low BAD set, while closure of $B_N$
gives the converse.

If $p_k(N)$ is the zero-based $k$th prime at or above $N/2$ and
$m=N-p_k(N)$, then
\[
 k=\pi(N-m)-\pi((N/2)^-)-1,
\]
and on the composite-mirror domain
\[
 \boxed{\,p_k(N)\text{ fails}\iff \rad(m)\mid R_N\,},\qquad
 R_N:=\prod_{q\in B_N}q .
\]
Thus the failure-rank spectrum is exactly the prime-counting image of the
$B_N$-smooth, prime-backed mirrors.  This is the correct exact replacement
for a hoped-for rank-only congruence law.

\subsection{Same $(k,m)$, opposite verdicts}

The ambient dependence is not cosmetic.  Exact certificates give:
\[
 (k,m)=(7,27):\quad N=116\ \text{success},\quad N=128\ \text{failure},
\]
\[
 (k,m)=(20,799):\quad N=1862\ \text{failure},\quad N=1886\ \text{success},
\]
and
\[
 (k,m)=(48,729):\quad N=2200\ \text{failure},\quad
 N=2180,2210\ \text{success}.
\]
Therefore no verdict function of $(k,m)$ alone exists, even when the complete
integer factorisation of $m$ is supplied.  The indispensable variable is the
ambient $N$-dependent basin.

\subsection{Finite rank spectrum on the six reconstructed hosts}

The independent 07G reconstruction found $301$ failing upper roots on
\[
 128,\ 1718,\ 1862,\ 1928,\ 2200,\ 6142,
\]
with $214$ distinct composite mirrors and $188$ distinct failed ranks.
Within $0\le k\le118$, the ranks avoiding failure on all six host spectra
are exactly
\[
 \boxed{\{0,10,14,26,28,30,62,63,71,74\}}.
\]
This is a finite-host statement.  It is not a theorem that the nine
noncanonical indices are universally composite-safe.

\section{Fixed-rank mirror universality and effective finite fibres}
\label{sec:postDH-fibres}

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-rank mirror surjectivity, audited]
\label{thm:postDH-surj}
\PROVEDs. Fix an odd integer $m\ge3$ and $k\ge0$.  There exists an odd
prime $P>m$ such that, for $N=P+m$,
\[
 P=p_k(N),\qquad N-p_k(N)=m.
\]
For $m=1$ the same holds exactly for $k\ge1$; $k=0$ is impossible.
\end{theorem}

Define
\[
 \kappa_m(P)=\#\{q\in\PP:(P+m)/2\le q<P\}.
\]
Along consecutive primes above $m$, $\kappa_m$ starts at $0$, has upward
jumps of size at most $1$, and tends to infinity by the prime number theorem.
Hence it assumes every nonnegative integer.  For $m=1$ it starts at $1$.

\begin{scopenote}[Audited boundary correction]
If all even $N\ge4$ are admitted, then $N=4,p_0=2$ gives mirror $2$.
Thus
\[
 \{N-p_0(N):p_0(N)<N\}
 =\{2\}\cup\{3,5,7,\ldots\},
\]
whereas for every fixed $k\ge1$ the range is
$\{1,3,5,7,\ldots\}$.  The odd-only formula for $p_0$ is correct after
restricting to odd roots or $N\ge6$.  All composite-mirror conclusions are
unchanged.
\end{scopenote}

Mirror surjectivity immediately rules out every proposed protection that
depends only on the value, support, radical, $\Omega$, largest factor, or
complete first-row factorisation of $N-p_k$ at a fixed rank.

The same theorem has a complementary finiteness statement.

\begin{theorem}[Effective finite rank--mirror fibres]
\label{thm:postDH-finitefibre}
\PROVEDs. Let $m\ge1$ be odd, $P>m$ an odd prime, $N=P+m$, and
$P=p_k(N)$.  Put
\[
 c(m)=\left\lceil\frac{m-1}{4}\right\rceil,\qquad
 n=k+c(m)+2.
\]
Then, writing $R_n$ for the $n$th Ramanujan prime,
\[
 P<R_n<4n\log(4n),\qquad
 N<m+4n\log(4n).
\]
Hence each fixed $(k,m)$ fibre is finite and effectively enumerable.
\end{theorem}

The external numerical bound is Sondow's
$R_n<4n\log(4n)$ \cite{Sondow2009}; the rank/mirror reduction is elementary.
For $m=1$ it follows that every $k\ge1$ has a nonempty but finite set of
unit-row inputs, while $p_0$ has none.

\begin{theorem}[Upper-corner last-realisation principle]
\label{thm:postDH-uppercorner}
\PROVEDs. Fix odd $M\ge3$ and $K\ge0$.  Among all odd
$1\le m\le M$ and ranks $k\le K$, the largest realised $N=P+m$ is attained
at the upper corner $m=M,k=K$.
\end{theorem}

For $M=3053,K=74$ the exact endpoint is
\[
 \boxed{P=4271,\qquad N=7324}.
\]
Consequently increasing an arbitrary $N$ cutoff cannot add new cases for
these already bounded mirrors and ranks.

\subsection{Globally exhausted bounded-mirror experiments}

The finite-fibre theorem upgrades two previously cutoff-labelled scans into
complete all-$N$ statements for their fixed domains.

First, the $214$ dangerous mirrors extracted from the six reconstructed
failure hosts, transplanted into
\[
 k\in\{10,14,26,28,30,62,63,71,74\},
\]
have exactly $4035$ realisations over \emph{all} $N$; none fails, while
$147$ full worlds have exactly one GOOD escape edge.  The control ranks
$7,8,9,11,20,48$ recover genuine failures, so the harness is not vacuous.

Second, enumerating \emph{every} odd composite mirror $m\le3053$ at
\[
 k\in\{0,10,14,26,28,30,62,63,71,74\}
\]
gives exactly $22130$ realised composite cases over all $N$, with zero
failures.  This is a rigorous exhaustive statement for a bounded mirror
box, not evidence that larger mirrors are harmless.

\begin{warning}[Do not promote the survivor ranks]
The set above was discovered inside the same finite failure landscape.
Neither the $4035$ transplant exhaustion nor the $22130$ bounded-mirror
census proves universal composite-success of any noncanonical rank.
A new failure may require a new mirror integer and a new moving basin.
\end{warning}

\section{Run H: same-$N$ finite views versus complete support}
\label{sec:postDH-samen}

Run H attacks a stronger possibility: perhaps $p_0$ can be recognised by
finite local data \emph{at the same ambient $N$}.  The answer is negative for
any fixed finite valuation projection.

\begin{theorem}[Same-$N$ prefix valuation realisation]
\label{thm:postDH-samen}
\PROVEDs. Fix $K\ge0$, a finite set $T$ of odd primes, and arbitrary
prescribed nonnegative integers $e_\ell$ for $\ell\in T$.  There are
infinitely many even $N$ such that, for the zero-based primes $p_j$ at or
above $N/2$,
\[
 p_0=N/2+1,\qquad
 v_\ell(N-p_j)=e_\ell
 \quad(\ell\in T,\ 0\le j\le K).
\]
All $K+1$ complements may additionally be required composite.  Along an
infinite subfamily there are fixed offsets
\[
 0=d_0<d_1<\cdots<d_K,\qquad p_j=p_0+d_j.
\]
\end{theorem}

The construction chooses one reduced congruence class by CRT and invokes
Freiberg's theorem on bounded-diameter strings of consecutive primes in a
prescribed reduced residue class \cite{Freiberg2013}.  It controls the
requested valuations but deliberately leaves the remaining cofactors
unbounded.

\begin{corollary}[Fixed-label projection no-go]
\label{cor:postDH-fixedprojection}
For any fixed finite label set $T$ and fixed $K$, infinitely many same-$N$
worlds have identical root-to-$T$ multiplicities and identical retained
rows/GOOD--BAD flags on $T$ after relabelling the root.  Therefore a fixed
prime-label projection cannot identify $p_0$ among a fixed early prefix.
\end{corollary}

This is \emph{not} a theorem about a complete bounded-depth ball: new prime
labels can already appear on the first full BFS layer and tend to infinity.

The complementary theorem controls complete factorizations in a genuinely
fixed alphabet.

\begin{theorem}[Early-rank fixed-support separation]
\label{thm:postDH-supportsep}
\PROVEDs. Let $S$ be a fixed nonempty finite set of odd primes,
$s=|S|$, and put
\[
 A(S)=1.4\,30^{s+3}s^{9/2}\prod_{q\in S}\log q,\qquad
 c(S)=\frac{(\log3/e)^{A(S)}}{6}.
\]
For all sufficiently large even $N$, if
\[
 N/2\le p_i<p_j\le2N/3
\]
and both $N-p_i$ and $N-p_j$ are completely $S$-smooth, then
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 j-i>c(S)\frac{N^{19/40}}{(\log N)^{A(S)}} .
 \quad}
\]
Consequently, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<19/40$, sufficiently large
$N$ have at most one $S$-smooth complement among
\[
 N-p_0,\ldots,N-p_{\lfloor N^{19/40-\varepsilon}\rfloor}.
\]
\end{theorem}

The proof combines the already audited rational Matveev estimate with the
Baker--Harman--Pintz exponent $0.525$ \cite{BHP2001}; the exponent
$19/40=1-0.525$ is exactly the resulting rank scale.  No BAD closure is
assumed.

\begin{corollary}[Finite-view matching with cofactor escape]
\label{cor:postDH-viewescape}
Fix a finite valuation prescription and $K\ge1$.  The same-$N$ theorem
matches that finite view across $p_0,\ldots,p_K$ infinitely often.  Yet for
any additional fixed finite prime alphabet $S$, after finitely many
exceptions at least $K$ of those $K+1$ complete complements contain a prime
outside $S$.
\end{corollary}

The quantifier is crucial:
\[
 \boxed{\text{fixed }S\quad\neq\quad S=B_N\text{ chosen separately for each }N.}
\]
No theorem in this chapter permits the latter substitution.

A useful elementary overlap consumer also survives: if upper roots
$r<s$ share a prime factor $q$ in their complements, then
\[
 2q\mid(s-r),\qquad h_s\ge h_r+2q.
\]
Thus sufficiently low-gap later roots have initial support disjoint from
every earlier upper root.  Certified failed examples show that such
disjointness still does not force success.

\section{Binding current frontier after 07H}
\label{sec:postDH-frontier}

\begin{frontierbox}{Primary target: selector versus moving basin}
Find a necessary condition on a complete closed BAD basin $B_N$ that
interacts with the \emph{actual position} of the first upper prime (or,
more generally, with the rank-realisation curve).  For a fixed rank $k$ the
exact failure question is whether there exist a composite $m$ and prime
$P=N-m=p_k(N)$ such that
\[
 \rad(m)\mid R_N,\qquad R_N=\prod_{q\in B_N}q.
\]
For $k=20$ such an intersection exists at $(N,m)=(1862,799)$.
For $k=10,14,26,28,30,62,63,71,74$ none is known.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{frontierbox}{Uniformise the fixed-$S$ geometry or prove why it cannot be}
The fixed-support Matveev/BHP theorem is pointwise strong but cannot accept
$S=B_N$ when $B_N$ changes with $N$.  A useful advance must control the
size, height, growth, or internal spacing of the \emph{moving} alphabet
well enough that the fixed-$S$ constants do not become vacuous, or replace
them by an inequality uniform in an admissible family of basins.
\end{frontierbox}

\begin{frontierbox}{Adversarial alternative: construct a genuinely new failure host}
The bounded mirror fibres through $m\le3053$ are exhausted.  More scanning
of the same mirrors cannot add information.  A computational attack should
instead search for a new complete closed BAD basin / EAC host and then inspect
its entire upper-root rank spectrum.  A new host would immediately stress the
current survivor ranks with genuinely new ambient data.
\end{frontierbox}

The 07D low-gap Diophantine branch remains a legitimate secondary target, but
the H results show that repeated fitting of fixed residues, fixed valuations,
or fixed alphabets cannot by itself explain $p_0$.

\section{$p_0$ status after 07H}\label{sec:postDH-p0status}

The project now has a sharper separation between what is genuinely canonical
and what is shared by nearby ranks.

\begin{itemize}
\item $p_0$ remains the least upper prime, the reflection-complete boundary
root, and the unique fixed rank with no unit-row input.
\item It is \emph{not} characterised by the possible odd values or complete
factorisations of its first mirror: every fixed rank realises every odd
$m\ge3$ somewhere.
\item It is \emph{not} characterised by any prescribed finite list of small
prime valuations, even when comparison is made at the same $N$: such data can
be synchronised across any fixed prefix.
\item Fixed finite full-support alphabets are themselves too rigid to describe
many early roots simultaneously for large $N$.
\item What remains potentially special is therefore global: how the
least-upper-prime choice sits relative to the full, moving basin $B_N$ and how
its complete cofactors enter or escape that basin over multiple generations.
\end{itemize}

\begin{statusbox}{cOpen}
\textbf{\OPENs\ --- no promoted conclusion.}
No result through 07H proves Goldbach, universal canonical success, a global
classification of EAC hosts, or universal composite-success of any
noncanonical rank.  The absence of a novelty claim is deliberate: several
new statements are applications of classical PNT, Ramanujan-prime,
Matveev, prime-gap, and consecutive-prime inputs and have not been externally
checked for priority.
\end{statusbox}

\section{Other observables}\label{sec:comp-obs}

\begin{statusbox}{cEmp}
\textbf{Depth.} \EMPPAT. The success depth of the canonical traversal is $\le2$
for $3\,910\,310$ of $4\,999\,999$ cases ($78.21\%$) and $\le4$ for
$4\,953\,205$ cases ($99.06\%$).
The tail is extremely thin: a single case reaches $d=10$. No mechanism is known
that would force a bounded depth, and the depth is \emph{not} the right measure
of difficulty --- see \S\ref{sec:margin}.
\end{statusbox}

\begin{statusbox}{cEmp}
\textbf{$p_0$ is not measurably better at escaping.} \EMPPAT. Beyond the
aggregate table of \S\ref{sec:ablation}: within the $301$ failing upper roots
of EXP3, the canonical root wins at all six $N$, but the set of failing roots
is neither an initial nor a final segment of $p_1,p_2,\dots$
(Example~\ref{ex:128}: $p_1$ wins, $p_2$ fails). Ordering by height does not
order the outcome.
\end{statusbox}

\begin{statusbox}{cEmp}
\textbf{Two censuses agree.} \EMPPAT. The six $N$ with $\Blow\ne\varnothing$
(EXP7, $N\le6\cdot10^{4}$) coincide with the six $N$ carrying failing upper
roots (EXP3, $N\le2\cdot10^{4}$) and with the six numbers with an exceptional
autonomous component reported to $10^{8}$ by Bo\.zek \cite{Bozek2019}. The
three lists measure different things; their coincidence is data, not a theorem,
and it has not been checked beyond $6\cdot10^{4}$ in this project.
\end{statusbox}


% =====================================================================
\chapter{Failed and Killed Approaches}\label{ch:killed}
% =====================================================================

\begin{summarybox}
This chapter is the curated narrative; Chapter~\ref{ch:faillog} is the complete
raw record. Read this one first: it groups $239$ individual entries into the
dozen mistakes that actually recur. A model that internalises this chapter will
not need the raw log except to check a specific ID.

\textbf{The five recurring shapes of error.}
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Domain mixing} --- quoting a result outside the class (A/B/C/D)
on which it was proved. Most common single failure.
\item \textbf{Functional substitution} --- proving a bound in one functional
and consuming it in another. Kills TD, P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$, K1.
\item \textbf{Vacuity mistaken for canonicity} --- a construction that ``only
works for $p_0$'' because for $p_k$ it is undefined on $k$ coordinates.
\item \textbf{Finite certificate} --- deriving a contradiction from a bounded
canonical transcript. Provably impossible (\S\ref{sec:crdwall}).
\item \textbf{Promotion} --- turning a scan with zero counterexamples into a
theorem, or an exact identity into a mechanism.
\end{enumerate}
\end{summarybox}

\item Incidence ledger IL1--IL6 on the domain $S=Q_{\mathrm{smooth}}$: two
independent reconstruction routes, $1\,000$ worlds, $0$ errors \src{ILA} ---
\AUDID.
\item The escape-or-reuse alternative: $61\,452$ instances, $0$ orphans;
independent red team $60\,413$ atoms, $0$ orphans \src{ORPH, RT} ---
\VERIFCOMP, as a theorem \OPENs.
\item The whole genealogical layer (\S\ref{sec:genealogy}) and the filtration
(\S\ref{sec:filtration}) --- \PROVEDs.
\item The phase diagram and the bidirectional rank (\S\ref{sec:phase},
\S\ref{sec:rho}) --- \PROVEDs.
\item Global two-sheet collision budget, no-bad-return-to-$p_0$, the $\Blow$
characterisation --- \PROVEDs.
\item All $34$ hostile certificates of the corpus were reproduced here and
pass (\S\ref{sec:comp-cert}).
\end{itemize}

\section{Post-CRD successor theories}\label{sec:successors}

\src{PCRD} documents a sequence of theories built after CRD1, each intended to
preserve information lost by its predecessor. All reached a wall. The table
summarises them; their proofs are \emph{not} reproduced here.

\begin{longtable}{p{0.11\textwidth}p{0.25\textwidth}p{0.26\textwidth}p{0.30\textwidth}}
\toprule
Theory & Fundamental object & What it was to recover & What stopped it\\
\midrule
\endhead
\bottomrule
\endfoot
CRD1 & support/valuation dynamics from $p_0$ & reachability, shadow, capacity &
the ``same container'' argument, generic smooth counting, residue saturation,
exact self-consistency of the fixed point\\
CMFT & lossless mirror-factorization tensor $(\delta,q,a,b)$ &
parent--valuation--cofactor correlation &
the least-factor tree \emph{is} the Buchstab/sieve decomposition; the cofactor
star at fixed $q$ is an affine bijection\\
CGST & canonical cell $N_h$ and the convolution $a_P*a_P$ &
exact additive pairing $+$ phase &
the factorization layer collapses diagonally in $(h,t)$; exception propagation
reduces to prime-pair geometry\\
CSD & exceptional spectral configurations $+$ the gap &
a pointwise inverse anomaly &
finite conductor patterns are consistent with an arbitrarily long \emph{fixed}
canonical gap\\
CAPT & Li--Liu almost-prime witnesses & a massive real family of sources &
at fixed $(r,s)$ the system reduces to two linear prime forms; $(3,3)$ is the
natural degeneration\\
RSD & rough reservoir $+$ Liouville sign $+$ $P_3$ correction &
explicit exposure of parity &
either level of distribution $>2/3$, or a pointwise binary prime--Liouville
correlation\\
rough-$P_2$ matrix & $A_N(q,r)=\mathbf 1_\PP(N-qr)$ &
global higher-order correlation &
boundary blindness, local spectrum $=$ singular series, co-degrees $=$
prime-tuple problem, $K_{3,3}$ grids exist arithmetically\\
H1-FP & root-factor descent at $h=1$ with shift-$2$ orthogonality &
elementary closure of the $2$-core &
reduces to a Pillai/Bennett equation $a^\alpha-a=b^\beta-b$\\
\end{longtable}

\begin{example}[A $K_{3,3}$ grid at $N=10^{6}$]\label{ex:k33}
\VERIFCOMP. For $q\in\{61,67,73\}$ and $r\in\{113,179,599\}$ all nine numbers
$N-qr$ are prime, and all six factor vertices are BAD. A full rank-two
bipartite rough-$P_2$ grid is therefore arithmetically real and is \emph{not} a
contradiction. \src{PCRD, hostile exact survivor}
\end{example}

\begin{statusbox}{cScope}
\textbf{Updated verdict on the $p_0$ programme.} The \emph{old local
$p_0$-exceptionality proof architecture} is \SUPERSEDEDs, but the stronger
historical claim that finite complete-BFS neighbourhoods are universally
programmable was scope-corrected in September 2026. Consequently universal
$p_0$ reachability and the $h=1$ complete-support problem remain live open
questions. What is ruled out rigorously is narrower: selected partial
transcripts by themselves, and hereditary first-support graph/valuation
separators, cannot explain universal $p_0$ reliability.

\textbf{What remains alive:} $p_0$ as a selector, the exact full-BFS/root-$2$
conjugacy at $h=1$, complete-support/moving-support analysis, non-hereditary
selector invariants, and the full reachability problem.
\end{statusbox}


\section{Surviving lemmas of the killed programmes}\label{sec:survivors}

\begin{navbox}
\textbf{A killed theory is not a theory whose theorems are false.} Each
successor programme of \S\ref{sec:successors} died at an \emph{architecture}
wall, and each left behind correct, reusable lemmas. Compression is exactly
where those get thrown out with the dead programme, so they are collected here
with their statuses intact. \emph{Every item below is \PROVEDs\ in \src{PCRD}
unless marked otherwise; the proofs are not reproduced here.} Using one of them
is legitimate; restarting its parent programme is not.
\end{navbox}

\subsection{From CMFT (Canonical Mirror Factorization Theory)}
\label{sec:surv-cmft}

CMFT's objects: for $N=2x$,
$\mathcal U_N=\{p\in\PP:x\le p<N\}$,
$\mathcal M_N=\{m\le x:N-m\in\PP\}$, so that Goldbach is exactly
$\mathcal M_N\cap\PP\ne\varnothing$; the canonical root has mirror anchor
$m_0=N-p_0=\max\mathcal M_N$; and the CMFT atom is
$\mathfrak e=(\delta,q,a,b)$ with $m_0-\delta=q^ab$ and
$p_0+\delta+q^ab=N$.

\begin{theorem}[Lossless anchor filtration, \tid{PCRD-CMFT-1}]
\label{thm:anchorfiltration}
\PROVEDs. For upper primes $p_0<p_1<\cdots$ with $m_j=N-p_j$, the full left
history of the anchor $p_j$ grows by adjoining the \emph{entire} hyperedge row
$m_j$:
\[
\boxed{\ \mathscr H_{j+1}=\mathscr H_j\sqcup\mathscr A_j,\qquad
L_{j+1}(\ell,k)-L_j(\ell,k)=\mathbf1_{\ell^k\mid m_j}.\ }
\]
The ablation $p_0\to p_1$ loses exactly the full factorization of $m_0$.
\end{theorem}
\emph{Why it is worth keeping.} This is the precise
\emph{information-theoretic} form of the ablation result of
\S\ref{sec:ablation}: it says what is lost, not merely that something is.

\begin{theorem}[Tail hard-edge universality, \tid{PCRD-CMFT-2}]
\label{thm:tailuniversality}
\PROVEDs\ / no-go. For any later anchor $p_j$, after truncating the earlier
prefix its complement $m_j$ becomes the maximal element of the tail mirror
field and satisfies \emph{identical} local gcd, offset and bilinear identities.
Hence
\[
\boxed{\ \text{the local geometry of the tail does not distinguish }p_0.\ }
\]
The genuinely unique information carried by $p_0$ is only the \emph{zero lost
prefix}.
\end{theorem}
\emph{Reading.} This is the sharpest available formulation of what
\S\ref{sec:p0what} establishes empirically, and it is a theorem. Combined with
Warning~\ref{warn:ledger}(2) it is the strongest reason to doubt that any
purely local property of $p_0$ can do dynamical work.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical least-factor split, \tid{PCRD-CMFT-3}]
\label{thm:leastfactorsplit}
\PROVEDs. For a composite mirror row $m$ choose uniquely $q=\PFm(m)$,
$b=m/q$. If $q>x^{1/3}$ then $b$ must be prime, hence
\[
\boxed{\ m\text{ composite}\ \Longrightarrow\
\PFm(m)\le x^{1/3}\ \ \vee\ \ m=qr\text{ a balanced semiprime}.\ }
\]
\end{theorem}
\emph{Why it is worth keeping.} It repairs the divisor-multiplicity bias of any
raw bilinear form over rows: without it, divisor-rich rows are counted
$\tau(m)$ times.

\begin{theorem}[All-root collision identity, \tid{PCRD-CMFT-4}]
\label{thm:allrootcollision}
\PROVEDs. For a composite row family $S$,
\[
\boxed{\ \sum_\ell\sum_{k\ge1}\binom{\nu_{\ell,k}(S)}2\log\ell
=\sum_{i<j}\log\gcd(m_i,m_j).\ }
\]
A pigeonhole over least factors yields a positive collision floor.
\end{theorem}
\emph{Limitation, recorded by the source.} The floor has \emph{no consumer}:
nothing in the corpus converts it into a contradiction. Compare
Theorem~\ref{thm:actualpp}, which is the residual-row analogue and does have
one.

\begin{theorem}[Prime-pressure failure ceiling, \tid{PCRD-CMFT-5}]
\label{thm:primepressure}
\PROVEDs. With $\mathcal P_N=\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_N}\Lambda(m)$, a hypothetical
Goldbach failure eliminates every $k=1$ contribution, so
\[
\mathcal P_N\le E(x):=\sum_{r^k\le x,\ k\ge2}\log r\le\sqrt x\log x,
\qquad\text{whence}\qquad
\boxed{\ \mathcal P_N>\sqrt x\log x\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{Goldbach}.\ }
\]
\end{theorem}
\emph{Reading.} A clean quantitative reformulation of Goldbach for a single
$N$, entirely elementary. It did not supply the matching lower bound, which is
why CMFT died --- but the reformulation itself is correct and reusable, and it
is a class-D-free statement (it does not assume $\Good_N=\varnothing$; it
concludes Goldbach).

\begin{statusbox}{cKill}
\textbf{The CMFT wall.} Raw bilinear mass counted divisor-rich rows repeatedly.
After the least-factor repair the machinery turned out to be \emph{exactly} the
Buchstab/sieve decomposition, and the fixed-$q$ cofactor star
$p\leftrightarrow b=(N-p)/q$ is an affine bijection, not an independent Type-II
correlation. Giant stars have the natural scale of primes in arithmetic
progressions and can be far larger than the ``forced'' $x^{2/3}$ with no
anomaly at all.
\end{statusbox}

\subsection{From CGST (Canonical Gap-Spectral Theory)}\label{sec:surv-cgst}

CGST's reformulation: with $A_P=\{u\in\Z:P+2u\in\PP\}$ and $N_h=2(P-h)$,
\[
\boxed{\ N_h\text{ is Goldbach}\iff -h\in A_P+A_P.\ }
\]

\begin{theorem}[Canonical straddle theorem, \tid{PCRD-CGST-1}]
\label{thm:straddle}
\PROVEDs. If no direct pair through $P$ exists, every Goldbach representation
has the form
\[
P+2t+\bigl(P-2(h+t)\bigr)=2(P-h),\qquad t\ge1,
\]
and the lower prime must lie \emph{below} the previous prime $P_-$.
\end{theorem}
\emph{Reading.} This is the additive counterpart of the phase trichotomy
(Theorem~\ref{thm:phase}) and explains why Type~I forces the search strictly
past $p_-$.

\begin{theorem}[Arbitrarily deep finite reflection obstruction,
\tid{PCRD-CGST-2}]\label{thm:deepreflection}
\PROVEDs. For any fixed $T$, CRT and Dirichlet construct infinitely many
canonical $h=1$ worlds in which $P-2,P-4,\dots,P-2(T+1)$ are all composite.
Hence \emph{no bounded-depth reflection search can be a universal closer}.
\end{theorem}
\emph{Reading.} The reflection-specific instance of the architecture wall
(\S\ref{sec:crdwall}). If a proposed argument inspects the reflected block to
any fixed depth, this theorem kills it immediately.

\begin{theorem}[Diagonal collapse, \tid{PCRD-CGST-3}]\label{thm:diagcollapse}
\PROVEDs. In cell coordinates the reflection row is $C_P(h,t)=P-2(h+t)$, so the
entire valuation/factor tensor on the $(h,t)$ plane depends only on $h+t$. The
extra ``cell dimension'' is a \emph{false degree of freedom} for the
factorization layer.
\end{theorem}
\begin{warning}
Any construction that treats $(h,t)$ as two independent parameters at the
factorization layer is already dead. The exception-amplification wall follows:
two cells $h$ and $h+s$ share exact rows only when the upper-prime offsets form
a prime pair of difference $2s$, and same-row factor certificates satisfy
$\gcd\bigl(C_P(h,t),C_P(h+s,t)\bigr)=\gcd\bigl(C_P(h,t),s\bigr)$, which is $1$
for $s=1$. Factorization-driven propagation of one Goldbach exception to
neighbouring $N$ is therefore far too weak.
\end{warning}

\subsection{From CSD (Canonical Spectral Defect)}\label{sec:surv-csd}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical conductor--gap compatibility, \tid{PCRD-CSD-1}]
\label{thm:conductorgap}
\PROVEDs. For any fixed modulus pattern $M$ and any fixed length $L$, CRT and
Dirichlet construct infinitely many canonical $h=1$ worlds with $M\mid N$ and a
prime-free interval of length at least $L$ immediately before $p_0$. Hence
\emph{any finite conductor pattern is compatible with an arbitrarily long fixed
canonical gap.}
\end{theorem}
\emph{Reading.} The bridge ``exceptional characters $\Rightarrow$ canonical gap
contradiction'' does not exist, and this theorem says why in one line. Keep it:
it is the cheapest available refutation of an entire family of circle-method
hybrids.

\subsection{From CAPT (Canonical Almost-Prime Transfer)}\label{sec:surv-capt}

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-$(r,s)$ compression, \tid{PCRD-CAPT-1}]
\label{thm:fixedrs}
\PROVEDs. After freezing $(r,s)$ in the Li--Liu representation
$N=p+rq$ with $N-q=sb$, one has $q=N-sb$ and
\[
\boxed{\ p=rsb-(r-1)N,\ }
\]
so the system becomes \emph{two linear prime forms in the single variable $b$}.
\end{theorem}
\begin{remark}[The $(3,3)$ degeneration]
For $(r,s)=(3,3)$: $q=N-3b$, $p=9b-2N$ --- an ordinary two-linear-prime
pattern that occurs abundantly in real canonical worlds. Second-layer
compression is therefore not a contradiction. Large-factor consequences of
Li--Liu that remain correct: under Goldbach failure $r\ne1$, and from $rq<N$
with $r\le q^{9/10}$ one gets $r<N^{9/19}$ and $q>N^{10/19-o(1)}$ for almost
all of the relevant mass.
\end{remark}

\subsection{From RSD (Rough Signed Decomposition)}\label{sec:surv-rsd}

\begin{theorem}[Exact rough signed identity, \tid{PCRD-RSD-1}]
\label{thm:roughsigned}
\PROVEDs. On the rough support ($\rho_z(n)=\mathbf1_{(n,P(z))=1}$, $z>X^{1/4}$,
so $\Om(n)\le3$),
\[
\boxed{\ \mathbf1_\PP(n)\rho_z(n)
=\rho_z(n)\Bigl[\frac{1-\lambda(n)}2-\mathbf1_{\Om(n)=3}\Bigr],\ }
\]
and for shifted-prime weights
\[
\boxed{\ G_z(N)=\tfrac12R_z(N)-\tfrac12L_z(N)-T_{3,z}(N),\ }
\]
so that under Goldbach failure
$\boxed{L_z(N)=R_z(N)-2T_{3,z}(N)}$.
\end{theorem}
\emph{Reading.} This is the cleanest \emph{exact} statement in the corpus of
where the parity obstruction sits for this problem. It is worth keeping
precisely because it is an identity, not an estimate.

\begin{theorem}[Distribution--roughness phase law, \tid{PCRD-RSD-2}]
\label{thm:phaselaw}
\PROVEDs. If the usable distribution level is $D=X^\theta$ and one sieves to
$z=X^\beta$, the lower linear sieve needs $\beta<\theta/2$, while forcing
$\Om(n)\le k$ by roughness needs $\beta>1/(k+1)$. The two are compatible
\emph{iff}
\[
\boxed{\ \theta>\frac2{k+1}.\ }
\]
For $k=2$ the natural threshold is $\theta>2/3$.
\end{theorem}
\emph{Reading.} A quantitative triage rule: any proposal in this family can be
checked against it in one line. Pascadi's $5/8-o(1)$ \cite{Pascadi2025} for
special factorable weights is below $2/3$, so branch A is closed at current
technology.

\begin{remark}[The parity endpoint, exactly]\label{rem:parityendpoint}
At $z=X^{5/16-\varepsilon}$ the surviving $P_3$ sits in a narrow balanced box
that switching/modern Chen sieves control well, but after reduction to
$P_1/P_2$ the exact identity
\[
P_1(N)=\frac{D_{1,2}(N)-\Delta_2(N)}2,\qquad \Delta_2=P_2-P_1
\]
remains, and Goldbach failure means full saturation $\Delta_2=D_{1,2}$. Any
theorem giving ``even a little desaturation'' is \emph{already equivalent} to
finding a prime complement on that family. This is the precise sense in which
the parity barrier is the endpoint (\S\ref{sec:parity}).
\end{remark}

\subsection{From the global rough-$P_2$ matrix route}\label{sec:surv-roughp2}

With $A_N(q,r)=\mathbf1_\PP(N-qr)$:

\begin{theorem}[$K_{3,3}$ explosion, \tid{PCRD-M-1}]\label{thm:k33explosion}
\CONJ\ (conditional \PROVEDs). At rough-$P_2$ mass of order $X/\log^2X$,
K\H ov\'ari--S\'os--Tur\'an forces a $K_{3,3}$ at the natural scales
$|Q|\sim X^{1/2}$, $|R|\sim X^{11/16}$. \emph{$K_{4,4}$ is not forced} by that
density scale.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Boundary blindness, \tid{PCRD-M-2}]\label{thm:boundaryblind}
\PROVEDs. Extending the bulk matrix by the boundary row/column $r=1$ encodes
the Goldbach entries. Zeroing the whole boundary axis is a perturbation of rank
at most $2$, whose operator norm is asymptotically small against the bulk
scale. A generic operator norm or energy can therefore \emph{almost fail to
notice} the loss of every Goldbach entry.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[$h=1$ matrix invisibility, \tid{PCRD-M-3}]\label{thm:h1invisible}
\PROVEDs. For $N=2(P-1)$ we have $m_0=P-2=X-1$, so every odd product
$qr\le X$ automatically satisfies $qr\le X-1=m_0$. The canonical hard edge
removes \emph{no} rough-$P_2$ matrix cell: $p_0$ disappears from the domain
geometry entirely.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-modulus spectrum, \tid{PCRD-M-4}]\label{thm:fixedmodspec}
\PROVEDs. The local admissibility matrix modulo a prime $\ell\nmid N$ has the
form $J-P_N$; its singular values are explicit and recover \emph{only} local
density / singular-series data. The fixed-modulus spectrum does not see
Goldbach failure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[The codegree wall]
The pointwise codegree
$C_N(q_1,q_2)=\sum_rA_N(q_1,r)A_N(q_2,r)$ counts simultaneous primality of the
three linear forms $r$, $N-q_1r$, $N-q_2r$, i.e.\ it enters the prime-tuple
problem; average codegrees are boundary-blind by
Theorem~\ref{thm:boundaryblind}. Only a specially constructed
bulk-to-boundary inverse theorem would remain, and no candidate is known that
does not reduce to an earlier binary-correlation wall.
\end{remark}

\subsection{From the $p_0$ kill programme and the H1-FP revival}
\label{sec:surv-h1}

\begin{theorem}[Gap scalar freedom, \tid{PCRD-P0-3}]\label{thm:gapscalar}
\PROVEDs\ (from known facts). For a fixed prime $P$ with gap $G=P-P_-$, all
$N_h=2(P-h)$, $0\le h<G$, have canonical root $P$. With unbounded prime gaps
the ratio $h/G$ can approximate all of $[0,1]$; with bounded-gap results there
are infinitely many small $G$. Hence \emph{the scalars $h$, $G$, $h/G$ have no
universal closing regime}.
\end{theorem}
\begin{warning}
This is the exact statement that kills every attempt to close the problem by a
size condition on $\theta=h/G$ (\S\ref{sec:phase}). The phase diagram is a
correct classification; it is not a filter.
\end{warning}

\begin{theorem}[H1 root-factor descent, \tid{PCRD-H1-1}]\label{thm:h1descent}
\PROVEDs. If $q,r\mid m_0=P-2$ then
\[
\boxed{\ r\mid N-q\iff r\mid q-2.\ }
\]
The root-factor subsystem is therefore a strictly decreasing DAG, and the least
root factor $q_*$ satisfies
\[
\boxed{\ \PF(N-q_*)\cap\PF(m_0)=\varnothing,\ }
\]
so failure must \emph{immediately} produce external factors.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[H1 shift-2 orthogonality, \tid{PCRD-H1-2}]\label{thm:h1shift2}
\PROVEDs. For $N=2(P-1)$ with $P$ prime and $u<N/3$ prime,
\[
\boxed{\ \gcd(N-u,\ u+2)=1.\ }
\]
Every terminal fixed core must therefore satisfy full shift-$2$ coprimality on
all of its hyperedges.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[The $3$-core normal form]\label{rem:3core}
The two smallest rows of a terminal core have disjoint factor supports. For
$K=\{a<b<c\}$ this leads to one of two coupled forms, e.g.
\[
N-b=a^\alpha,\qquad N-a=b^\beta c^\gamma,\qquad N-c=a^ub^v.
\]
A hostile reverse search over large finite boxes found no $3$-core; the status
is \VERIFCOMP, \emph{not} a theorem.
\end{remark}

\begin{statusbox}{cKill}
\textbf{Why the H1-FP revival was not enough.} Closing
$N=2(P-1)\Rightarrow\Blow=\varnothing$ requires classifying complete
self-consistent shifted $S$-unit systems \emph{and} the primality of the linear
form $N/2+1$. Already the minimal case $|K|=2$ touches an unresolved
Pillai/Bennett-type uniformity ($a^\alpha-a=b^\beta-b$;
Remark~\ref{rem:2200}). $p_0$ supplies no mechanism of its own for that
problem.
\end{statusbox}

\subsection{Live CRD results retained through every pivot}
\label{sec:surv-crdlive}

\src{PCRD} records the following as explicitly retained when CRD1 was frozen.
They are the intersection of everything that survived; all appear elsewhere in
this file and are listed together here so a future model can see the retained
core at a glance.

\begin{itemize}
\item the fixed-point characterisation $\Blow$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedpoint});
\item the C0b decomposition and its correct gap-scale congruence consequences
(Theorem~\ref{thm:c0brd});
\item T2 first-front residue closure;
\item T3 mod-$3$ exclusion/rigidity (Theorems~\ref{thm:residuenogo},
\ref{thm:mod3return});
\item the source-free core $K$ with its shifted $S$-unit equations
(Remark~\ref{rem:2200}, Remark~\ref{rem:3core});
\item the exact container/product identities (\S\ref{sec:coreidentities});
\item the correct prime-power collision geometry (\S\ref{sec:ppledger});
\item the empirical six-EAC corpus (\S\ref{sec:six}).
\end{itemize}

\begin{statusbox}{cKill}
\textbf{What killed CRD1 --- the convergence, not a single false lemma.}
\begin{enumerate}
\item Selected-divisor capacity routes were \emph{same-container} arguments:
one cannot beat a container with one of its own divisors. (This is exactly what
Corollary~\ref{cor:sizedeath} later made quantitative.)
\item Generic smooth-population bounds lost self-consistency: the factor
alphabet is simultaneously the set of state labels.
\item The pure local-residue route saturates for $q\ge5$; modulus $3$ is an
exception, not a mechanism (Theorem~\ref{thm:residuenogo}).
\item Reflection is not a universal closer: $h=1$ gives an \emph{empty} strict
reflected block.
\item Nonprimitive large product/reuse is compatible with a failed world and
gives no capacity contradiction.
\item A source-free core is not itself contradictory: $N=2200$,
$K=\{3,13\}$ is an exact witness.
\item After removing the intermediate ledgers the frontier returned to the
exact self-consistency $\PF(m_0)\subseteq\Blow$ with no independent
intermediate parameter.
\end{enumerate}
\end{statusbox}

\section{The parity barrier and why it is the real wall}\label{sec:parity}

\begin{summarybox}
Two distinct obstructions are present and must not be conflated.
\begin{description}
\item[\normalfont The partial-transcript wall (\S\ref{sec:crdwall})] is internal
and scope-corrected: compatible selected finite divisibility/valuation
patterns can be realised canonically, so those selected patterns alone cannot
supply a contradiction. It does \emph{not} rule out a theorem about a complete
bounded-depth frontier.
\item[\normalfont The parity barrier] is external and classical: sieve methods
cannot distinguish numbers with an even number of prime factors from those
with an odd number, so no purely sieve-theoretic argument produces a
\emph{prime} complement.
\end{description}
Thus selected-edge programming cannot replace complete-support control, while
pure sieve input cannot by itself force primality. The current moving-support
frontier may require a combination of exact complete-row arithmetic and
analytic input; the old slogan ``not locally'' was too broad.
\end{summarybox}

\begin{description}
\item[RSD and parity.] RSD attempted to expose parity explicitly through a
rough reservoir with a Liouville sign and a $P_3$ correction. It requires
either level of distribution $>2/3$ --- beyond Pascadi's $5/8$
\cite{Pascadi2025} --- or a pointwise binary correlation between primes and the
Liouville function, which is at least as hard as the problems calibrated by
Mangerel \cite{Mangerel2024}. \KILLED.
\item[The weaker $P_2$ desaturation target.] Also \KILLED: at $\Om\le2$ a
sign-$(-1)$ witness \emph{is} a prime complement, so the ``weaker'' target is
the original problem.
\item[Chen-type input.] R.~Li's bound $D_{1,2}(N)\ge1.9728\,C(N)N/\log^2N$
\cite{RunboLi2026} and Li--Liu's $(1+1.9)$ \cite{LiLiu2026} supply almost-prime
representations in quantity, but not the last bit distinguishing $P_1$ from
$P_2$. That last bit is the parity barrier.
\item[Friedlander--Iwaniec.] The asymptotic sieve for primes \cite{FriedlanderIwaniec1998} is the
template for what the missing input looks like: a bilinear form estimate. No
bilinear input of the required shape has been produced in this project, and the
rough-$P_2$ matrix was the attempt to manufacture one.
\end{description}

\begin{warning}[Do not try to route around parity by enlarging the graph]
Several killed routes are variations on ``add more structure to the graph until
the parity obstruction disappears''. The obstruction is not a property of the
graph; it is a property of the sieve information being used. Adding vertices,
weights or higher-order correlations to a construction whose only input is
sieve-type data cannot remove it.
\end{warning}

\textbf{How to use it.}
\begin{itemize}

are also listed in the index.
\item The index in \S\ref{sec:failindex} gives ID, status and page.
\item Every entry is labelled \texttt{fail:FAIL-ID}, so
\verb|\ref{fail:FAIL-XXX-001}| resolves.
\item Cross-references that pointed into the original document and cannot be
resolved here appear as \textup{[\,target\,]} rather than being silently
dropped.
\item Legacy status macros of the source were mapped onto the status vocabulary
of \S\ref{sec:nav-status}; the mapping is stated below.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Legacy status mapping.} \texttt{R}, \texttt{RI}, \texttt{RM}
$\to$ \KILLED; \texttt{SC} $\to$ \SCOPECORR; \texttt{SU}, \texttt{RET}
$\to$ \SUPERSEDEDs; \texttt{SR}, \texttt{C} $\to$ \VERIFCOMP;
\texttt{P} $\to$ \PROVEDs; \texttt{PA} $\to$ \REPAIR;
\texttt{H} $\to$ \EMPPAT; \texttt{O} $\to$ \OPENs. The mapping is
status-preserving in the sense that no entry was moved to a stronger status.
\end{navbox}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-ABOVE-BV-MASS-INVISIBLE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-ABOVE-BV-MASS-INVISIBLE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-ABOVE-BV-MASS-INVISIBLE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.19.
\item[Old description:] Mirror mass above one scalar BV boundary is
unavailable to clean selection.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Replacement:] Track both designated-base scale \(Q\) and roughness scale
\(z\).  With polylogarithmic \(z\), the clean designated-base range reaches
\(Q_*=N^{1/2}/\operatorname{polylog}N\).  Significant mass beyond \(Q_*\)
forces a polynomial actual-state packet rather than disappearing.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-ABSORBED-FRINGE-RESIDUAL-HAS-ARBITRARY-COFACTOR-001}\label{fail:FAIL-ABSORBED-FRINGE-RESIDUAL-HAS-ARBITRARY-COFACTOR-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-ABSORBED-FRINGE-RESIDUAL-HAS-ARBITRARY-COFACTOR-001.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Rejected statement:] A first-front residual prime
$\ell\in(N/6,N/3)$ may occur with an arbitrary cofactor in $N-q$.
\item[Certificate:] since $q<N/6$, $(N-q)/\ell$ is an odd integer strictly
between $1$ and $6$, hence
$N-q=3\ell$ or $N-q=5\ell$.  The root-supported gcd then divides $3$ or $5$.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Exact repair:] The support-capacity inequality contains
\(\omega_h(x)\log c_{\max}/t\), so one also needs
\[
 \omega_h(x)\le\omega(x)=O\!\left(\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}\right).
\]
With that explicit dependency, the quantified population conclusion survives.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not suppress the \(\omega(x)\) dependency when invoking
this population lemma.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-BABS-PRODUCTION-001}\label{fail:FAIL-BABS-PRODUCTION-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-BABS-PRODUCTION-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Canonical bridge audit \S4, 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] Every failed world produces a nontrivial absorbed base
product \(B_{\rm abs}>1\), which is therefore the universal carrier of
failure mass.
\item[Original motivation:] \(B_{\rm abs}\) is the natural object of ambient
promotion and was observed nontrivial in most instances.
\item[Status:] \SUPERSEDEDs.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] \((N,r)=(128,79)\).
\item[Exact certificate:] Full-\(Q\) production is nontrivial for this root
while the recorded \(B_{\rm abs}\) equals \(1\).  Production and absorption
are different channels, and only the former is always nonvacuous on the
composite-complement domain.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] One channel of a four-channel ledger
was promoted to the whole ledger.
\item[Why the argument failed:] \(B_{\rm abs}\) collects exactly the
residual primes with \(\kappa_R(\ell)=m_\ell\); nothing forces that set to
be nonempty.
\item[What survives:] \texttt{ARS-BABS-INTERNAL}, that
\(\mathcal B_{\rm abs,int}=\mathcal B_{\rm abs}\) under failure --- which
explicitly yields \emph{no} nonvacuity conclusion --- and \(B_{\rm abs}\) as
one channel and the proper object of ambient promotion.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Carry failure mass on
\(\mathfrak F_Q=\prod_{q\in Q_r}M_q\), not on \(B_{\rm abs}\).
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
\texttt{G-FULLQ-PRODUCTION}, which gives
\(\mathfrak F_{Q_r}>(5/3)^{|Q_r|}\operatorname{rad}(m_r)>1\)
unconditionally on the composite-complement domain.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not make one ledger channel universal.
\item[Related current target:] \(P1^{\rm br}\), K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-BOUNDED-ARITY-WEIGHT-001}\label{fail:FAIL-BOUNDED-ARITY-WEIGHT-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-BOUNDED-ARITY-WEIGHT-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Bombieri--Vinogradov four-ary continuation,
1 September 2026.
\item[Claim:] Once every selected parent has at most four unintended
children, the large-state packet \(E\) is automatically a lower-order cost,
or the clean parent family closes P1BR by cardinality alone.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural; one unintended prime
factor is already enough.
\item[Exact certificate:] A squarefree selected row may have
\[
 N-p=\ell r,
 \qquad r> N^{1/4-\varepsilon},
\]
with \(r\in R\).  The four-ary conclusion permits this configuration, and
the only universal weight estimate it supplies is
\[
 \log r=\log(N-p)-\log\ell.
\]
Thus even \(\omega(E_\ell)=1\) permits the unintended label to carry the
entire non-base cofactor mass.  More generally
\[
 \log E\le L(\mathscr P)-\log\!\prod\ell,
\]
with equality when every unintended child lies in \(R\).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] An unweighted degree bound was used
as a weighted logarithmic capacity bound.
\item[Why the argument failed:] The number of factors and the sum of their
logarithms are different functionals.  Roughness makes each surviving
factor larger, not cheaper.
\item[What survives:] The four-ary theorem turns \(E\) into a bounded-degree
dynamic packet.  The exact clean source-surplus identity then cancels the
base copy of every internal unintended factor and exposes its true cost as
\((\kappa_R(r)-1)\log r\).
\item[Safe weaker version:] Use bounded arity only for dynamic branching and
population statements.  For P1BR prove an external-mass-versus-rooted-reuse
inequality with logarithmic weights.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core v1.6,
\texttt{G-CLEAN-MULTIPARENT-SURPLUS-IDENTITY} and
\texttt{G-BV-FOUR-ARY-DISPOSITION}.
\item[Do not repeat:] \(\omega(E)=O(|A_0|)\) does not imply
\(\log E=o(L(\mathscr P))\).
\item[Related current target:] P1BR, K1, large-layer disposition.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-BUNDLE-ENLARGES-CAPACITY-001}\label{fail:FAIL-BUNDLE-ENLARGES-CAPACITY-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-BUNDLE-ENLARGES-CAPACITY-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.1, Phase 7.
\item[Claim:] That preserving a canonical bundle \(D\) in the lifted row forces
a canonical contribution --- to the denominator of (RC4\('\)), or to a
state-difference packing budget --- and so extracts more from \(R\) than an
arbitrary external row does.
\item[Original motivation:] The lifted row shares exact prime powers with a
canonical reflected row, and empirically bundle rows are much more often
nonpositive than single-base rows on the same reflected row
(\(87\%\) against \(72\%\) in \texttt{COMP-VNEXT41-DISPOSITION}).  Nonpositive
rounds are the ones with a recorded consumer, so this looked exploitable.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Exact certificate:] Theory Core \texttt{G-EXTERNAL-INTERFACE-CAPACITY}.
For any globally coprime family \(\mathscr P\) of external rows and any failed
world \(R\), the integers \(\gcd(N-p,N-u)\), \(p\in\mathscr P\), are pairwise
coprime divisors of \(N-u\), so
\(\sum_{p}\sum_{u}\log\gcd(N-p,N-u)\le\sum_u\log(N-u)<|R|\log N\).  The bound
has \emph{no} hypothesis on how \(\mathscr P\) was chosen.  Consequently at
most \(2|R|<6.6\gamma\log N\) members with \(N-p>\sqrt N\) can be nonpositive,
whatever the provenance; the empirical bias towards nonpositivity is therefore
not exploitable beyond that ceiling.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Confusing a richer \emph{description} of
a row with a larger \emph{charge} on \(R\).  The charge is a gcd against the
fixed integers \(N-u\), and those integers have finitely many divisors.
\item[What survives:] The bundle lift, the exact valuations and the mirror
relation, all \PROVEDs; and the ceiling (IC3), which is new and which also
strengthens the vNEXT4 statement (MD1) by dropping the designated-base
hypothesis.
\item[Do not repeat:] Before claiming a selection strategy extracts more from
\(R\), check it against (IC1), which is provenance-blind.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{P1BR-ADDITIVE-COUPLING}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-C-SYMBOL-COLLISION-001}\label{fail:FAIL-C-SYMBOL-COLLISION-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-C-SYMBOL-COLLISION-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT2 independent audit.
\item[Claim:] The symbol \(c\) may be read uniformly across the Theory Core.
\item[Original motivation:] Both quantities are small integers attached to a
packet and were introduced in different rounds.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Internal.  In (LE1)--(LE6),
\(c=|D_S^{\rm src}|\) is the \emph{source count}; in (FC7)--(FC10),
\(c=|C|\) is the \emph{low-core cardinality}.  For a canonical \(R\) the first
is \(1\) and the second is typically large, so any statement that combines an
LE identity with an FC bound while reading \(c\) uniformly is wrong by a factor
that grows with the world.
\item[Exact certificate:] (LE4) reads \(\eta(S)+\nu(S)\ge|S|+c\) with \(c=1\)
for a canonical rooted world, whereas (FC8) reads
\(J_R<N^{c+\tau}(25/18)^\tau/\prod_{q\in C\setminus Q}q\) with \(c=|C|\).
Substituting one into the other is a category error.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Symbol reuse across rounds without a
concordance entry.
\item[What survives:] Both families of statements, unchanged, on their own
readings.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Use \(\gamma=|C|\) for the low core and reserve
\(c\) for the source count, as fixed by Convention~\textup{[\,conv:c-collision\,]} in
the Theory Core.  (FC7)--(FC10) are not restated; their \(c\) is \(\gamma\).
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, Convention~\textup{[\,conv:c-collision\,]}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not introduce a symbol already bound in an earlier
round without a concordance line.
\item[Related current target:] (FC8), K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-CAB-001}\label{fail:FAIL-CAB-001}

\(U_R=J_R=1\) but \(B_{\rm abs}=11\cdot29>1\).  The other first-front
state \(53\) is GOOD because \(322-53=269\in\PP\).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] A successful-world local ledger
was treated as a failure-world capacity law.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Absorption can occur on the bad branch
while another first-front branch already succeeds, leaving zero proposed
denominator.
\item[What survives:] This witness does not refute a theorem explicitly
conditioned on a closed canonical failure.

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-CASCADE-DIRECTION-001}\label{fail:FAIL-CASCADE-DIRECTION-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-CASCADE-DIRECTION-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT3.1 correction round.
\item[Claim:] \texttt{G-CASCADE-GAMMA-TERMINUS}: the (FC10) cascade closes
precisely on \(\gamma\le(\log N)^A\), proved by bounding
\(\sum_iM_i\log z_i\ll(\log N)^A\log N\).
\item[Original motivation:] The selector supplies at most one clean row per
designated base and the bases are polylogarithmically bounded, so the total
production looked easy to estimate.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ as stated and as proved.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] The proof itself.  (DP5) states that
\emph{simultaneous nonpositivity implies} \(\sum_iM_i\log z_i<\log J_R\);
to conclude that some round is positive one must therefore exhibit a
\textbf{lower} bound \(\sum_iM_i\log z_i\ge\log J_R\).  The vNEXT3 proof
supplied an \textbf{upper} bound \(\sum_iM_i\log z_i\ll(\log N)^A\log N\) and
used it in that place.  An upper bound on a quantity can never certify that the
quantity is large; the argument establishes nothing, in either direction.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] The two roles of
\(\sum_iM_i\log z_i\) --- what (DP5) concludes about it, and what must be
supplied to invoke (DP5) contrapositively --- were interchanged.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Counting the \emph{number} of available bases
bounds production from above.  Forcing a positive round needs the
\emph{logarithmic mass} of the bases actually used, bounded from below.
\item[What survives:] The intended conclusion, correctly proved, with the
quantifiers made explicit and the domain moved to the global-failure DAG: see
\texttt{G-SELECTABLE-CLEAN-LOG-MASS} and
\texttt{G-GAMMA-POLYLOG-FORCES-POSITIVE-ROUND} in the Theory Core.  The
correct relation between the exponents is \(A>B+1\), with \(B\) fixed first.
\item[Safe weaker version:] None; the statement must be reproved from a lower
bound, which is what the replacement does.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
Theorem~\textup{[\,thm:clean-log-mass\,]} and
Theorem~\textup{[\,thm:gamma-forces-positive\,]}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Before invoking a contrapositive, check which side of the
inequality must be supplied and which side is concluded.
\item[Related current target:] \(\gamma\),
\texttt{P1BR-POSITIVE-ROUND-CONSEQUENCE}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-CLEAN-ROOTED-CAP-P1-001}\label{fail:FAIL-CLEAN-ROOTED-CAP-P1-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-CLEAN-ROOTED-CAP-P1-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Clean-support-load continuation, 1 September 2026.
\item[Claim:] Once one selects pairwise-coprime upper-half external parents,
the rooted capacity \(\mathcal C_N(R)=L(R)\) supplied by the clean
base-layer theorem can be beaten by the cofactor production of those same
parents, closing P1BR.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural; no finite witness is
needed.
\item[Exact certificate:] In a canonical failed world, every non-root state
\(r\in R\setminus\{p_0\}\) lies below \(N/3\), hence
\(N-r>2N/3\).  Every selected upper-half parent satisfies \(p>p_0\), hence
\(N-p<m=N-p_0<N/2\).  With at most one selected parent per distinct internal
base label, \(|\mathscr P|\le|R|-1\), so
\[
 L(\mathscr P)<(|R|-1)\log m
 <\log m+(|R|-1)\log(2N/3)<L(R).
\]
Thus the exact rooted upper bound \(K_\times+K(\mathscr P)\le L(R)\) is too
large for this naive production choice to exceed.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Solving the collision-selection problem
was mistaken for solving the production-versus-capacity comparison.
\item[Why the argument failed:] The clean theorem makes external complements
small and noncolliding, but the failed-world rows are individually larger:
non-root rows exceed \(2N/3\), whereas selected upper-half-parent complements
are below \(m<N/2\).  The order geometry points in the wrong direction for
\(L(\mathscr P)>L(R)\).
\item[What survives:] \texttt{G-CLEAN-POLYLOG-PARENT-SELECTION} and
\texttt{G-CLEAN-BASE-ROOTED-CAPACITY} remain exact \PROVEDs\ statements.  They
close the W1/K1 collision side on the fixed-polylog base-layer subdomain.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Use the clean selection to isolate the remaining
cost: the base-copy surcharge from unintended labels of \(R\).  A future
P1BR route must control that smaller support set, or use a different common
production/capacity functional; it may not simply take \(L(R)\).
\item[Do not repeat:] ``Pairwise coprime parents'' is a capacity statement,
not a production surplus.
\item[Related current target:] P1BR, W1, K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-COFACTOR-SIBLING-PRIME-UNSCOPED-001}\label{fail:FAIL-COFACTOR-SIBLING-PRIME-UNSCOPED-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]

\item[Date / iteration:] v1.22 cofactor-window continuation, 1 September 2026.
\item[Claim:] For every internal returned fresh seed, the cofactor
$r_j=(N-w_j)/\ell_j$ is prime.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Why the inference fails:] v1.21 proves only that all prime factors of
$r_j$ lie in $U$ and are at least $s=\min U$.  Primality follows in v1.22 only
when $r_j<s^2$, supplied by the bounded window
$r_j<2\Lambda h<h^2\le s^2$ under no descent.
\item[What survives:] On $b_j\le\Lambda h$ with $s\ge h>2\Lambda$, the return
cofactor is prime and yields the sibling packet of
\texttt{TF-COFACTOR-WINDOW-SIBLING-RENEWAL}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not replace cofactor roughness by primality outside
the explicit short-window inequality.
\item[Related current target:] TF, above-BV return transport.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-CRITICAL-VERTICAL-CARRIES-TLOGN-001}\label{fail:FAIL-CRITICAL-VERTICAL-CARRIES-TLOGN-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-CRITICAL-VERTICAL-CARRIES-TLOGN-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.7.
\item[Claim:] On \(h\ge\sqrt{N/3}\), the block-derived vertical family can
still absorb a positive proportion of a \(t\log N\)-scale obligation.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Exact certificate:] The monomial collapse puts every vertical base in
\((\sqrt{2N/3},\sqrt N)\), so standard prime counting gives
\[
 |\mathcal V|\ll\sqrt N/\log N=O(t/\log N),
\]
and exactly one vertical layer per base gives
\[
 \log U_{\mathcal V}\ll\sqrt N=O(t)=o(t\log N).
\]
\item[What survives:] The critical square-root branch itself is not closed,
because production of enough large block factors degenerates there.  What is
closed is the possibility that an already-produced critical block family can
hide its logarithmic cost in vertical layers.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{C-MONOMIAL-REFLECTED-PAIR-SPARSITY}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-CUBEROOT-PIGEONHOLE-IS-BOUNDARY-CASE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-CUBEROOT-PIGEONHOLE-IS-BOUNDARY-CASE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-CUBEROOT-PIGEONHOLE-IS-BOUNDARY-CASE-001.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Earlier failure:] \texttt{FAIL-CUBEROOT-DEFECT-PIGEONHOLE-GIVES-POLYNOMIAL-STAR-001}
correctly kills raw cube-root pigeonhole as a concentration theorem.
\item[New explanation:] this is exactly the boundary value $m=2$ of
\texttt{G-POWER-THRESHOLD-DEFECT-COMPRESSION}: the threshold
$N^{1/(m+1)}$ is then $N^{1/3}$ and the guaranteed star exponent
$1/3-1/(m+1)$ is zero.  Every fixed $m\ge3$ gives a nontrivial polynomial
star.
\item[What survives:] do not infer polynomial concentration from cube-root
pigeonhole alone; first split the alphabet at a lower power threshold.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-DEADSMOOTH-PILLAI-001}\label{fail:FAIL-DEADSMOOTH-PILLAI-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-DEADSMOOTH-PILLAI-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Phase-3 continuation, 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] No canonical \(N\) carries two simultaneous dead-smooth carriers,
since none was found below \(3\cdot10^5\).
\item[Original motivation:] The search returned nothing at all, and the
configuration looks arithmetically absurd.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.  The \emph{search result} stands as
\texttt{COMP-DEADSMOOTH-CENSUS}; the \emph{exclusion} does not.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] None is needed: the claim has no proof.
\item[Exact certificate:] By \texttt{TD-DEADSMOOTH-NORMALFORM}(5), two
simultaneous dead-smooth carriers with \(\omega(a_j)=1\) are exactly a Pillai
coincidence \(|q^{e}-q'^{e'}|<h\) with \(q^{e},q'^{e'}>4x/5\), \(q,q'<h\) and
\(qq'\mid x\).  Excluding that unconditionally requires effective linear forms
in logarithms.  The corpus contains no such argument.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] An empty finite search was read as an
exclusion theorem.
\item[Why the argument failed:] This is \texttt{PROHIB-STATUS-LADDER}: a finite
computation, however clean, is not a universal statement.
\item[What survives:] The exact reduction to a Pillai equation, which is a
genuine normal form and the right object for a future attack.
\item[Safe weaker version:] ``No such pair occurs below \(3\cdot10^5\)'',
labelled \VERIFCOMP.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
\texttt{TD-DEADSMOOTH-NORMALFORM}(5) and \texttt{COMP-DEADSMOOTH-CENSUS}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Never convert an empty search into an exclusion.
\item[Related current target:] TD-SMALLSMOOTH.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-DEADSMOOTH-UNBOUNDED-001}\label{fail:FAIL-DEADSMOOTH-UNBOUNDED-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-DEADSMOOTH-UNBOUNDED-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Phase-3 continuation, 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] The exceptional dead-smooth class is negligible for every
\(N\), so the side condition \(\lceil t/3\rceil>\sigma^{+}_N(h)\) of
\texttt{TD-C0B-CLOSURE} can be discharged and removed.
\item[Original motivation:] Dead-smooth carriers are extraordinarily rare ---
\(19\) among \(514\,447\) tested, none doubled --- which invites the conclusion
that the class is uniformly negligible.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] \(N=60\,060\), \(p_0=30\,047\),
\(h=17\), \(t=8\).
\item[Exact certificate:] \(x=30\,030=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\) is a
primorial, so \(\mathcal P_N(h)=\{3,5,7,11,13\}\) --- every odd prime below
\(h\) divides \(x\).  The ceiling then degenerates:
\(\sigma^{+}_N(h)=6.32\) while \(\lceil t/3\rceil=3\).  The side condition
fails.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Rarity of the class in a sample was
confused with a bound valid for every \(N\).  The ceiling depends on how many
small primes divide \(x\), and \(x\) may legitimately be a primorial.
\item[Why the argument failed:] \(\sigma^{\rm dead}\) and \(\sigma^{+}\) are
small \emph{because} \(x\) usually has few small prime factors, not because the
dead-smooth normal form is intrinsically bounded.  No theorem forbids
\(x=\prod_{\ell\le h}\ell\).
\item[What survives:] \texttt{TD-DEADSMOOTH-CEILING} and
\texttt{TD-C0B-CLOSURE} exactly as stated, with the side condition retained as
a hypothesis.  It is an arithmetic condition on \(N\) alone, checkable in
\(O(\pi(h)\log x)\) operations, and it held in every tested canonical instance
with \(t\ge16\).
\item[Safe weaker version:] State the closure with the side condition, and
treat the small-smooth-\(x\) regime as a separate open case.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
\texttt{TD-C0B-CLOSURE} and the retained target TD-DENSITY.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not discharge a hypothesis because a sample makes it
look automatic; check the extremal arithmetic first.
\item[Related current target:] TD-DENSITY, \(P1^{\rm br}\).
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-EXACTD-NONCANONICAL-001}\label{fail:FAIL-EXACTD-NONCANONICAL-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-EXACTD-NONCANONICAL-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Exact-D audit; reaffirmed in the canonical bridge
audit \S11.2.
\item[Claim:] The Exact-D local row algebra --- pair compensation,
smoothness, primitive normal form, prime endpoint --- is enough to isolate
the canonical root, so canonicity need not be used as boundary transport.
\item[Original motivation:] The local conditions are sharp and eliminate
most models.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ as a substitute for minimality; \SCOPECORR\ as machinery.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] The recorded noncanonical normal
forms, including
\((q,r,m_0)=(3,\,5\,413\,103,\,81\,196\,545)\) --- note
\(81\,196\,545=3\cdot5\cdot5\,413\,103\) --- together with the two recorded
\(k=1\) examples.
\item[Exact certificate:] These models satisfy the local \(D_q,D_r\)
conditions, smoothness, pair failure and a prime endpoint, and are
eliminated \emph{only} by \(h<G\).  Removing \(h<G\) restores them.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Row algebra was asked to do the work
of the empty prime interval.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Local normal forms constrain a row; they do
not constrain the position of the root relative to \(x\).
\item[What survives:] \texttt{ARS-EXACTD}: pair compensation outside
\(q<r<2h\), the primitive normal form, and \(h^2>4m\) in the residual
regime --- all under an Exact-D \emph{pair failure} hypothesis, not under
CRD failure alone.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Use Exact-D only where the pair-failure
hypothesis is explicit, and state \(h<G\) as a separate input.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, \texttt{ARS-EXACTD} and the
ablation discussion of \(h<G\).
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not attempt to repair Exact-D by improving a
constant; the corpus already localises the missing step as
interval-to-ledger transport.
\item[Related current target:] C0a, \(T_D\), \(P1^{\rm br}\).
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-EXACTD-RESIDUAL-SURVIVES-SUBROOT-001}\label{fail:FAIL-EXACTD-RESIDUAL-SURVIVES-SUBROOT-001}

\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.20.
\item[Branch:] Retain Exact-D Pair Compensation failure as an obstruction when
$h\le\sqrt x$.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Certificate:] Existing Exact-D high-gap amplification says pair failure
forces $h^2>4m$.  But $h\le\sqrt x$ gives $h^2\le x<4m$ for sufficiently large
$x$.  Thus all first-front SMOOTH pairs satisfy Exact-D compensation on this
domain.
\item[Scope guard:] This closes only the pair-failure branch; it does not by
itself strengthen the global weighted-cut/K1 bound.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-EXTERNAL-ETA-IDENTIFICATION-001}\label{fail:FAIL-EXTERNAL-ETA-IDENTIFICATION-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-EXTERNAL-ETA-IDENTIFICATION-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT2 independent audit, Phase 3.
\item[Claim:] The high-floor reuse \(\eta(U)\ge\lceil n/3\rceil+c\) of an
external orthogonal packet can be charged to the canonical capacity ledger.
\item[Original motivation:] \(\eta\) is the same functional in both places, and
a large value looks like a large obligation wherever it occurs.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural, and it is exactly the
orthogonality that was thought to help.
\item[Exact certificate:] The packet is orthogonal, \(K_\times(R,U)=0\).  That
identity says precisely that \(U\) contributes nothing to the rooted collision
ledger.  Any functional built from cross-collision is therefore identically
zero on this configuration, so no such functional can carry \(\eta(U)\) into
\(\mathcal C_N(R)\).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Orthogonality was read as a licence to
add the two ledgers; it is the obstruction to doing so.
\item[What survives:] \texttt{TF-HIGH-FLOOR-HORIZONTAL-RIGIDITY} itself, now
\PROVEDs\ with both of its skeleton gaps closed.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Report \(\eta(U)\) as a property of \(U\) only.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
Proposition~\textup{[\,prop:missing-bridge\,]}, which states the exact minimal lemma
required: a \emph{source-side} statement that re-closing \(R\cup U\) changes
the multisource product by a factor whose logarithm is bounded below in terms
of \(\eta(U)\).
\item[Do not repeat:] Never add an orthogonal packet's ledger to the rooted
one; the zero cross-term is the reason it cannot be done.
\item[Related current target:] TF, K1, W1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

 A_R=(\gamma+\tau)\log N+\tau\log\frac{25}{18}
     -\sum_{q\in C\setminus Q}\log q.
\]
The exact target must use the exact right-hand side, not a lower bound for it.

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-FC8-SELF-CONTRADICTION-001}\label{fail:FAIL-FC8-SELF-CONTRADICTION-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-FC8-SELF-CONTRADICTION-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT2 independent audit, Phase 2.
\item[Claim:] The low-core capacity bound (FC8), being an upper bound on
\(J_R\) under canonical failure, can be contradicted by the forced lower bounds
already available, closing the \(\mathcal D\)/low-core front.
\item[Original motivation:] (FC8) is the first genuine upper capacity for
\(J_R\), and upper capacities are what a contradiction architecture wants.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.  (FC8) itself is \PROVEDs; the inference from it is not.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural; no finite witness needed.
\item[Exact certificate:] The only unconditional lower bound on \(J_R\)
available from canonical failure is \(J_R\ge3^{\eta(R)}\) by (LE3).  A
contradiction with (FC8) therefore requires
\(\eta(R)>(\gamma+\tau)\log_3N+\tau\log_3(25/18)-\sum_{C\setminus Q}\log_3q\),
that is \(\eta(R)\gtrsim\gamma\log N\).  Nothing in the corpus forces a
reuse count carrying a factor \(\log N\); the strongest available floor is
\(\eta(R)\ge|Q|+|H|\) (Theorem~\textup{[\,thm:lowcore-floor\,]}), which is bounded by
\(|R|\).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] An upper capacity was treated as
self-contradictory without a matching lower bound of the same order.
\item[Why the argument failed:] The two sides differ by a factor \(\log N\)
per low-core element; that gap is not an accident of effort but of what the
available identities can produce.
\item[What survives:] (FC8) as an upper capacity usable through the external
comparison (FC10), exactly as its own capacity paragraph states.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Report (FC8) only in the (FC10) form.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
Proposition~\textup{[\,prop:fc8-barrier\,]}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not attempt another self-contained contradiction from
(FC8); the barrier is at the level of available bounds.
\item[Related current target:] K1, P1BR.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-FRESH-BRANCH-PRIMACY-001}\label{fail:FAIL-FRESH-BRANCH-PRIMACY-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-FRESH-BRANCH-PRIMACY-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Phase-3 continuation, 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] The external fresh branch \(\mathcal D_{\rm fr}^{\rm ext}\) is
where the \(\mathcal D\) obligation is strongest, so cut statements should be
developed there first and restricted to it.
\item[Original motivation:] External carriers are candidate \emph{new sources}
and therefore the ones that bear on \(P1^{\rm br}\); that relevance was
transferred to the cut itself.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural, by
\texttt{TD-LOCALIZED-CUT}.
\item[Exact certificate:] For \(\tau\ge2\) distinct active primes bounded by
\(y\), \(C_{\rm cut}>\tau(\tau-1)\log((N-y)/y)\).  A fresh carrier gives only
\(y=N/6\) and hence the constant \(\log5\); a live smooth carrier gives
\(y<h\) and hence \(\log((N-h)/h)\), larger by orders of magnitude once
\(h=o(N)\).  The fresh branch is therefore the \emph{weakest} of the three for
cut purposes.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Relevance to \(P1^{\rm br}\) was
conflated with strength of the cut.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Two different functionals were being compared.
Only external carriers can be new sources; but the cut constant is governed by
the \emph{localisation} of the primes, and small primes localise better.
\item[What survives:] Both facts, kept apart.  Only the external branch bears on
\(P1^{\rm br}\); the live-smooth branch gives the largest cut defect.
\item[Safe weaker version:] State the cut with the explicit bound \(y\) and read
the constant off it, rather than fixing \(\log5\).
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, \texttt{TD-LOCALIZED-CUT}, with
\texttt{TD-FRESH-CUT} and \texttt{TD-FIVEFOLD-CUT} as its \(y=N/6\) cases.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not restrict a theorem to the sub-branch that happens
to be relevant downstream; state it where its proof lives.
\item[Related current target:] \(T_D\), \(P1^{\rm br}\).
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-FRINGE-ALPHABET-TRANSFER-001}\label{fail:FAIL-FRINGE-ALPHABET-TRANSFER-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-FRINGE-ALPHABET-TRANSFER-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT2 independent audit, Phase 4.
\item[Claim:] For \(\lambda_N>3\) the upper fringe is charged by the alphabet
\(\{\lambda,2\lambda-1\}\), by analogy with \(\{3,5\}\).
\item[Original motivation:] \(\{3,5\}=\{\lambda,2\lambda-1\}\) at
\(\lambda=3\), and (AN7) features \(2\lambda-1\).
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Exact certificate:] The admissible coefficients are determined by (AN5),
\(N(1-1/\lambda)/q<b<N/q\), together with \(b\) odd, \((b,N)=1\),
\(b\ge\lambda\).  For \(q\) ranging over
\((N/(2\lambda),N/\lambda)\) this interval has length \(N/(\lambda q)\in(1,2)\)
only near the top of the band; lower in the band it admits several odd values,
so the alphabet is a range, not a pair.  The two-letter alphabet at
\(\lambda=3\) is an accident of \(2<b<6\) admitting exactly \(\{3,5\}\).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] A coincidence at one value of
\(\lambda\) was read as a pattern.
\item[What survives:] (AN5) itself, which is the correct general statement and
the right starting point: compute the alphabet from the interval before
proposing any potential.
\item[Safe weaker version:] For general \(\lambda\), state the admissible
coefficient set as the odd integers coprime to \(N\) in the (AN5) interval.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, Phase-4 note in
Section~\textup{[\,sec:vnext2\,]}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not propose a monotone potential of \(D(q)=4q-N\) type
for \(\lambda>3\) before the alphabet is computed; \(D\) was built from the
coefficient \(3\).
\item[Related current target:] \(\lambda_N>3\) fringe capacity.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-GAMMA-BOUND-ROUTES-001}\label{fail:FAIL-GAMMA-BOUND-ROUTES-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]

\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT2 independent audit, Phase 2.
\item[Claim:] The adaptive indegree bound, the denominator of (FC8), a distinct
resource per low-core element, or the layered Euler defect bounds
\(\gamma=|C|\).
\item[Original motivation:] Each route looks like it converts local structure
into a global count.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ for all four, as routes; the underlying statements are
untouched.
\item[Exact certificate:] (i) Summing (AN2) against
Theorem~\textup{[\,thm:lowcore-floor\,]} gives
\(\gamma+|H|\le\sum_{q\in C}\lceil N/(6q)\rceil\), which every summand already
satisfies term by term.  (ii) Nothing distinguishes \(C\setminus Q\) from an
arbitrary set of distinct odd primes, so only the primorial bound applies, and
Corollary~\textup{[\,cor:primorial-ceiling\,]} then gives
\(\gamma\log\gamma\lesssim2\gamma\log N\), i.e.\ \(\gamma\lesssim N^2\).
(iii) A single row can host \(\log_3N\) low prime factors, so the parent count
bounds \(\gamma\) only by \(|R|\log_3N\).  (iv) The layered Euler route
produces Theorem~\textup{[\,thm:lowcore-floor\,]} itself, which bounds \(\eta(R)\) below
and the low-core primorial mass above, and \(\gamma\) in neither direction.
\item[What survives:] Theorem~\textup{[\,thm:lowcore-floor\,]} and
Corollary~\textup{[\,cor:primorial-ceiling\,]}, both new and both genuine.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not retry these four; a bound on \(\gamma\) needs a
mechanism that is not a summation of an existing local bound.
\item[Related current target:] (FC8), K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-GENERIC-ABSORPTION-001}\label{fail:FAIL-GENERIC-ABSORPTION-001}

\]

contains the factor \(59\), and
\(1718-59=1659=3\cdot7\cdot79\).  Thus the audited \(59\)-valuations of

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-GENERIC-PRIME-ROW-RPD-001}\label{fail:FAIL-GENERIC-PRIME-ROW-RPD-001}

\[
 \sum_{Y<r\le N^{1/3}}\sum_{k\ge2}(n_k^X(r)-1)_+

\]
\item[Certificate:] using the analytic sparse-moduli theorem underlying

 \qquad

\]
