\begin{faillog}{FAIL-GREEDY-AVOIDANCE-NAIVE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-GREEDY-AVOIDANCE-NAIVE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-GREEDY-AVOIDANCE-NAIVE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT3 hostile proof of the external selector.
\item[Claim:] In the external selector one may choose complements greedily,
avoiding the primes already used, and the surviving proportion of the fan is
\(\prod_{r\in\mathcal E}(1-\frac1{r-1})\gg1/\log\log N\).
\item[Original motivation:] \(|\mathcal E|=O((\log N)^{A+1})\), so the avoided
set is small compared with the fan, and the product looks Mertens-like.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ as an argument.  The \emph{conclusion} of the selector is
true --- see \texttt{G-BAD-BASE-SQUAREFREE-POLYLOG-EXTENSION-PROVED} --- but
not by this route.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural, two independent failures.
\item[Exact certificate:] (i) Without a prior roughness condition,
\(\mathcal E\) may contain small primes.  If \(3\in\mathcal E\) then
\(\sum_{r\in\mathcal E}1/(r-1)\ge\frac12\), and the Brun--Titchmarsh union
bound over \(\mathcal E\) already exceeds the whole fan, so the union bound
gives nothing.  (ii) To use \(\prod_{r\in\mathcal E}(1-\frac1{r-1})\) as a
density one needs a \emph{sieve} over \(\mathcal E\), not a union bound.  The
combined modulus is \(\prod_{r\in\mathcal E}r=\exp(\theta(y))\) with
\(y\approx(\log N)^{A+2}\), that is \(\exp((\log N)^{A+2})\), which vastly
exceeds \(N\); Siegel--Walfisz does not apply there, and a sieve at that level
would require a level-of-distribution input such as Bombieri--Vinogradov, which
was never declared.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] A product of local densities was used
where only a union bound was available, and the modulus range needed for the
alternative was never checked.
\item[What survives:] Everything, after reordering.  Imposing
\(w\)-roughness \emph{first} --- no prime below \(w=(\log N)^{A+2}\) divides a
complement except its own designated base --- forces \(\mathcal E\) to consist
only of primes \(\ge w\), whence
\(\sum_{r\in\mathcal E}1/(r-1)\le|\mathcal E|/(w-1)\ll1/\log N\) and a plain
union bound suffices.  The sieve then used has polylogarithmic sifting limit
and is truncated at a polylogarithmic level, so every modulus stays inside the
Siegel--Walfisz range and no level-of-distribution theorem is imported.
\item[Attribution correction:] the \(1/\log\log N\) loss is real, but it belongs
to the roughness sieve, where it is \(\asymp1/\log w\).  The coprimality step
costs only \(1+O(\log w/\log N)\).  vNEXT2 attributed the loss to the wrong
step.
\item[Safe weaker version:] State the selection as: sieve for roughness, then
delete squares, then union-bound the coprimality classes.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, Theorem~\textup{[\,thm:selector\,]}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not multiply local densities across conditions that
are only accessible by a union bound, and always check that the combined
modulus stays in the range of the distribution theorem being used.
\item[Related current target:] (FC10), K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-HALL-SUPPORT-001}\label{fail:FAIL-HALL-SUPPORT-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-HALL-SUPPORT-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Escape-or-Reuse campaign, 30 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] A Hall expansion over the support counts of all sources
yields the required capacity bound.
\item[Original motivation:] Every source contributes support, so a global
counting argument looked available.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] The recorded compression figure:
\(456\) sources compress to \(17\) factor atoms.  Status \VERIFCOMP; the raw
table was not reloaded in this extraction.
\item[Exact certificate:] With that degree of compression the naive
expansion has no room to run: the support side is far smaller than the
source side, so no Hall-type surplus exists in the required direction.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Sources and atoms were counted as if
they were in near-bijection.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Compression is exactly the regime in which
a counting surplus disappears.
\item[What survives:] The precise asymptotic polylog Hall matching theorem
is \emph{not} refuted by this: \texttt{G-POLYLOG-MATCHING} runs on a fixed
finite family of polylog prime-power layers with an enormous per-layer fan,
not on an all-source support count.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Restrict any Hall argument to the polylog layer
family where the fan is proved.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
\texttt{G-POLYLOG-PARENTS}, \texttt{G-POLYLOG-MATCHING}, target W1.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not run a counting argument across a compression.
\item[Related current target:] W1, K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-HIGHFLOOR-DOMAIN-VACUITY-001}\label{fail:FAIL-HIGHFLOOR-DOMAIN-VACUITY-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-HIGHFLOOR-DOMAIN-VACUITY-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT2 independent audit, Phase 1E.
\item[Claim:] \texttt{TF-HIGH-FLOOR-HORIZONTAL-RIGIDITY} applies to packets
that actually occur.
\item[Original motivation:] The theorem is stated unconditionally on its
hypothesis and its proof is complete.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.  The theorem is \PROVEDs; its \emph{antecedent} is
unverified.
\item[Exact certificate:] An exhaustive search over even \(N<3\cdot10^4\) and
all admissible seeds found \emph{no} bad child-closed packet with
\(\min U>N^{1/3}\) and \(U\subset(0,N/3)\).  Status of that search: \VERIFCOMP.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] None mathematically; the risk is
rhetorical --- quoting \(\eta(U)\ge\lceil n/3\rceil+c\) as though it were about
an exhibited object.
\item[What survives:] The theorem in full, with both skeleton gaps now proved:
\(\sigma\) has no cycles (a \(1\)-cycle forces \(N=u(u+1)\), hence \(u\mid N\)
and \(u\) inactive; a \(2\)-cycle forces \((v-u)(v+u+1)=0\); longer cycles are
excluded because \(f(x)=\sqrt{N-x}\) is strictly decreasing), and there are no
three consecutive square rows (the contraction constant of \(f\) puts
\(u_2,u_3\) within \(0.111\) of the fixed point for \(N\ge50\), forcing
\(u_2=u_3\) and hence a \(1\)-cycle).
\item[Safe weaker version:] Always state it as a conditional.
\item[Do not repeat:] An empty finite search is not evidence that the
hypothesis is unsatisfiable, and a complete proof is not an exhibited instance.
\item[Related current target:] TF, K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-INDIVIDUAL-MESOSCALE-BV-001}\label{fail:FAIL-INDIVIDUAL-MESOSCALE-BV-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-INDIVIDUAL-MESOSCALE-BV-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] v1.10 scale-wall continuation, 1 September 2026.
\item[Claim:] The v1.6 ``sub-sum of ordinary Bombieri--Vinogradov'' argument
can be transferred unchanged from a polylogarithmic base modulus to one
fixed base \(q=N^{\beta}\), \(\beta>0\), and still prove a positive lower-
sieve fan.
\item[Original motivation:] Extend the clean-parent theorem directly from
polylogarithmic labels to polynomially sized states.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Exact certificate:] For one polynomial base the expected prime/sieve
main term is of size at most
\[
 \asymp \frac{N}{q\,\log N\,\log z}
 =N^{1-\beta}\operatorname{polylog}(N)^{-1},
\]
whereas the ordinary Bombieri--Vinogradov all-moduli error available from
simply taking a sub-sum is
\[
 O_B\!\left(\frac{N}{(\log N)^B}\right).
\]
For every fixed \(B\) and every fixed \(\beta>0\), the latter is larger by a
factor \(N^{\beta}/\operatorname{polylog}(N)\).  Therefore the v1.6 error
comparison does not prove positivity for an individual mesoscopic base.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] A global mean error was treated as
though it scaled with the individual base modulus.
\item[What survives:] Aggregate use over many bases does work at the
unsieved parent-incidence level.  \texttt{G-BV-HARMONIC-PARENT-MASS} proves
that fixed positive reciprocal mass below the BV level yields
\(\gg N/\log N\) parent incidences and \(\gg N/\log^2N\) distinct
external parents.  \texttt{TD-HARMONIC-SUPPORT-DISPOSITION} supplies the
reciprocal-mass input on the D branch.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Use the existing individual selector only while
the prescribed base modulus is polylogarithmic, or prove a genuinely
aggregate many-base theorem with its own remainder accounting.
\item[Current replacement:] v1.10 adaptive lift remains the individual
polylog tool.  v1.11 adds genuinely aggregate clean extraction:
\texttt{G-BV-HARMONIC-CLEAN-EXTRACTION} selects a clean load-one subfamily
from mesoscopic reciprocal mass, and
\texttt{G-BV-POLYNOMIAL-HARMONIC-CLEAN-EXTRACTION} gives a polynomially
large clean family on fixed power bands.  Neither theorem supplies a fan for
every prescribed mesoscopic base.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not cite ordinary BV's total error as an
individual polynomial-modulus lower bound.
\item[Related current target:] TD scale bridge, W1, P1BR/K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-LARGE-MONOMIAL-PACKET-CAN-OCCUR-IN-BOTH-MOD3-CLASSES-001}\label{fail:FAIL-LARGE-MONOMIAL-PACKET-CAN-OCCUR-IN-BOTH-MOD3-CLASSES-001}

$3$.
\item[Certificate:] if $N\equiv1\pmod3$, then $w=N-q^2\equiv0\pmod3$; prime
$w$ must equal $3$, so at most one such edge exists.
\item[What survives:] a polynomial monomial packet can only remain when
$N\equiv2\pmod3$.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-LEDGER-INDEPENDENCE-LI5-SCOPE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-LEDGER-INDEPENDENCE-LI5-SCOPE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-LEDGER-INDEPENDENCE-LI5-SCOPE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.1, Phase 0B.
\item[Claim:] vNEXT4 introduced (LI5) under the heading ``that trivial bound is
the only one available'', suggesting \(\eta_{\rm supp}\) is the unique
ledger-derivable lower bound on \(\eta(S)\).
\item[Original motivation:] The witness family drives \(\eta(R_n)\) to infinity
at constant round datum, which does refute every \emph{growing} bound.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.  \texttt{G-POSITIVE-ROUND-LEDGER-INDEPENDENCE} is
preserved in full.
\item[Exact certificate:] The \(n=1\) member has \(\eta(R_1)=2\).  Hence any
\(F\) with \(F\le\eta\) satisfies only \(F(\mathfrak d)\le2\) at that datum;
constants up to \(2\) are consistent with the family.  So the family excludes
unbounded growth in \(\Delta\), not the existence of some bounded lower bound.
\item[What survives:] (LI5\('\)): no universally valid lower bound on
\(\eta(S)\) expressible solely as a function of the round datum can grow
unboundedly with \(\Delta\); in particular none supplies the
\(\gamma\log N\)-scale bound the (LE3)+(FC8) route consumes.  This is the only
form used downstream, and it is what makes the route unavailable.
\item[Do not repeat:] Distinguish ``no bound of the required size'' from
``no bound''.  Only the former was proved.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{P1BR-ADDITIVE-COUPLING}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-LF2-AS-UPPER-BOUND-001}\label{fail:FAIL-LF2-AS-UPPER-BOUND-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-LF2-AS-UPPER-BOUND-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT3.1 correction round.
\item[Claim:] In the (FC8) frontier certificate, ``(LF2) bounds \(\eta(R)\)
above by \(|R|\)''.
\item[Original motivation:] \(|Q|+|H|\le|R|\) is true, and the certificate
needed \(\eta(R)\) to be small.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Exact certificate:] (LF2) reads \(\eta(R)\ge|Q|+|H|\).  It is a
\emph{lower} bound.  The inequality \(|Q|+|H|\le|R|\) says only that this
recorded lower bound is itself at most \(|R|\); it places no ceiling on
\(\eta(R)\), which by (LE2) can exceed \(|R|\) whenever rows carry repeated
support.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] A bound on the right-hand side of a
lower-bound inequality was read as a bound on the left-hand side.
\item[What survives:] The certificate, correctly stated: to contradict (FC8)
through (LE3) one needs a \emph{lower} bound on \(\eta(R)\) of order
\(\gamma\log N\), and the recorded (LF2) does not carry a factor \(\log N\).
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
Proposition~\textup{[\,prop:fc8-corrected\,]}, status
\textsf{FRONTIER CERTIFICATE / RELATIVE TO RECORDED BOUNDS}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Never infer a ceiling from a floor.
\item[Related current target:] K1, \(\gamma\).
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-LITERAL-LINEAGE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-LITERAL-LINEAGE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-LITERAL-LINEAGE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Post-v7.5 layer-lineage audit.
\item[Claim:] Once a prime label \(\ell\) is produced, its valuation can be
followed literally through the row indexed by \(\ell\).
\item[Original motivation:] Residual factors were pictured as conserved
tokens moving down a path.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Universal for active \(\ell\).
\item[Exact certificate:] Since \(\ell\nmid N\),
\(N-\ell\equiv N\not\equiv0\pmod\ell\); hence
\[
v_\ell(N-\ell)=0.
\]
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Row labels and factor labels were
identified.
\item[Why the argument failed:] The dynamics changes the row index; it
does not conserve a prime token along a path.
\item[What survives:] Global valuation accounting \(T=UJ\), collision
layers, and residual products.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Track incidence across a finite set of rows,
not literal pathwise conservation.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, G-TUJ and the prime-power layer
formalism.
\item[Do not repeat:] Never write a lineage law without an exact valuation
identity at every transition.
\item[Related current target:] \(E1,K1\).
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-LOSSLESS-INTERFACE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-LOSSLESS-INTERFACE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-LOSSLESS-INTERFACE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.1, Phase 4.
\item[Claim:] That a canonical row \(c_j\) can be transferred to a global prime
selection with its information preserved --- the round's primary success
criterion, third arrow.
\item[Original motivation:] The bundle query does preserve strictly more than
the old single-base query: exact valuations, the cofactor class and the mirror
relation \(D\mid p-a_j\).  It was natural to hope the preserved part could be
made all of \(A_j\).
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ for lossless transfer, under every distribution theorem
presently available.  The bundle lift itself is \PROVEDs.
\item[Exact certificate:] Theory Core \texttt{P0-QUERY-CAPACITY}: if every
member of a residue class \(n\equiv a\ (M)\) satisfies \(v_q(N-n)=e\), then
\(q^{e+1}\mid M\).  Taking \(n=a\) and \(n=a-M\) forces \(q^e\mid M\); and if
\(v_q(M)=e\) exactly then one \(k\) in each complete residue system mod \(q\)
gives \(q^{e+1}\mid N-a+kM\).  Hence \(D\rad D\mid M\) and
\(\log D\le\frac E{E+1}\log M\).  With Siegel--Walfisz, \(\log M\le K\log\log
N\), so the preserved fraction is \(<K\log\log N/\log(N/2)\to0\).  Under GRH
the fraction is at most \(\tfrac12\) (at most \(\tfrac14\) for squarefree
bundles), so GRH does not make it lossless either.  Losslessness needs a level of distribution \(\theta\ge1\) for an
\emph{individually specified} modulus of size \(N^{1-o(1)}\) --- stronger than
GRH, and not the average-level statement of Elliott--Halberstam.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Treating ``retain more information'' as
free.  Retention is paid for in the modulus, at a rate fixed by (QC1), and the
modulus is capped by the available distribution theorem.
\item[What survives:] The exact capacity: \(\log D\le\frac E{E+1}K\log\log N\),
and everything the bundle does preserve, which is genuinely more than the old
query.  See \texttt{P0-EXACT-BUNDLE-LIFT} and
\texttt{P0-ADAPTIVE-BUNDLE-DICHOTOMY}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not propose an interface that preserves a positive
proportion of a canonical row without first naming the level-of-distribution
theorem that pays for it, and do not import Bombieri--Vinogradov silently ---
this corpus does not use it anywhere.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{P1BR-ADDITIVE-COUPLING},
\texttt{P0-BUNDLE-ROUGH-HIGHPOWER-BRANCH}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-LOWBASE-POWERFUL-ROWS-AS-INDEPENDENT-VERTICAL-WALL-001}\label{fail:FAIL-LOWBASE-POWERFUL-ROWS-AS-INDEPENDENT-VERTICAL-WALL-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-LOWBASE-POWERFUL-ROWS-AS-INDEPENDENT-VERTICAL-WALL-001.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ as an independent primary frontier.
\item[Killed description:] a polynomial-size canonical low core may keep an

\item[Certificate:] v4.37 proves, pending audit, that for

\[
 \log(D_CJ_R)=\Omega_\alpha(\gamma\log N).
\]
Equivalently, near-pure vertical escape forces $\gamma=N^{o(1)}$.
\item[What survives:] a subpolynomial low core or a non-negligible D/J
payment; rowwise powerful-divisor structure remains useful downstream.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-LOWCORE-CARDINALITY-FC8-WEIGHT-001}\label{fail:FAIL-LOWCORE-CARDINALITY-FC8-WEIGHT-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-LOWCORE-CARDINALITY-FC8-WEIGHT-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.4.
\item[Claim:] Once the reflected block forces large \(\gamma=|C|\), the layered
Euler theorem automatically converts this into enough rooted reuse to contradict
FC8.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Exact certificate:] Canonical layered Euler gives only
\[
 \eta(R)+\nu(R)\ge |R|+1\ge\gamma+2,
\]
hence only
\[
 \max\{\log J_R,\log U_R\}\ge\frac{\gamma+2}{2}\log3.
\]
This is \(O(\gamma)\) guaranteed log mass.  The recorded FC8 route through
\(J_R\ge3^{\eta(R)}\) needs a lower bound at scale \(\gamma\log N\) unless a
separate large denominator is supplied.  Moreover the population may be paid
vertically through prime-power layers \(U_R\); the generic failed-world
prime-power examples show that such vertical storage is a real mechanism.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Cardinality was confused with weighted
prime-base mass, and horizontal reuse was treated as if it were the only defect
channel.
\item[What survives:] vNEXT4.4 produces a genuine FC8 denominator on the
sub-square-root large-factor branch, and the exact horizontal/vertical split
remains available.  A theorem forcing large bases or upper-bounding cheap
vertical storage would reopen the route.
\item[Do not repeat:] A new lower bound on \(\gamma\), \(\eta+\nu\), or an
unweighted layer count is not a consumer unless its logarithmic bases are
controlled.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{C-VERTICAL-LOWCORE-CAPACITY}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-LOWCORE-CHILDCLOSED-001}\label{fail:FAIL-LOWCORE-CHILDCLOSED-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-LOWCORE-CHILDCLOSED-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] v1.23 low-core continuation, 1 September 2026.

$C=R\cap(0,N/6)$ may be treated as a child-closed failed subsystem.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Why the inference fails:] The theorem controls the location of
\emph{repeated targets}, not all children of low rows.  A low row $u<N/6$ has
$N-u>5N/6$, and a prime factor of this complement can lie in $(N/6,N/3)$.
Thus an edge may leave $C$ for the upper fringe.
\item[What survives:] Every repeated target and the complete factor $J_R$ are
supported in $C$; every high state has a unique-parent forest structure and
returns to $C$ when parent ancestry is followed backwards.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
\texttt{G-CANONICAL-REUSE-LOWCORE} and
\texttt{G-CANONICAL-UPPER-FRINGE-FOREST}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not apply G-MULTISOURCE-LOCK, low-packet product locks,
or child-closed component arguments directly to $C$ without separately proving
closure for the subset in question.
\item[Related current target:] K1 low-core upper capacity.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-MATCHING-CAPACITY-001}\label{fail:FAIL-MATCHING-CAPACITY-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-MATCHING-CAPACITY-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Canonical bridge audit \S5.3, 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] An injective, load-one assignment of external parents to
layers bounds the ambient collision cost, closing the capacity target.
\item[Original motivation:] Load one removes repeated use of a single
parent, which was mistaken for removing the cost.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ --- the matching theorem itself is \PROVEDs; the
inference drawn from it is not.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural; no finite witness is
needed.
\item[Exact certificate:] Injectivity leaves two costs untouched.  One
selected row \(N-p\) may meet many atoms of \(R\), inflating
\(K_\times(R,\mathscr P)\); and two distinct selected rows may share
unintended new support, inflating \(K(\mathscr P)\).  Greedy selection of
pairwise-coprime complements would have to avoid, for each previously
chosen \(p'\), every class \(p\equiv N\pmod t\) with \(t\mid N-p'\);
Siegel--Walfisz for a single polylog modulus gives no uniform positive count
under a growing adaptive system of such prohibitions, and some \(t\) may be
large.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Existence and load were confused with
cost.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Abundance is a statement about one modulus
at a time; capacity is a statement about a whole selected family at once.
\item[What survives:] \texttt{G-POLYLOG-PARENTS} and
\texttt{G-POLYLOG-MATCHING}, now for all polylog prime-power layers, both
with an explicitly \textsf{INEFFECTIVE} threshold.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Report load one and the two uncontrolled terms
separately; never report their conjunction as capacity.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, target K1, which is exactly the
missing bound \(K_\times(R,\mathscr P)+K(\mathscr P)\le\mathcal C_N(R)\).
\item[Do not repeat:] This is the precise point at which abundance stops
becoming clean capacity; do not cross it silently.
\item[Related current target:] W1, K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-MERGER-COUNT-IMPLIES-AMBIENT-J-001}\label{fail:FAIL-MERGER-COUNT-IMPLIES-AMBIENT-J-001}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-MERGER-WEIGHT-TO-J-TOPOLOGY-001}\label{fail:FAIL-MERGER-WEIGHT-TO-J-TOPOLOGY-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-MERGER-WEIGHT-TO-J-TOPOLOGY-001.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Killed sufficient strategy:] prove
$\Delta\log J\gg W(E)$ using only child closure, source counts, graph
topology, support multiplicities and the v28 reverse-extension ledger.
\item[Certificate:] ELCFS finite realisation permits arbitrarily large source
weights attached through a fixed low target.  The topology grows while the
horizontal receiving weight remains only $e\log q$.
\item[What survives:] CRD arithmetic absent from ELCFS---the map $N-p$,

\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.2.

\(r=x+h_r\), \(m_r=x-h_r\), one has \(r=m_r+2h_r\).  Hence for every odd

\[
 q\mid(r-2j)\iff q\mid h_r-j.
\]
No minimality of \(p_0\) is used.

classification changes from ``canonical selector information'' to generic
upper-root geometry.

minimality/prime-freeness, e.g.\ \(h<G\), not identities valid for every
upper root.

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-NESTED-PRIMEPOWER-PACKING-GIVES-CUMULATIVE-SAVING-001}\label{fail:FAIL-NESTED-PRIMEPOWER-PACKING-GIVES-CUMULATIVE-SAVING-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-NESTED-PRIMEPOWER-PACKING-GIVES-CUMULATIVE-SAVING-001.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Killed inference:] simultaneous use of the nested spacing bounds for
$r^2,r^3,\ldots,r^e$ must create an extra cumulative saving beyond the
single-layer parent-slot envelope.
\item[Certificate:] if $\kappa$ rows lie in one exact layer
$v_r(N-p)=e$, then $n_k(r)=\kappa$ for every $1\le k\le e$.
Consequently all nested layers are realised by the same packet and
\[
 \sum_{k\ge2}(n_k(r)-1)_+=(e-1)(\kappa-1).
\]
The support graph sees only $\kappa-1$ repeated $r$-edges.
\item[Do not repeat:] nested packing alone cannot turn valuation depth into an
$O(1)$ or $O(\log\log N)$ bounded-multiplicity graph charge.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-ORTHOGONAL-BRIDGE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-ORTHOGONAL-BRIDGE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-ORTHOGONAL-BRIDGE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT3, Phases 2--3.
\item[Claim:] Although cross-collision is dead under \(K_\times(R,U)=0\), a
source- or product-side functional can still carry \(\eta(U)\) from an external
orthogonal packet into a capacity determined by \(R\).
\item[Original motivation:] The source product of \texttt{G-MULTISOURCE-LOCK}
does change when a packet is adjoined, so it looked like a live channel.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural, by exact decoupling.
\item[Exact certificate:] For disjoint bad child-closed \(R,U\),
\texttt{G-ORTHOGONAL-DECOUPLING} gives
\(\Gamma_N(S)=\Gamma_N(R)\dot\cup\Gamma_N(U)\),
\(\Src(S)=\Src(R)\dot\cup\Src(U)\), \(T_S=T_RT_U\), \(J_S=J_RJ_U\),
\(U_S=U_RU_U\), \(\eta(S)=\eta(R)+\eta(U)\), \(\nu(S)=\nu(R)+\nu(U)\), and the
multisource lock for \(S\) factors as the product of the two locks.  Every
recorded functional is therefore a disjoint-union homomorphism, and the
recorded state of \(R\) is \emph{identical} for every admissible \(U\).  The
target inequality \(\log(T_{R\cup U}/T_R)\ge c_0\eta(U)\) does hold, with
\(c_0=\log3\), and is worthless: its left side equals \(\log T_U\).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] The source product does change, but it
changes by exactly \(U\)'s own source product; nothing is shared.
\item[Why the argument failed:] \(K_\times(R,U)=0\) is not an extra hypothesis
to be worked around --- it is \emph{automatic} for disjoint child-closed
packets, and it is a symptom of total decoupling rather than of one blocked
channel.
\item[What survives:] \texttt{G-BRIDGE-ROUTING-EQUIVALENCE}: a bridge can exist
only if \(U\cap R\ne\varnothing\), which is precisely the TD/TF routing target.
The two fronts are one.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Report \(\eta(U)\) as a property of \(U\) alone.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
Theorem~\textup{[\,thm:decoupling\,]}, Corollary~\textup{[\,cor:worthless-coupling\,]},
Theorem~\textup{[\,thm:bridge-routing\,]}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not seek any functional coupling two disjoint
child-closed packets; all recorded functionals provably factor.
\item[Related current target:] TD, TF, K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-ORTHOGONALITY-AS-HYPOTHESIS-001}\label{fail:FAIL-ORTHOGONALITY-AS-HYPOTHESIS-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-ORTHOGONALITY-AS-HYPOTHESIS-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT3, Phase 2.
\item[Claim:] \(K_\times(R,U)=0\) is a special favourable hypothesis on the
external packet, to be secured by construction.
\item[Original motivation:] It is written as a hypothesis throughout the
external-packet material.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Exact certificate:] (OD4).  If \(R\) and \(U\) are disjoint and both
child-closed, then \(\Gamma_N(R)\subseteq R\) and
\(\Gamma_N(U)\subseteq U\) are disjoint, so no prime divides a complement on
both sides and every cross gcd is \(1\).  Orthogonality is a consequence of
disjointness plus child-closure, not an independent assumption.
\item[What survives:] Every statement conditioned on orthogonality, now with
the hypothesis recognised as redundant given the other two.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not spend effort ``arranging'' orthogonality, and do
not read it as evidence of a favourable configuration; it signals decoupling.
\item[Related current target:] TF, K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-P0-INFORMATION-SELECTOR-001}\label{fail:FAIL-P0-INFORMATION-SELECTOR-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-P0-INFORMATION-SELECTOR-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.1, Phase 9.
\item[Claim:] The central hypothesis of the round: that \(p_0\) identifies the
particular additive--multiplicative correlations a global prime-distribution
theorem should preserve.
\item[Original motivation:] The canonical reflected block is the only place in
CRD where a \emph{composite} row of size \(>N/2\) with a canonical mirror is
produced deterministically.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.  Not refuted; \textbf{not established}.
\item[Exact certificate:] Theory Core \texttt{P0-CANONICITY-ABLATION}.  Every
clause of \texttt{P0-EXACT-BUNDLE-LIFT} classifies as (AB-A) ``fixed \(N\)
only'' or (AB-B) ``an arbitrary reflected pair \(a+c=N\)''.  Replacing \(p_0\)
by any upper-half prime \(p_1\) leaves (BL3)--(BL6) and (BL5) word for word
intact on every row whose \(c'_j\) is composite.  Canonicity is used in exactly
one place: the prime-free interval \([x,p_0)\) makes \emph{every} \(c_j\)
composite, so branch (MC1) is available on the whole block.  Measured on the
\(301\) recorded noncanonical failed upper roots, \(32{,}766\) of \(130{,}090\)
reflected rows --- \(25.2\%\) --- have \(c'_j\) prime and are unbundleable
(their single block costs \(c_j'^2>N\)).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] A non-vacuity guarantee is not an
information-selection principle.  Canonicity guarantees the construction is
always available; it does not make the construction, or its conclusion,
different.
\item[What survives:] One genuinely canonical statement, (MR2): for
\(q^e\Vert m\), \(q\mid c_j\iff q\mid h-j\), from
\texttt{ARS-CANON-GEOMETRY}.  No consequence was built on it in this round.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not record a \texttt{P0-INFORMATION-SELECTOR-CERTIFICATE}
without an ablation in which the conclusion actually fails after the canonical
datum is deleted.  None was found.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{P1BR-ADDITIVE-COUPLING},
\texttt{P0-BUNDLE-ROUGH-HIGHPOWER-BRANCH}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-P0-ZEROHOLE-ESSENTIAL-001}\label{fail:FAIL-P0-ZEROHOLE-ESSENTIAL-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-P0-ZEROHOLE-ESSENTIAL-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.2.
\item[Claim:] The fact that the canonical reflected block has no prime holes is,
by itself, the essential \(p_0\)-specific additive--multiplicative glue.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ as a mechanism for the active/overflow mass argument.
\item[Exact certificate:] If \(p_1\) is the immediate next prime after canonical
\(p_0>x\), the strict \(p_1\)-reflected block has exactly one prime hole,
namely \(p_0\), at index \((p_1-p_0)/2\).  More generally the fixed \(p_k\)
block has exactly the \(k\) earlier primes as holes.  Iterating the recorded
pointwise short-interval bound a fixed number of times gives
\(p_k-x=O_k(x^{0.525})\), so deleting the holes costs only \(O_k(\log x)\) in
the block active-mass identity when the width tends to infinity.
\item[Why the argument failed:] The earlier 25.2\% statistic concerned a broad
family of noncanonical upper roots; it was not the immediate \(p_0\to p_1\)
ablation.  The correct immediate ablation is a one-hole perturbation, not a
positive-density destruction of the block.
\item[What survives:] \(p_0\) still gives the exact zero-hole formulation and
may be essential through stronger canonical information such as \(h<G\),
Exact-D, or another conclusion which actually fails already at \(p_1\).
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not infer a \texttt{P0-INFORMATION-SELECTOR-CERTIFICATE}
from the absence of prime holes alone.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{C-CRITICAL-SQRT-GAP-BRANCH}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-PARENT-LATTICE-DOMAIN-001}\label{fail:FAIL-PARENT-LATTICE-DOMAIN-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-PARENT-LATTICE-DOMAIN-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] v0.1 audit, canonical--ambient split correction.
\item[Claim:] The parent lattice of a layer may be treated as the full
residue class \(p\equiv N\pmod{\ell^k}\) over all primes.
\item[Original motivation:] The analytic count is naturally stated over all
primes in an interval.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Definitional.
\item[Exact certificate:] The correct object is
\(\mathcal P_N(\ell^k)=\{p\in\mathcal A_N:\ell^k\mid N-p\}\), the
intersection of the congruence class with the \emph{finite active prime
universe} \(\mathcal A_N\).  Primes dividing \(N\), and primes at least
\(N\), are not states.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] An ambient analytic set was used as
a set of CRD states.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Counting in the class is legitimate;
treating every counted prime as a usable parent is not.
\item[What survives:] \texttt{G-POLYLOG-PARENTS}, which restricts to
\(p\in(N/2,N)\) and proves activity and externality explicitly.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Intersect with \(\mathcal A_N\) at the moment
the class is introduced.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, notation entry
\(\mathcal P_N(\ell^k)\) and \texttt{G-POLYLOG-PARENTS}.
\item[Do not repeat:] A residue class is not a state set.
\item[Related current target:] W1, K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-POSITIVE-ROUND-CONSEQUENCE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-POSITIVE-ROUND-CONSEQUENCE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-POSITIVE-ROUND-CONSEQUENCE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT3.1, Phase-3 semantic audit.
\item[Claim:] Forcing a positive signed round is progress toward a
contradiction, so the (FC10) route closes once \(\gamma\) is controlled.
\item[Original motivation:] The (DP1)--(DP5) depletion apparatus is elaborate
and its conclusion is that nonpositive rounds cannot continue; the natural
reading is that the alternative must be favourable.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.  The depletion apparatus is untouched; the inference from
its escape branch is not supported.
\item[Exact certificate:] By (EB6), \(\Delta>0\) says exactly
\(\sum_{r\in B_0}\log r>W_R(B_-)\): the fresh support mass of the selected rows
exceeds the rooted reuse mass they touch.  A mechanical audit of every
\texttt{DOMAIN} line and every proof in the Theory Core found three theorems
assuming \emph{nonpositive} rounds ---
\texttt{G-ROW-SATURATION-ROOTED-DEFECT},
\texttt{G-EXTERNAL-BAD-SUPPORT-SATURATION-DISPOSITION},
\texttt{G-GLOBALLY-CLEAN-EXTERNAL-SUPPORT-BUDGET} --- and \emph{none} assuming
a positive round.  Nothing derives a GOOD state, a capacity violation, or any
canonical obligation from \(\Delta>0\).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] The escape branch of a dichotomy was
treated as a conclusion.  Structurally \(\Delta>0\) is \emph{growth} of the
enlarged world, not contradiction; and growth cannot be iterated to exhaustion,
because designated bases live below \((\log N)^A\) while
\(|\mathcal A_N|\sim N/\log N\).
\item[What survives:] Everything about nonpositive rounds, and
\texttt{G-GAMMA-POLYLOG-FORCES-POSITIVE-ROUND}, which correctly delivers the
positive round.  What is corrected is only what that delivery is worth.
\item[Safe weaker version:] ``\(\gamma\) polylog forces a positive signed
round.''  Never ``\ldots\ forces a contradiction''.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
Proposition~\textup{[\,prop:positive-dead-end\,]} and the new open target
\texttt{P1BR-POSITIVE-ROUND-CONSEQUENCE}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not announce that a wall has moved because an object
is now forced to exist; check first that something consumes that object.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{P1BR-POSITIVE-ROUND-CONSEQUENCE},
P1BR, K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-POSITIVE-ROUND-EXHAUSTION-001}\label{fail:FAIL-POSITIVE-ROUND-EXHAUSTION-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-POSITIVE-ROUND-EXHAUSTION-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4, Phase 9.
\item[Claim:] That repeated positive rounds must eventually run out of fresh
primes, giving a contradiction by exhaustion.
\item[Original motivation:] Nonpositive rounds deplete the integer potential
\(\mathfrak J_k\) of (DP4); by symmetry one hopes positive rounds deplete
something too.
\item[Status:] \KILLED, quantitatively.
\item[Exact certificate:] All fresh support of an external upper-half round
lies below \(N/6\) by (RC2).  The total logarithmic demand of the whole
selector output at exponent \(A\) is at most \((\log N)^{A+1}\); the supply in
that band is \(\vartheta(N/6)\ge N/12\).  The ratio tends to \(0\) like
\((\log N)^{A+1}/N\).  Theory Core,
\texttt{G-AMBIENT-SUPPLY-NONDEPLETION}.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] \(\Delta>0\) is a statement of growth.
Growth has no terminal state when the reservoir is superpolynomially larger
than the demand.
\item[What survives:] The depletion statement for \emph{nonpositive} rounds,
(DP1)--(DP4), which is unaffected and remains the only monotone integer
potential in the DAG.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not argue by exhaustion without comparing demand to
\(\vartheta\) of the relevant band.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{P1BR-ADDITIVE-COUPLING}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-POSITIVE-ROUND-LEDGER-CONSEQUENCE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-POSITIVE-ROUND-LEDGER-CONSEQUENCE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-POSITIVE-ROUND-LEDGER-CONSEQUENCE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4, Phase 7.
\item[Claim:] That the failure recorded at
\texttt{FAIL-POSITIVE-ROUND-CONSEQUENCE-001} was a gap in the present list of
theorems, so that a consequence of \(\Delta>0\) could be found by writing more
theorems in the same language.
\item[Original motivation:] vNEXT3.1 established option F by a mechanical
audit of the file's headers.  An audit of a text is silent about what could be
added to the text.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ for ledger-only derivations.  \textbf{Not} a refutation of
\texttt{P1BR-POSITIVE-ROUND-CONSEQUENCE} itself.
\item[Exact certificate:] Define the round datum
\(\mathfrak d(S,\mathscr P)\) as the rows, their supports, the heights on those
supports and \(\kappa_S\) restricted to those supports.  Every quantity in
(EB6)--(EB10), (DP1)--(DP5) and (PD1) is a function of \(\mathfrak d\).  The
family \(\mathfrak S_n\) of Theory Core
\texttt{G-POSITIVE-ROUND-LEDGER-INDEPENDENCE} has constant \(\mathfrak d\),
constant \(\Delta>0\), and \(\eta(R_n)=n+1\to\infty\); it is child-closed with
a unique source, has no unit rows, and is routing-compatible.  Its member
\(n=1\) has \(\eta(R_1)=2\) while \(\Delta\) can be made arbitrarily large by
raising the two fresh heights.  Hence the only lower bound on \(\eta\)
expressible in \(\mathfrak d\) is the trivial
\(\eta_{\rm supp}=\sum_{r\in B_-}(\kappa(r)-1)\), which is \(0\) whenever
\(B_-=\varnothing\); in particular no such bound grows with \(\Delta\).  The
witnesses exist by \texttt{GEN-FINITE-REALISATION}.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] The (LE3)+(FC8) route consumes a
\emph{lower} bound on \(\eta(R)\) of order \(\gamma\log N\).  A nonpositive
round supplies one by (EB8).  A positive round supplies an \emph{upper} bound
on the rooted mass of its own support and constrains \(\Gamma_N(R)\) nowhere
else --- which is exactly where the witnesses place all their incidence.
\item[What survives:] The asymmetry is proved, not assumed: for a nonpositive
round the same datum does bound \(\eta(S)\) below.  The obstruction is the sign,
not the bookkeeping.
\item[Safe weaker version:] A consequence may still be derivable using an
axiom that the witness family violates.  Three are identified and recorded as
live: (L1) \(\mathcal D(p)=N-p\); (L2) \(\gcd(N-p,N-p')\mid p'-p\); (L3) band
localisation plus prime counting.  All three are additive.
\item[Do not repeat:] Loss-control rule (LR1): a claimed consequence of a
positive round must name a quantity that is not a function of the round datum.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{P1BR-ADDITIVE-COUPLING}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-POTENTIAL-CAPACITY-001}\label{fail:FAIL-POTENTIAL-CAPACITY-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-POTENTIAL-CAPACITY-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] v7.5 first-front audit; retained in v0.1.
\item[Claim:] A first-front-only potential capacity
\(\mathcal C_S<\mathcal D_S\) holds canonically and supplies the needed
contradiction.
\item[Original motivation:] Pairwise row isolation seemed to make the
available factor capacity smaller than root demand.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] \(N=4736, p_0=2371, h=3\),
\(m=2365=5\cdot11\cdot43\).
\item[Exact certificate:] The three first-front rows are
\[
4736-5=4731=3\cdot19\cdot83,
\quad 4736-11=4725=3^3\cdot5^2\cdot7,
\]
\[
4736-43=4693=13\cdot19^2.
\]
With the source definitions, the audited values are
\(\mathcal C_S\approx22.60>\mathcal D_S\approx20.16\).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Potential parents were counted as
if their availability already encoded closure and actual incidence.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Pair isolation controls collisions, not
which rows are dynamically realised or simultaneously usable.
\item[What survives:] Exact collision identities for actual rows.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Introduce closure/activation first, then charge
only realised rows.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, G-COLLISION-CUT,
G-AMBIENT-PROMOTION, and target \(P1^{\rm br}\).
\item[Do not repeat:] Potential incidence is not actual incidence.
\item[Related current target:] \(L1,W1,K1\).
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-POWER-THRESHOLD-TO-POLYLOG-001}\label{fail:FAIL-POWER-THRESHOLD-TO-POLYLOG-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-POWER-THRESHOLD-TO-POLYLOG-001.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Original killed formulation:] power-threshold compression can never
force a polylogarithmic / near-logarithmic star, because reaching that scale
requires $m\to\infty$.
\item[Correction:] variable $m$ is legal with its explicit occupied-base
error.  Taking $m\asymp\log N/\log\log N$ can force
$q_0\le(\log N)^{1+o(1)}$ with multiplicity $N^{1/3-o(1)}$ on the low branch.
\item[What the no-go really says:] one threshold cannot simultaneously reach
that star scale and retain the old $M\log N$-scale generic high-$J$ lower
bound.  The high branch falls to
$M(\log\log N)^2/\log N$.
\item[Do not repeat:] do not interpret the v4.43 fixed-$m$ calculation as a
ban on growing $m$.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-PRODUCT-BUDGET-ALONE-CANNOT-PRESERVE-NEARCRITICAL-STAR}\label{fail:FAIL-PRODUCT-BUDGET-ALONE-CANNOT-PRESERVE-NEARCRITICAL-STAR}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-PRODUCT-BUDGET-ALONE-CANNOT-PRESERVE-NEARCRITICAL-STAR.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Killed mechanism:] preserve $N^{1/3-o(1)}$ rows under repeated exact-layer
peeling using only distinct peeled bases, growth of the common modulus,
parent-slot, and separate valuation-layer counts.
\item[Sharp cumulative-loss bound:] writing
$X=\log N$, $B_i=\log Q_i$ and $\ell_i=\log q_i$,
\[
 \mathcal L_t:=\sum_{i<t}\log E_i
 \le
 \sum_{i<t}\log\frac{X-B_i}{\ell_i}
 \le
 \log\frac{Q_t}{Q_{\rm in}}
 +(1+o(1))\frac{\log N}{(\log\log N)^2}.
\]
The coefficient $1$ before $\log(Q_t/Q_{\rm in})$ is asymptotically sharp
from the inspected scalar data alone.
\item[Certificate:] a primorial hostile sequence with consecutive small
primes up to $a\log N$, $1/3<a<2/3$, satisfies simultaneously
\[
 Q_t=N^{a+o(1)},\qquad \prod_iE_i=N^{a+o(1)}.
\]
Thus the formal cardinality can collapse before the modulus reaches the
$N^{2/3}$ parent-slot scale.
\item[Sharp scope guard:] the no-go ignores global compatibility of all
valuations in the same integer $N-p$ and therefore does not apply to
simultaneous joint-valuation compression.
\item[Current replacement:] \texttt{G-SUBCRITICAL-ALPHABET-SIMULTANEOUS-VALUATION-FREEZE}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-QUOTIENT-SIEVE-POLYNOMIAL-RANGE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-QUOTIENT-SIEVE-POLYNOMIAL-RANGE-001}

\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-QUOTIENT-SIEVE-POLYNOMIAL-RANGE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.6.
\item[Claim:] The fixed-\((s,b)\) two-linear-form upper sieve can be union-bounded
without loss over all \(s\le N^\delta\).
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Exact certificate:] For a given \(s\), there are \(O(s)\) possible parent
coefficients \(b\), while the reflected progression has only \(O(t/s)\)
indices.  These factors cancel, leaving roughly one \(t/\log^2 t\) cost per
quotient band.  The present union bound therefore gives no polynomial range.
\item[What survives:] Fixed and sufficiently slowly growing \(S\) satisfying
(QS4).
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not spend another round merely optimising constants in
QS3 in hopes of reaching \(N^\delta\).

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-RDS-GEOMETRY-DENSITY-001}\label{fail:FAIL-RDS-GEOMETRY-DENSITY-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-RDS-GEOMETRY-DENSITY-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] v1.13 support-free continuation, 1 September 2026.
\item[Claim killed:] From canonical reflected geometry and
\(\operatorname{rad}(c_j)\mid d_j\) alone, one may infer a universal bound
\(|\mathrm{RDS}|\le t/8\).
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Exact certificate:] Take
\[
 N=4368,\quad x=2184,\quad p_0=2203,\quad
 h=19,\quad \operatorname{prevprime}(p_0)=2179,
 \quad G=24,\quad t=9.
\]
Thus \(h<G\), so the root is canonical.  The strict reflected block contains
\[
 j=3:\ d_j=13,\quad c_j=2197=13^3,
\]
and
\[
 j=8:\ d_j=3,\quad c_j=2187=3^7.
\]
Hence both indices satisfy
\(\operatorname{rad}(c_j)\mid d_j\), so
\(|\mathrm{RDS}|\ge2>9/8=t/8\).
\item[Scope warning:] This is a successful-world certificate:
\(m=N-p_0=2165=5\cdot433\) and the first-front state \(5\) is GOOD because
\(N-5=4363\) is prime.  Therefore the witness kills only a
\emph{geometry-only} density inference; it does not refute a stronger theorem
conditioned on a genuinely stopped canonical failed world.
\item[What survives:] \texttt{TS-REFLECTED-DEADSMOOTH-CEILING} is exact and
remains PROVED.  Any stronger failure-conditioned density bound requires
additional dynamic input, not the reflected geometry alone.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not infer a small universal RDS density from
powerful-number rarity or from finite empirical scarcity without using a
proved failure-conditioned mechanism.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-REFLECTION-ACTIVATION-001}\label{fail:FAIL-REFLECTION-ACTIVATION-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-REFLECTION-ACTIVATION-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Canonical bridge audit, 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] Canonical \(h<G\) alone forces at least one reflected index
\(j\) with \(a_j=N-c_j\) an active prime, hence an actual reflected CRD row.
\item[Original motivation:] The Reflection Gate Lemma makes every \(c_j\)
composite, and compositeness was read as if it also produced a parent row.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] \(N=242\), \(x=121\), \(p_0=127\),
previous prime \(113\), so \(h=6<G=14\).
\item[Exact certificate:] The two internal offsets give
\((c_1,a_1)=(125,117)\) and \((c_2,a_2)=(123,119)\), with
\(125=5^3\), \(117=3^2\cdot13\), \(123=3\cdot41\), \(119=7\cdot17\).  Both
reflections are composite, so no reflected row exists at all.  Verified
exactly.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] The gate was treated as a state
activation statement.
\item[Why the argument failed:] \texttt{ARS-REFLECTION-GATE} is an
\emph{if and only if}: the factorisation of \(c_j\) is a CRD row precisely
when \(a_j\) is an active prime, and nothing in \(h<G\) supplies that.
\item[What survives:] Compositeness of every \(c_j\), and the classification
\texttt{C0b-RD} which does not require any \(a_j\) to be prime.
\item[Safe weaker version:] State separately \emph{boundary} \(\to\)
\emph{active reflected state} as an open implication.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
\texttt{ARS-REFLECTION-GATE}; target BIA remains \OPENs.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not hide a missing activation step under the word
``reflection''.
\item[Related current target:] \(T_I\), \(P1^{\rm br}\).
\item[Domain note:] \(N=242\) is not a failed canonical instance, so it does
not refute BIA itself; it refutes any proof of BIA that uses only selector
geometry before invoking failure.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-REUSE-DOUBLE-CHARGE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-REUSE-DOUBLE-CHARGE-001}

\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-REUSE-DOUBLE-CHARGE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] v1.21 depletion audit, 1 September 2026.
\item[Claim:] If one nonpositive clean round forces a rooted reuse payment
$J_*\mid J_R$, then running clean selection again automatically forces a new,
disjoint payment and therefore decreases the remaining rooted budget.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Exact logical obstruction:] The second ``round'' may select the identical
family or may use complements sharing exactly the same rooted negative labels.
Then the same set $B_-$ and the same factor $J_*$ are being observed again.
Nothing implies $J_*^2\mid J_R$ or any decrease of a residual quotient.
\item[What survives:] If complete complement supports are pairwise disjoint
across rounds, then the negative rooted label sets are disjoint and the product
of the corresponding $J_i$ divides $J_R$.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
\texttt{G-MULTIROUND-EXTERNAL-SINGLE-CHARGE} and
\texttt{G-BAD-BASE-FORBIDDEN-SUPPORT-CLEAN-CONTINUATION}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Never infer depletion from repeated invocation of a
selector alone.  First prove cross-round support freshness or enter the explicit
support-saturation alternative.
\item[Related current target:] K1, P1BR, TF renewal termination.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-ROOTED-AMBIENT-001}\label{fail:FAIL-ROOTED-AMBIENT-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-ROOTED-AMBIENT-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Canonical bridge audit, 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] After adjoining a selected set \(\mathscr P\) of external
active parents, the old rooted lock still controls the enlarged system, so
\(T_R,U_R,J_R\) bound the promoted valuation mass.
\item[Original motivation:] The rooted congruence was the strongest
available global identity and was reused outside its domain.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural, by
\texttt{G-MULTISOURCE-LOCK}.
\item[Exact certificate:] For child-closed \(S\),
\(T_S\equiv(-1)^{|S|}\prod_{d\in D_S^{\rm src}}d\pmod N\).  Adjoining
\(\mathscr P\) and re-closing changes the source set from \(\{p_0\}\) to a
set containing \(\mathscr P\), so the right-hand side changes.  A large
ambient \(J\) is consistent with a large source product.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] A one-source identity was applied to
a multi-source system.
\item[Why the argument failed:] The lock is an identity \emph{about the
sources}, not a bound on the collision channel.
\item[What survives:] The exact multi-source congruence itself, and the
promotion inequality
\(\log(J_{R\cup\mathscr P}/J_R)\le K_\times(R,\mathscr P)+K(\mathscr P)\).
\item[Safe weaker version:] Any future capacity theorem must book the new
sources explicitly.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
\texttt{G-MULTISOURCE-LOCK}, \texttt{G-AMBIENT-PROMOTION}, target K1.
\item[Do not repeat:] Never carry a rooted bound across a change of source
set.
\item[Related current target:] K1, W1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-ROUTING-INDIFFERENCE-SCOPE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-ROUTING-INDIFFERENCE-SCOPE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-ROUTING-INDIFFERENCE-SCOPE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.1, Phase 0A.
\item[Claim:] vNEXT4 (RI1),
\(\texttt{TD-UNIVERSAL-ROUTING}\not\Rightarrow\texttt{P1BR}\).
\item[Original motivation:] Under routing every fresh seed returns, and the
return branch was shown to move no recorded quantity of \(R\).
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.  The theorem survives; its reading does not.
\item[Exact certificate:] The proof enumerates the \emph{present} functionals
\(\kappa_R,\Gamma_N(R),\eta(R),J_R,U_R,T_R,\gamma,C,H,\tau,Q\) and observes
that each is a function of the set \(R\), which does not change when a closure
returns to it.  That establishes a non-implication \emph{through those
functionals}.  It says nothing about a theorem that uses the arithmetic of the
return path --- the actual integers \(N-p\) along it, the congruences placing a
returning seed inside \(R\), or \(\gcd(N-p,N-u)\mid p-u\).  Quantifying over
all future theorems was never proved and cannot be proved this way.
\item[What survives:] Theory Core,
\texttt{G-ROUTING-INDIFFERENCE-SCOPED}: routing alone together with the
currently recorded CRD ledgers does not close P1BR.
\item[Safe weaker version:] the scoped form above, which is what is used.
\item[Do not repeat:] Loss-control rule (LR5) is amended: routing may not be
cited as a \emph{sufficient} route to P1BR through the recorded ledgers; it
remains admissible as an \emph{ingredient} of an additive argument.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{P1BR-ADDITIVE-COUPLING},
\texttt{TD-UNIVERSAL-ROUTING}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-ROUTING-RESCUES-P1BR-001}\label{fail:FAIL-ROUTING-RESCUES-P1BR-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-ROUTING-RESCUES-P1BR-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4, Phase 6.
\item[Claim:] That proving \texttt{TD-UNIVERSAL-ROUTING} --- every BAD
child-closed closure meets \(R\) --- would remove the obstruction at
\texttt{P1BR-POSITIVE-ROUND-CONSEQUENCE}, since it removes the disjoint-packet
configuration ``without requiring any new theory''.
\item[Original motivation:] vNEXT3.1 recorded, correctly, that routing removes
the disjoint-packet discussion, the recorded-ledger bridge theorem and the
CRD-2 question.  It was natural to expect that it also unblocked the positive
round.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.  The routing statement itself is untouched and remains
\OPENs; only its claimed relevance to P1BR is rejected.
\item[Exact certificate:] Under routing, \(B_{\rm ext}=\varnothing\) and every
fresh seed of a positive round returns.  A returning seed \(r\) produces the
enlarged world \(R'=R\cup R_N(r)\), but \(\kappa_R\), \(\Gamma_N(R)\),
\(\eta(R)\), \(J_R\), \(U_R\), \(T_R\), \(\gamma\), \(|R|\), \(C\), \(H\),
\(\tau\), \(Q\) are functions of the set \(R\) alone and do not move; and the
capacity bounds (FC7)--(FC10) do not transfer to \(R'\), whose source set is
not a single upper-half root with composite complement.  See Theory Core,
\texttt{G-RETURN-BRANCH-NO-CANONICAL-CHARGE} and
\texttt{G-ROUTING-INDIFFERENCE}, (RI1).
\item[Second, independent certificate:] The witness family of
\texttt{G-POSITIVE-ROUND-LEDGER-INDEPENDENCE} is routing-compatible --- every
fresh state's closure meets \(R_n\) --- and still has \(\eta(R_n)\) unbounded
at fixed round datum.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Confusing ``the seed reaches \(R\)''
with ``\(R\) is charged''.  Reaching a fixed set does not alter any functional
of that set.
\item[What survives:] Routing remains the right question for the bridge, the
disjoint-packet configuration and the CRD-2 question, and the restricted form
\texttt{TD-POSITIVE-ROUND-ROUTING} is recorded in the Core.
\item[Do not repeat:] Loss-control rule (LR5): \texttt{TD-UNIVERSAL-ROUTING}
may not be cited as a \emph{sufficient} route to P1BR through the recorded
ledgers.  Scope-corrected at vNEXT4.1: see
\texttt{FAIL-ROUTING-INDIFFERENCE-SCOPE-001}; routing remains admissible as an
ingredient of an additive argument.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{P1BR-ADDITIVE-COUPLING},
\texttt{TD-UNIVERSAL-ROUTING}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-SATURATION-DOUBLE-CHARGE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-SATURATION-DOUBLE-CHARGE-001}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-SEALED-MULTISOURCE-LOCK-001}\label{fail:FAIL-SEALED-MULTISOURCE-LOCK-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-SEALED-MULTISOURCE-LOCK-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] v1.6 sealed-source continuation, 1 September 2026.
\item[Claim:] If many external upper-half bad parents have all children inside
the canonical failed world \(R\), adjoining them and applying
\texttt{G-MULTISOURCE-LOCK} yields a new modular obstruction stronger than the
rooted lock.
\item[Original motivation:] The sealed branch creates genuine new sources,
and the multi-source congruence explicitly records the source product.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural; the proposed new
congruence reduces identically to the old one.
\item[Exact certificate:] Let \(\mathscr P\) be finite, upper-half,
external and bad with \(\Gamma_N(\mathscr P)\subseteq R\), and put
\(S=R\cup\mathscr P\).  Then
\[
 \Src(S)=\{p_0\}\dot\cup\mathscr P,
 \qquad
 T_S=T_R\prod_{p\in\mathscr P}(N-p).
\]
The multi-source lock reads
\[
 T_R\prod_{p\in\mathscr P}(N-p)
 \equiv(-1)^{|R|+|\mathscr P|}p_0
       \prod_{p\in\mathscr P}p\pmod N.
\]
Using \(N-p\equiv-p\pmod N\) and cancelling the active labels
\(p\), which are units modulo \(N\), leaves exactly
\[
 T_R\equiv(-1)^{|R|}p_0\pmod N,
\]
the original \texttt{G-ROOT-LOCK} congruence.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] A larger source set was assumed to
create new modular information merely because the source product changed.
\item[Why the argument failed:] The row factors contributed by the new sealed
sources are congruent to the negatives of those same source labels, so their
entire modular contribution cancels.
\item[What survives:] \texttt{G-SEALED-SOURCE-LOCK-REDUCTION} is an exact
\PROVEDs\ structural statement.  The sealed branch remains potentially useful
through population size, valuation/reuse overload, or deeper topology, but
not through the source-lock congruence alone.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Use the sealed-source lift as bookkeeping only;
seek a noncongruential invariant for the new sources.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core v1.6,
\texttt{G-SEALED-SOURCE-LOCK-REDUCTION}; see also the four-ary
sign-overload disposition theorem in the Core.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not count new sealed sources as new modular
constraints without simplifying the multi-source congruence first.
\item[Related current target:] sealed-source branch, P1BR, K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-SELECTOR-CLOSES-CASCADE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-SELECTOR-CLOSES-CASCADE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-SELECTOR-CLOSES-CASCADE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT3, Phase 4.
\item[Claim:] Once \texttt{G-BAD-BASE-SQUAREFREE-POLYLOG-EXTENSION} is proved,
the (FC10) clean-round route yields a contradiction.
\item[Original motivation:] The selector was the last analytic blocker on that
route.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.  The selector is \PROVEDs; the inference is not.
\item[Exact certificate:] The selector supplies at most one clean row per
designated base, and the bases lie in \([3,(\log N)^A]\), so
\(\sum_iM_i\log z_i\ll(\log N)^A\log N\).  (FC10) forces a positive signed
round only once \(\sum_iM_i\log z_i\ge\gamma\log(25N^2/18)\), i.e.\ once
\(\gamma\lesssim(\log N)^A\).  The cascade therefore closes exactly on the
subdomain \(\gamma\le(\log N)^A\) and on no larger one by this route.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Removing an analytic obstruction was
read as closing the chain; the counting obstruction downstream is untouched.
\item[What survives:] \texttt{G-CASCADE-GAMMA-TERMINUS}, which states the
subdomain exactly, and the selector itself.
\item[Safe weaker version:] ``Contradiction on \(\gamma\le(\log N)^A\).''
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
the retired \texttt{G-CASCADE-GAMMA-TERMINUS}, whose proof body is kept at
Subsection~\textup{[\,fail:cascade-body\,]} of this document and no longer in the Core.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not announce a cascade closure without counting the
number of rounds the selector actually supplies against the capacity it must
exhaust.
\item[Related current target:] \(\gamma\), K1, X1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-SIMPLE-STATE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-SIMPLE-STATE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-SIMPLE-STATE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] v0.1 foundations review.
\item[Claim:] The simple directed support graph on \(\mathcal A_N\) is a
faithful presentation of the CRD dynamics.
\item[Original motivation:] Reachability questions are graph questions.
\item[Status:] \SUPERSEDEDs.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Structural.
\item[Exact certificate:] The support graph loses the valuations
\(\nu_N(p,q)=v_q(N-p)\), hence the prime-power layers
\(\mu_{\ell,k}\), hence the collision and cut functionals; and it carries no
record of ambient external parents.  \texttt{G-TUJ},
\texttt{G-FULLQ-LEDGER}, \texttt{G-COLLISION-CUT} and
\texttt{G-AMBIENT-PROMOTION} are all invisible to it.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Edge existence was taken for the
whole structure.
\item[Why the argument failed:] \(T=UJ\), residual production, prime-power
collision and ambient promotion all depend on valuations, not on the mere
existence of an edge.
\item[What survives:] Graph-level facts: closure, terminal SCC, source
deletion.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Use the support graph only for reachability
statements.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, the rooted ambient
valuation-incidence object
\(\mathfrak C_N=(N,\mathcal A_N,p_0,\nu_N)\).
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not state a valuation theorem in graph language.
\item[Related current target:] L1, K1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}
