\begin{faillog}{FAIL-TAGGED-P3-RESIDUE-FORCES-RETURN-001}\label{fail:FAIL-TAGGED-P3-RESIDUE-FORCES-RETURN-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-TAGGED-P3-RESIDUE-FORCES-RETURN-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.21.
\item[Killed inference:] Knowing $b\bmod q$ together with
$\Omega(b)\le3$ forces some sibling $r\mid b$ to satisfy
$r\equiv N\pmod q$.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ for every prime $q\ge5$.
\item[Exact certificate:] With
$G=(\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z)^\times$ and $a=N\bmod q$,
\[
 \boxed{(G\setminus\{a\})^2=G.}
\]
Thus two non-return sibling residues already realise every possible product
residue.
\item[Exceptional case:] $q=3$ is different.  If $N\equiv2\pmod3$ and
$b\equiv2\pmod3$, at least one sibling returns to $3$.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-TD-NAIVE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-TD-NAIVE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-TD-NAIVE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Interrupted \(T_D\) branch round, 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] Every composite \(D\)-carrier \(a_j\) has an active prime
factor, so every \(\mathcal D\) index produces an actual CRD state.
\item[Original motivation:] Fresh carriers do produce active states, and the
smooth case was assumed to differ only quantitatively.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] \(N=1862,\ r=1733,\ j=2\).
\item[Exact certificate:] \(m=N-r=129\) and
\(a_j=m+2j=133=7\cdot19\), while \(7\mid1862\) and \(19\mid1862\).  Both
prime factors of the carrier divide \(N\), so neither is active and
\(a_j\) contributes no CRD row.  The reflected partner is
\(c_j=1729=7\cdot13\cdot19\).  Verified exactly.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] Compositeness of the carrier was
confused with activity of its factors.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Activity is a condition on \(N\), not on
\(a_j\); a carrier can be built entirely from primes dividing \(N\).
\item[What survives:] The smooth/fresh split of \texttt{TD-CARRIER-SPLIT}
covers this instance instead of hiding it: a \emph{fresh} carrier, that is
one with \(\PFp(a_j)\ge h\), does give an active prime state
\(s_j<N/6\) by strict reflected-block nonreuse.  The exception lives in
\(\mathcal D_{\rm sm}\).
\item[Safe weaker version:] Assert activity only for
\(j\in\mathcal D_{\rm fr}\).
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, \texttt{TD-CARRIER-SPLIT} and
\texttt{C-STRICT-NONREUSE}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Never promote ``composite'' to ``has an active
factor''.
\item[Related current target:] \(T_D\), \(P1^{\rm br}\).
\item[Domain note:] \(r=1733\) is a \emph{noncanonical} upper root; the
canonical selector for \(N=1862\) is \(p_0=937\).  The certificate is an
exact arithmetic fact and is domain-independent, but it must not be quoted
as a canonical-world witness.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-TD-SMOOTH-INACTIVE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-TD-SMOOTH-INACTIVE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-TD-SMOOTH-INACTIVE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Phase-3 \(T_D\) second-layer attack, 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] The canonical geometry alone --- \(p_0\) canonical, \(h<G\),
\(a_j=m+2j\) odd composite, \(c_j\) composite --- forces a smooth reflected
carrier to transport some cost: an active state, a prime-power layer, or a
source term.
\item[Original motivation:] \texttt{TD-CARRIER-SPLIT} gives
\(\Omega(a_j)>\log m/\log h\), a large factorisation mass, and mass was assumed
to be transportable.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ as a proof route resting on the canonical geometry.  It
is \emph{not} a refutation of any statement conditioned on canonical failure;
see the domain note below.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] \(N=168\), \(x=84\), \(p_0=89\),
\(h=5<G=6\), \(m=79\), \(t=2\), \(j=1\).  Smallest instance with \emph{composite}
complement, hence with a genuine first front: \(N=2684\), \(p_0=1361\),
\(h=19<G=34\), \(m=1323=3^3\cdot7^2\), \(j=4\), \(a_4=1331=11^3\),
\(c_4=1353=3\cdot11\cdot41\), \(11\mid2684\).
\item[Exact certificate:] \(a_1=m+2=81=3^4\) and \(c_1=N-a_1=87=3\cdot29\).
Since \(3\mid168\), the only prime of \(a_1\) divides \(N\), so
\(3\notin\mathcal A_N\).  The carrier therefore contributes no active state, no
prime-power layer of the CRD system, and no source.  Its whole factorisation
mass \(\Omega(a_1)=4\) is inert.  Verified exactly.
\item[Domain note --- read before transferring this witness:] all six known
instances are \emph{successful} worlds.  At \(N=168\) and \(N=492\) the
complement \(m\) is prime, so \(p_0\) is GOOD at depth zero and
\(R=\varnothing\); at \(N=2684\), \(4380\), \(4386\), \(6260\) the complement is
composite but the traversal succeeds deeper.  In none of them is \(R\) a failed
world, so in none of them is the index \(j\) shown to lie in \(\mathcal D\).
By \texttt{PROHIB-DOMAIN-TRANSFER} this witness therefore kills only proofs that
use the canonical geometry alone; the failure-conditioned form of the claim is
untouched and remains open.  This is the same shape of kill as
\texttt{FAIL-TF-LOCAL-SCOPE-001}.
\item[Further instances:] \((N,p_0,j,a_j)=(492,251,1,3^5)\),
\((4380,2203,5,3^7)\), \((4386,2203,2,3^7)\), \((6260,3137,1,5^5)\).  Over
canonical \(N<1.2\cdot10^5\), \(22.24\%\) of composite reflected carriers have at
least one prime factor dividing \(N\).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] \(\Omega\)-mass of \(a_j\) was identified
with CRD mass.  The two live in different objects: \(a_j\) is not a row, and its
prime factors need not be states.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Activity is a condition relative to \(N\).  A
carrier assembled from primes dividing \(N\) is invisible to the CRD system.
\item[Structural note:] such a carrier is necessarily \emph{smooth}.  If
\(\ell\mid a_j\) and \(\ell\mid N\) then \(\ell\mid N-a_j=c_j\), so \(\ell\)
divides two distinct members of the strict reflected block and
\texttt{C-STRICT-NONREUSE} forces \(\ell<h\).  The fresh branch is therefore
immune, which is exactly the content of \texttt{TD-CARRIER-SPLIT}: only
\(\mathcal D_{\rm sm}\) can be inert.
\item[What survives:] The smooth branch is bounded in \emph{count} rather than
transported in \emph{mass}.  \texttt{TD-SMOOTH-CEILING} gives
\(|\mathcal D_{\rm sm}|\le\sigma_N(h)\) unconditionally, and that ceiling is what
the second-layer trichotomy consumes.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Never assert that a smooth carrier produces a state.
Use only its cardinality, via the ceiling.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, \texttt{TD-SMOOTH-CEILING} and
\texttt{TD-SECOND-LAYER}.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not attempt to transport smooth carrier mass to actual
layers.  That direction is closed by this certificate; the productive direction
is the ceiling.
\item[Relation to \texttt{FAIL-TD-NAIVE-001}:] complementary, not stronger.
\texttt{FAIL-TD-NAIVE-001} uses a noncanonical root, \((N,r)=(1862,1733)\) with
canonical selector \(937\), and kills ``every composite carrier has an active
factor''.  This entry uses canonical roots with \(h<G\) and kills the same claim
for any proof resting on that geometry, while strengthening the configuration
from ``some prime factor is inactive'' to ``the carrier is wholly inert''.
Neither entry reaches the canonical \emph{failed} domain, because no canonical
failed world is known.
\item[Related current target:] \(T_D\), \(P1^{\rm br}\).
\item[Exact classification (Phase-3 continuation):] the failure mode is now
completely understood.  By \texttt{TD-CARRIER-DICHOTOMY}, a carrier produces no
active state \emph{precisely} when \(\operatorname{rad}(a_j)\mid h-2j\).  All six
instances above are of that kind, and each realises the normal form
\(x=q^{e}+d\): \(84=3^4+3\), \(246=3^5+3\), \(1342=11^3+11\), \(2190=3^7+3\),
\(2193=3^7+6\), \(3130=5^5+5\).  The class is bounded by
\texttt{TD-DEADSMOOTH-CEILING} and is empty whenever no prime below \(h\)
divides \(x\) --- \(48.0\%\) of canonical instances with \(N<3\cdot10^5\).
Across that whole range only \(19\) dead-smooth carriers exist among
\(514\,447\), and no \(N\) carries two.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-TF-LOCAL-SCOPE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-TF-LOCAL-SCOPE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-TF-LOCAL-SCOPE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Interrupted \(T_D\) branch round, hostile scope
witness, 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] A fresh reflected state \(\ell_j\), certified locally as
\(\mathcal F\)-class together with \(h<G\), routes to \(\Good_N\) or into
\(R\).
\item[Original motivation:] The recorded census showed \(\mathcal F\) to be
empirically rigid, and the local certificate looked self-sufficient.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] \(N=128,\ p_0=67,\ j=1,\ c_1=65,\
\ell=13\).
\item[Exact certificate:] \(x=64\), \(p_0=67\), previous prime \(61\), so
\(h=3<G=6\); \(t=1\) and \(c_1=65=5\cdot13\) with
\(\PFp(c_1)=13\ge h\), so the local \(\mathcal F\) certificate holds.
The state \(13\) is active and not GOOD, since \(128-13=115=5\cdot23\), and
its stopped traversal fails with the separate closed world
\(\{3,5,7,11,13,23,29,41\}\).  Verified exactly.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] The certificate was evaluated without
the hypothesis that defines \(R\).
\item[Why the argument failed:] Here \(128-67=61\) is prime, so \(p_0\)
\emph{succeeds} at depth zero and \(R=R_N(p_0)=\varnothing\).  The condition
\(\PF(c_j)\cap R=\varnothing\) is satisfied vacuously.  The instance is a
\emph{successful world}, and \(R\) is not even defined as a failed world.
\item[What survives:] The canonical-failure-conditioned form of TF is
untouched.  What is killed is every proof of it that uses only the local
\(\mathcal F\) certificate together with \(h<G\).
\item[Safe weaker version:] Always carry the failure hypothesis into the
\(\mathcal F\) certificate; never evaluate \(\mathcal I,\mathcal D,\mathcal
S,\mathcal F\) at a root that succeeds.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, target TF.
\item[Do not repeat:] A vacuous \(R\) is not an empty support intersection
in the intended sense.
\item[Related current target:] TF, \(T_D\).
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-TWOVARIABLE-FULL-LEVEL-001}\label{fail:FAIL-TWOVARIABLE-FULL-LEVEL-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-TWOVARIABLE-FULL-LEVEL-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4.12.
\item[Claim:] The exact local density
\((2p-1)/p^2=2/p-1/p^2\) for the polynomial pair
\(q(N-kq^2)\) permits an elementary sieve level equal to a fixed power of
\(N\).
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Exact certificate:] The coefficient coordinate has length only
\[
 K=N/h^2.
\]
The elementary remainder term therefore restricts the second logarithmic
saving to \(\log K\), not \(\log N\).
\item[Do not repeat:] A local dimension-two identity is not a distribution
level theorem.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-UNIQUE-FRESH-TARGETS-MAY-FUNNEL-INTO-O(n)-PARENTS-001}\label{fail:FAIL-UNIQUE-FRESH-TARGETS-MAY-FUNNEL-INTO-On-PARENTS-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-UNIQUE-FRESH-TARGETS-MAY-FUNNEL-INTO-O(n)-PARENTS-001.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ on the high layer extracted in v4.40.
\item[Killed inference:] even after extracting linearly many fresh load-one
targets, they may all be fed by $o(n)$ parent rows.
\item[Certificate:] after removing targets below $n/(\log N)^2$, one parent can
feed at most three surviving targets because their product divides one
complement $<N$.  Therefore the parent population is at least
$(1/27-o(1))n$, and a greedy matching gives at least $(1/63-o(1))n$
vertex-disjoint parent--target edges.
\item[What survives:] the cofactor supports of those matched rows remain
uncontrolled.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-UNIQUE-MISSING-DATUM-001}\label{fail:FAIL-UNIQUE-MISSING-DATUM-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-UNIQUE-MISSING-DATUM-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT3.1, Phase-5 reclassification.
\item[Claim:] The vNEXT3 information-loss certificate named ``a share of the
ambient valuation tensor'' as \emph{the exact datum missing} for a coupling.
\item[Original motivation:] It is the most natural non-additive quantity in
sight.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Exact certificate:] What is proved is that all recorded packet
functionals factor on disjoint child-closed unions, hence cannot express
competition for an \(R\)-only capacity.  What is \emph{not} proved is that
ambient tensor occupancy is the unique repair, that no other non-additive
functional works, or that a CRD-2 is necessary.  No uniqueness argument was
given, and none is available.
\item[What survives:] The diagnosis, reclassified as
\textsf{FRONTIER CERTIFICATE / INFORMATION-LOSS DIAGNOSIS}, together with four
candidates recorded as \textsf{CONJECTURAL THEORY-DESIGN DIRECTIONS}: ambient
tensor occupancy, cofactor provenance, parent-pair correlations, non-additive
resource ownership.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not call a design hypothesis an ``exact missing
datum'' without a uniqueness proof.
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{TD-UNIVERSAL-ROUTING}, CRD-2 question.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-UNIT-COMPLEMENT-001}\label{fail:FAIL-UNIT-COMPLEMENT-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-UNIT-COMPLEMENT-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] Domain audit, frozen 31 August 2026.
\item[Claim:] Every failed active root has composite complement.
\item[Original motivation:] Failure has no prime-complement success, so the
complement was informally treated as composite.
\item[Status:] \KILLED.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] \(N=20, r=19\).
\item[Exact certificate:] \(19\in\mathcal A_{20}\), \(20-19=1\), and
\(1\notin\PP\).  The row has no prime children, hence the stopped traversal
fails, although the complement is not composite.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] The implication ``nonprime
\(\Rightarrow\) composite'' silently assumed the complement exceeds one.
\item[Why the argument failed:] The unit row was omitted from the domain.
\item[What survives:] If \(N-r>1\) and \(r\) is not GOOD, then \(N-r\) is
composite.
\item[Safe weaker version:] State the composite-complement hypothesis
explicitly whenever \(Q=\PF(N-r)\) or a root ledger is used.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core, rooted algorithm and Theorems
G-FULLQ-LEDGER/G-FULLQ-PRODUCTION on their stated domains.
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not infer compositeness from failure before
checking the unit row.
\item[Related current target:] C0a and every generic failed-root lemma.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-UNIVERSAL-BRIDGE-IMPOSSIBILITY-001}\label{fail:FAIL-UNIVERSAL-BRIDGE-IMPOSSIBILITY-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-UNIVERSAL-BRIDGE-IMPOSSIBILITY-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT3.1, Phase-4 scope correction.
\item[Claim:] \texttt{G-BRIDGE-ROUTING-EQUIVALENCE} of vNEXT3, read as: no
coupling of disjoint packets is possible at all.
\item[Original motivation:] (OD1)--(OD4) really do make every recorded
functional additive, which felt exhaustive.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.  The mathematics is correct; the quantifier was too
large.
\item[Exact certificate:] (OD1)--(OD4) quantify over the recorded ledger
\(T,J,U_{\bullet},\eta,\nu,K,\Src\).  They say nothing about an arbitrary
functional \(\Psi_N(R,U)\), which need not be a disjoint-union homomorphism.
Candidates not excluded: ambient valuation-tensor occupancy, parent or cofactor
correlations, residue geometry, shared ambient prime supply, non-additive
resource ownership.
\item[What survives:] \texttt{G-RECORDED-LEDGER-BRIDGE-ROUTING}: no bridge
built \emph{solely from the recorded disjoint-union-homomorphic ledgers} can
charge \(\eta(U)\) against an \(R\)-only capacity, and any such bridge requires
\(U\cap R\ne\varnothing\).
\item[Do not repeat:] Do not promote ``every functional we have recorded'' to
``every functional''.
\item[Related current target:] TD/TF routing,
\texttt{TD-UNIVERSAL-ROUTING}.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-UPPERHALF-SCOPE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-UPPERHALF-SCOPE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-UPPERHALF-SCOPE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] v0.1 hostile mathematical audit \S3.
\item[Claim:] Upper-half source compression applies to a failed canonical
world, so every active upper-half prime is a source of the bad graph.
\item[Original motivation:] Both settings are called ``failure''.
\item[Status:] \SCOPECORR.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] Hypothesis mismatch; no finite
witness is required.
\item[Exact certificate:] The source theorem assumes
\(\Good_N=\varnothing\), that is, that \(N\) is a Goldbach counterexample.
Only then do stopped and raw reachability coincide and every active
\(N/2<p<N\) become a source.  Canonical \(p_0\)-failure asserts nothing
about other roots: the recorded corpus contains many failed worlds for
arbitrary roots at values of \(N\) that have Goldbach representations.
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] The global hypothesis was imported
into the local one.
\item[Why the argument failed:] Using a theorem whose hypothesis is global
Goldbach failure in order to contradict \(p_0\)-failure assumes what is to
be proved for every other root.
\item[What survives:] \texttt{ARS-UPPERHALF-COMPRESSION} on its own domain,
and the direct-Goldbach-failure DAG in which it is legitimate.
\item[Safe weaker version:] Keep two separate DAGs --- universal
\(p_0\)-success, and direct contradiction under global failure --- and never
move a statement between them without annotation.
\item[Current replacement:] Theory Core,
\texttt{ARS-UPPERHALF-COMPRESSION} with its prohibition, and the exact
Goldbach boundary section.
\item[Do not repeat:] \(\text{PROVED}\neq\text{COMPUTATION}\neq\text{OPEN}
\neq\text{REJECTED}\), and failure of the canonical traversal is not global
Goldbach failure.
\item[Related current target:] X1.
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

\]
for a linear family of distinct vertical bases, and the weighted theorem gives

 V_{\rm blk}\gg t\log h

\]

\begin{faillog}{FAIL-WORLD-SIZE-NAIVE-001}\label{fail:FAIL-WORLD-SIZE-NAIVE-001}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.2em,style=nextline]
\item[FAIL-ID:] FAIL-WORLD-SIZE-NAIVE-001.
\item[Date / iteration:] vNEXT4, Phase 1b.
\item[Claim:] For a failed world \(R\) with composite complement,
\(|R|\le\eta(R)+1\), on the ground that every row satisfies
\(\omega(N-u)\ge2\) and that
\(\sum_{u\in R}\omega(N-u)=\eta(R)+|R|-1\).
\item[Original motivation:] Every state of a failed world is BAD, so its
complement is composite; a composite number ``has at least two prime
factors''.
\item[Status:] \KILLED\ as stated.
\item[Minimal / strong counterexample:] \(N=2200\), root \(r_\ast=1471\),
\[
 R=\{3,13,1471\},\qquad
 N-1471=729=3^6,\quad N-3=2197=13^3,\quad N-13=2187=3^7 .
\]
Here \(\Gamma_N(R)=\{3,13\}=R\setminus\{r_\ast\}\), \(\kappa_R(3)=2\),
\(\kappa_R(13)=1\), so \(\eta(R)=1\) while \(|R|=3>\eta(R)+1=2\).
\item[Failed hypothesis or mechanism:] A composite number has at least two
prime factors \emph{counted with multiplicity}; it need not have two
\emph{distinct} ones.  Every row of this world is a prime power, so
\(\omega=1\) on all three.
\item[Why the argument failed:] \(\kappa\) is layer-one incidence and therefore
sees \(\omega\), not \(\Omega\).  The step that requires \(\omega\ge2\) is the
only place where badness was used, and badness gives \(\Omega\ge2\).
\item[What survives:] The corrected count
\(|R|\le\eta(R)+1+2a_0+a_1\) with \(a_0\le1\) and
\(a_1\le\gamma(\lfloor\log_2N\rfloor-1)\), hence \(|R|<4\gamma\log N\) under the
(FC9) hypotheses: Theory Core, \texttt{G-CANONICAL-WORLD-SIZE-CAP}, (WS1)--(WS3).
Zero violations over the recorded \(301\) worlds.
\item[Safe weaker version:] The corrected form above; nothing weaker is needed.
\item[Do not repeat:] Whenever a count over the rows of a failed world uses
\(\omega(N-u)\ge2\), the prime-power rows must be excluded explicitly.  Recorded
as loss-control rule (LR6).
\item[Related current target:] \texttt{P1BR-ADDITIVE-COUPLING}, \(\gamma\).
\end{description}
\end{faillog}

edges/valuations but does not control every unprescribed factor of every
expanded row. The blanket bounded-depth complete-BFS no-go is therefore not
established. Exact witness: $N=92$, $p_0=47$ has a selected BAD cycle
$5\to29\to7\to5$ but succeeds at depth $1$ via $3$ because $92-3=89$ is
prime. \textbf{Survives:} compatible partial-transcript programming.
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{ENVELOPE-ESCAPE-AUTOMATIC-ITERATION-20260905}\label{fail:ENVELOPE-ESCAPE-AUTOMATIC-ITERATION-20260905}
\textbf{Status.} \KILLED\ as an inference. The proved $h=1$ envelope-escape
theorem can force new primes $>y$ at depth $2$, but after the envelope grows
the threshold $F_2(y)$ changes and need not remain below the same $N$.
Automatic repeated escape is not justified. \textbf{Survives:} the one-step
and all-first-branch escape theorems under their explicit size hypotheses.
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{AUTOMATIC-THIRD-GENERATION-SIEVE-SWITCH-20260906}\label{fail:AUTOMATIC-THIRD-GENERATION-SIEVE-SWITCH-20260906}
\textbf{Status.} \KILLED\ as an inference. Radius-two upper-bound sieve
estimates do not automatically iterate to a complete third generation: the
number and arithmetic shape of residual forms change, and complete cofactors
must be retained. No proved radius-two theorem is refuted.
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{SUCCESS-PRODUCT-BARRIER-TO-CLOSED-CORE-HEIGHT-20260906B}\label{fail:SUCCESS-PRODUCT-BARRIER-TO-CLOSED-CORE-HEIGHT-20260906B}
\textbf{Status.} \KILLED\ as an inference. Label/cofactor product barriers
quantify over successful paths. A completely closed BAD core contains no such
path, so the successful-path theorem is vacuous there and cannot be combined
with the closed-support height bound to obtain a contradiction.
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{PRIME-LIFT-PRIMALITY-FORCES-SUCCESS-20260907}\label{fail:PRIME-LIFT-PRIMALITY-FORCES-SUCCESS-20260907}
\textbf{Status.} \KILLED. Prime lift primality alone does not force BFS
success. Exact counterexample: $(N,d,R)=(1862,7,1597)$, where the full BFS
from inactive root $7$ and from prime lift $1597$ are conjugate and both fail
with a complete closed active support certificate. \textbf{Survives:}
PRIME-LIFT-FULL-BFS-CONJUGACY, and the special unresolved $d=2$/$h=1$ case.
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{LOW-GAP-FIVE-LABEL-OVERGENERALIZATION-20260907C}\label{fail:LOW-GAP-FIVE-LABEL-OVERGENERALIZATION-20260907C}
\textbf{Status.} \KILLED\ by exact counterexample. At
$N=44670$, $r=22469=p_{12}$, $m=149^2$, $h=134<149$, the complete BAD
frontiers through depth $2$ discover exactly four nonroot labels by depth $3$:
$\{149,211,23,1933\}$. Both depth-$3$ endpoints are GOOD. The proved universal
lower bound THREE survives; FOUR remains open in the stated low-gap domain.
\end{faillog}

\begin{faillog}{SUBGROUP-SEPARATION-OF-P0-AS-GENERAL-EXPLANATION-20260907C}\label{fail:SUBGROUP-SEPARATION-OF-P0-AS-GENERAL-EXPLANATION-20260907C}
\textbf{Status.} \KILLED\ as a general explanation. For five of the six
historical hosts, the subgroup of $(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^\times$ generated by
the maximal closed low BAD support is the entire unit group, so no character
trivial on that support can separate $p_0$. At $N=2200$ the subgroup is
proper, but membership is still not sufficient for failure. The elementary
necessary subgroup lemma survives as an exclusion test when a verified full
BAD envelope is available.
\end{faillog}

\chapter{Research Agenda}\label{ch:agenda}
% =====================================================================

\section{How to choose what to work on}\label{sec:agenda}

\begin{summarybox}
Three rules for triage, in order of importance.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Check complete support first.} A finite \emph{selected}
transcript can be programmed, but the old blanket theorem about complete
bounded-depth BFS was scope-corrected (Corollary~\ref{cor:wall}). If an
argument constrains only chosen divisibilities while ignoring residual
cofactors, it cannot prove full failure or success. A complete-frontier theorem
is still admissible, but it must control every factor of every expanded row.
\item \textbf{Check the functional.} If the argument proves a lower bound in
one functional and consumes it in another, it is the P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$/K1
error. Write down both functionals explicitly \emph{before} starting.
\item \textbf{Check the scope class.} If the argument uses a class-B lemma to
prove a class-A statement, it proves nothing about $p_0$. If it uses a class-D
hypothesis under canonical failure, it is invalid.
\end{enumerate}
\end{summarybox}


\begin{summarybox}
\textbf{2026-09-07C agenda override.} The tier table below is retained as the
historical v4.81 agenda. For new work, start instead with the three targets in
\S\ref{sec:postDH-frontier}: (1) the exact $h=1$ full-BFS/root-$2$ closed-support
question, (2) the low-gap three-label Diophantine obstruction split, and (3)
the radius-three large-label/large-cofactor asymptotic region. The moving
closed-support problem is the global wall.
\end{summarybox}

\subsection{Tiered targets}

\begin{longtable}{p{0.06\textwidth}p{0.30\textwidth}p{0.58\textwidth}}
\toprule
Tier & Target & Why it is in this tier\\
\midrule

\bottomrule

1 & Prove or refute (N3):
$\sum_qd_R(q)\ge|R|+1$ (\S\ref{sec:euler}, Q8) &
Small, self-contained, elementary in appearance, and it repairs the part of the
corpus that used the false Euler normalisations. Zero counterexamples in

1 & Refute L1 by exhibiting $\nu(R)=O(1)$ with $J_R$ unbounded
(\S\ref{sec:L1}) &
A \emph{negative} result that would remove a whole family of capacity
arguments. The data already point this way. Cheap to test computationally.\\
1 & Extend the $\Blow$ census beyond $6\cdot10^{4}$ &
The coincidence of the three six-element lists (\S\ref{sec:comp-obs}) is
unexplained. A seventh $N$ would be the single most informative new datum in
the project.\\
2 & \tid{TS}: smooth branch to escape (\S\ref{sec:frontier-branch}) &
The branch with the largest quantitative margin and the most elementary
statement. Success would give Goldbach in a specific regime, which is a real
theorem.\\
2 & \tid{E1}: escape-or-reuse, or the bounded-charging lemma
(\S\ref{sec:E1}) &
Overwhelming data, explicit statement, and the missing ingredient is named
(bounded charging multiplicity). The most likely target to actually fall.\\
2 & Invariants of the boundary filtration (Q7) &
Purely combinatorial, independent of Goldbach, publishable on its own terms if
anything nontrivial exists.\\

The only open target carrying an explicit quantitative margin. Its original

Strictly stronger than Goldbach. Do not attack directly.\\

These are the external walls (\S\ref{sec:parity}). Working on them is working
on a different, famous problem.\\

\subsection{Experiments that would change the picture}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{$\Blow$ census to $10^{6}$.} Currently $6\cdot10^{4}$. Cost:
roughly quadratic in the limit as implemented; a smarter implementation should
use the fact that $B_0$ can be built once per $N$ from a shared sieve. A
seventh nonempty $\Blow$, or its absence at $10^{6}$, is decisive information
about whether the six are an artefact of smallness.
\item \textbf{Full upper-root census beyond $2\cdot10^{4}$.} The $301$ number
is the project's most-cited statistic and it is known only to $2\cdot10^{4}$.
Extending it to $10^{5}$ would test whether ``failing roots cluster at
$\Blow\ne\varnothing$ numbers'' persists.
\item \textbf{$J_R$ versus $\nu(R)$ scatter.} Directly tests L1 and is a few
lines on top of the existing world routine.
\item \textbf{$G_{\mathrm{esc}}$ to $10^{6}$.} Tests Q2 (does the margin
grow?). The current dyadic minima $1,1,1,1,1,1,2,2,3,3,3$ are suggestive but
the range is small.
\item \textbf{Phase-conditioned traversal statistics.} Does anything about the
traversal, beyond immediate success, depend on $\theta$? Currently unknown, and
$\rho_0$ is the only boundary invariant that varies between canonical worlds
(Q1).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Prior art and the novelty boundary}\label{sec:priorart}

\begin{warning}
\textbf{No claim of novelty is made anywhere in this file.} Establishing
novelty would require a separate literature review that has not been done. Any
label of the form ``derived here'' means \emph{derived from the corpus's own
definitions in this document}, not ``new in number theory''.
\end{warning}

\begin{navbox}
\textbf{The bibliography is a search record, not a citation list.} It
reproduces the Biblia's full list of $92$ sources plus three later additions.
Many entries are \emph{not} cited anywhere in the running text: they are there
so that a future model can see what has already been looked at and does not
repeat the search. An entry's presence means ``this was examined''; the
disposition tables of \S\ref{sec:litrejected}--\S\ref{sec:salvage} say with
what result. An entry's absence is the useful signal --- it means the project
has probably not looked there.
\end{navbox}

graph; recursive search through complement factors; valuation weights
$v_q(N-p)$; reachability, source and sink components, autonomous closed
components; the study of Goldbach pairs near $N/2$; elementary parent residue
classes and gcd identities. \src{NOV}

\subsection{The safe formulation}

\begin{summarybox}
Building on earlier work on Goldbach factorization graphs and on recursive
search through complement factors, we study the \emph{unconditional} selector
$p_0(N)=\min\{p\in\PP:p\ge N/2\}$ as a distinguished initial condition of the
full dynamics. To the best of our knowledge we have not found earlier work
using this selector --- without requiring $N-p_0$ to be prime --- as a
distinguished root, and systematically comparing its reachable bad world with
those of non-canonical roots. \emph{This is a report on the extent of a
literature search, not a claim of priority.}
\end{summarybox}


\section{Register of rejected literature applications}\label{sec:litrejected}

\begin{summarybox}
\textbf{This section exists so that a future model does not re-import a tool
the project has already tried and discarded.} Each row records a specific
\emph{application} of a specific external result, and why it does not do the
job here. A \KILLED\ row means the application is dead, \emph{not} that the
cited theorem is wrong. An \OPENs\ row means the tool may still be usable once
a stated precondition is met.
\end{summarybox}

$|Q|\sim N/\log N$ & \KILLED &
$Q=\PF(m_0)$, so $|Q|=\omega(m_0)$; a global density comparison does not apply
to the first front.\\
SMOOTH $\Rightarrow$ huge powerful part & \KILLED &
A SMOOTH row can be squarefree with many distinct small prime factors
(Warning~\ref{warn:twochannel}).\\
Positive density of squarefree values $\Rightarrow$ positive fraction of $Q$ &
\KILLED &
A result for all arguments, or all primes, does not transfer to the
\emph{adaptive} set of prime divisors of a single $m_0$.\\
Bombieri--Vinogradov on $Q$ & \KILLED &
The theorem controls primes in arithmetic progressions \emph{on average over
moduli}, not the distribution of the prime divisors of one specific $m_0$.\\
Filaseta--Trifonov as a uniform lower gap between consecutive powerful numbers
& \KILLED &
The short-interval squarefull-counting literature does not supply the universal
lower gap barrier that was assumed.\\
Darmon--Granville $\Rightarrow$ uniform bound for a varying family & \KILLED &
Coefficients, the difference and the curve itself vary with $N$; finiteness for
a fixed curve gives no uniformity.\\
Fixed-polynomial radical theorem with $F(X)=\prod_{q\in Q}(X-q)$ & \NEEDSVER &
Degree, height and the whole polynomial vary with $N$; an explicit uniform
dependence is required.\\
Pairwise classical $abc$ closes SMOOTH & \KILLED &
The shift $|q-r|$ can be of order $N$ and consumes the radical; without extra
global structure the required first-front lower bound does not arise.\\
Corvaja--Zannier greatest-prime-factor result & \OPENs &
Qualitatively supports escape, but gives no \emph{moving} threshold
$\PFp(N-q)\ge m_0/q$.\\

Usable only after freezing a small alphabet/rank inside one counterexample.
See also the vacuity result recorded in \S\ref{sec:v481routes}.\\
Gallagher's larger sieve \cite{Gallagher1971} & \OPENs &
Requires first showing that a large part of $Q$ occupies few classes modulo
many primes.\\
Multiplicity-order literature & \OPENs &
Known generic / almost-all results give no deterministic lower side for
specific ports modulo a specific $N$.\\
\end{longtable}

\subsection{Iteration-12 audit of $52$ primary sources}\label{sec:lit52}

\begin{statusbox}{cComp}
\textbf{An honest protocol instead of a fictitious ``1000''.} The scope and
metadata of \textbf{52 distinct primary sources} were checked; for 18 of them
the main theorems and the proof passages directly relevant to the project were
read as well. This is \emph{not} called ``reading 1000 papers'': automatically
fetching a thousand bibliographic records is not reading and does not raise
mathematical credibility. Below, mode \texttt{T} means ``theorems and relevant
sections'', mode \texttt{Z} means ``scope audit from abstract, introduction and
statements of results''.
\end{statusbox}

\small
\begin{longtable}{p{0.30\textwidth}p{0.06\textwidth}p{0.56\textwidth}}
\toprule
Sources & Mode & Conclusion for the project\\
\midrule
\endhead
\bottomrule
\endfoot
Bhowmik--Grimmelt \cite{BhowmikGrimmelt2026};
Li--Liu \cite{LiLiu2026} & T &
Goldbach still open. The first localises the barrier in minor arcs and
exceptional sets; the second gives $(1+1.9)$, not an adaptive traversal path.
Contributed calibration of the main gap.\\
Lichtman \cite{Lichtman2023}; Ford \cite{Ford2024} & T &
Strong distribution and the anatomy of shifted primes work \emph{on average}.
They do not give a pointwise choice from a reachable parent set.\\
Grimmelt--Ter\"av\"ainen \cite{GrimmeltTeravainen2025};
Halupczok \cite{Halupczok2012} & Z &
Transference and Goldbach in progressions / short intervals still leave an
exceptional set or averaged conditions. Useful as a weighting template,
insufficient pointwise.\\
Friedlander--Iwaniec \cite{FriedlanderIwaniec1998};
Polymath8 \cite{Polymath82014} & T &
\textbf{The most important analytic input:} breaking parity needs Type-II
bilinear information, not a linear sieve alone.\\
Green--Tao \cite{GreenTaoRestriction2004};
Bienvenu--Shao--Ter\"av\"ainen \cite{BienvenuShaoTeravainen2021} & T/Z &
Transference needs a pseudorandom majorant and positive relative density for a
\emph{fixed} configuration. Those hypotheses are not available for adaptive
reachability.\\
Ford \cite{Ford2014,Ford2021};
Assing--Blomer--Li \cite{AssingBlomerLi2020} & T &
Pratt-type closures and uniform Titchmarsh problems are the closest structural
analogues, but the relation $q\mid N-p$ moves with $N$.\\
Matom\"aki--Radziwi\l\l\ \cite{MatomakiRadziwill2016} & T/Z &
``Almost all'' short intervals give no certificate for every adaptive set.\\
Helfgott \cite{HelfgottMinor,HelfgottMajor};
Oliveira e Silva et al.\ \cite{OHP2014};
Huang--Li \cite{HuangLi2020}; Li \cite{Li2023} & T/Z &
Circle method, finite verification, EH and short intervals are important
calibration, but none synchronises a prime with the basin of $p_0$.\\
Evertse--Schlickewei--Schmidt \cite{ESS2004} & T/Z &
The number of $S$-unit solutions may depend only on dimension and rank, which
is better than fixed-$S$ constants. Application needs genuinely small rank; the
known zero-wrap branch is empty.\\
Vaaler \cite{Vaaler2012} & T/Z &
Heights may give a short multiplicative dependence \emph{after} an independent
rank and height bound. They do not handle the present $\delta$-forcing
automatically.\\
Amoroso--Sombra--Zannier \cite{AmorosoSombraZannier2014} & Z &
Sparse-polynomial / unlikely-intersection results work for fixed families;
Smith normal form is an excellent lattice algorithm but supplies no arithmetic
contradiction by itself.\\
Bugeaud \cite{Bugeaud2026}; Siksek--Stoll \cite{SiksekStoll2011};
Bennett--Siksek \cite{BennettSiksek2021,BennettSiksek2021b} & Z &
Effective once a specific curve or support is frozen; no uniformity for a
moving full SCC.\\
Bellman \cite{Bellman1958}; Karp \cite{Karp1978} & T &
The variational calculus of paths reduces to dynamic programming and a cycle
criterion. Gave the cycle--potential duality, not prime selection.\\
Prajna--Jadbabaie \cite{PrajnaJadbabaie2004} & Z &
Barrier certificates and occupation measures are the right shape for
reachability; on an SCC they need an arithmetic inequality that is missing.\\
Angeli--Philippe--Athanasopoulos--Jungers \cite{AngeliEtAl2016} & T/Z &
A complete Lyapunov function is constant on recurrent classes, which justifies
SCC compression. Multi-part versions do not evade the cycle barrier.\\
Friedman--Tillich \cite{FriedmanTillich2004};
Jiang--Lim--Yao--Ye \cite{JiangEtAl2011};
De Leenheer \cite{DeLeenheer2019}; Dodziuk \cite{Dodziuk1976} & T/Z &
Calculus and Hodge theory on graphs formalise the gradient and the cyclic part.
They contributed an exact no-go, not a primality theorem.\\
Bass \cite{Bass1992}; Rangarajan \cite{Rangarajan2017} & Z &
The graph zeta function and $\operatorname{coker}(I-A)$ repackage
determinant/Smith data. No new information about the rows $N-p$.\\
Z-transform / Koopman resolvent literature & Z &
Appropriate for a \emph{fixed} operator; the adaptive graph is not an LTI
system.\\
Discrete variational calculus literature & Z &
Gives stationarity equations, but for a sum of path costs it is not stronger
than Bellman.\\
\end{longtable}

\subsection{Frontier salvage audit (v4.81)}\label{sec:salvage}

The v4.81 attack performed a targeted salvage audit of the older Biblia
against the \emph{current} frontier. Its verdict in one sentence: \emph{the old
corpus contributed exactly one genuinely missing tool --- the gap-scale shadow
identity --- and one correct \textbf{shape} for the replacement frontier (the
smoothness budget); everything else in the neighbourhood of the current
obstruction is either already in the Core, or vacuous on the primitive branch,
or domain-mismatched.}

\endfoot
Prime-Gap Shadow Identity (Theorem~\ref{thm:shadow}) &
$N=2m+\delta$, $\delta=2h$; for $r\mid m$: $r\mid N-y\iff r\mid\delta-y$ &
\PROVEDs, re-proved from v4.80 definitions. Used to obtain the gap-scale form
of primitive load-one (V81.11). \emph{Not previously used in the v4.79/v4.80

Retention--Escape (Theorem~\ref{thm:retention}) &

\section{Literature verdicts and named missing lemmas}\label{sec:litverdicts}

\begin{statusbox}{cOpen}
\textbf{Iteration-157 verdict.} Checked: the Euclidean algorithm for positive
$2\times2$ matrices, the free monoid of positive $SL_2$, Conway--Coxeter friezes
\cite{ConwayCoxeter1973,BessenrodtHolmJorgensen2017}, unit equations
\cite{BeukersSchlickewei1996}, graph toric ideals
\cite{Villarreal1995,MartinezBernalVillarreal2008}, higher Lawrence
configurations \cite{SantosSturmfels2003}, cyclic congruence systems
\cite{Lagarias2010}, and prime-escape theorems from subset products
\cite{LeonettiTringali2014}. \emph{None} supplies a dynamical transition
preserving simultaneously $N$, the row identities, the full valuations and the
self-label roles. The nearest missing theorem is named:

\medskip
\textbf{Matched Euclidean Gluing Lemma} (\OPENs). To the word or matrix of one
packet one must assign an \emph{actual} continuation to the next packet in the
same system, preserving all roles, in such a way that a Euclidean measure
strictly decreases or an escape is forced.

\medskip
Without that lemma, word length, continued-fraction depth and matrix entry sums
are only \emph{static} coordinates. \textbf{They must not be used as Lyapunov
functions for self-label dynamics.} Compare Remark~\ref{rem:k1cf}, where the
same continued-fraction structure appears exactly and still yields no descent.
\end{statusbox}

\begin{statusbox}{cOpen}
\textbf{The one external input whose shape is known.} Across every audit the
same conclusion recurs: what is missing is \emph{Type-II bilinear information}
in the sense of the asymptotic sieve for primes
\cite{FriedlanderIwaniec1998,Polymath82014}. Every internal construction that
appeared to supply it turned out on inspection to be a Buchstab/sieve
decomposition or an affine reparametrisation
(\S\ref{sec:surv-cmft}). A future model should treat ``does this really produce
bilinear information, or is it an affine relabelling?'' as the first question to
ask of any new proposal.
\end{statusbox}

\section{What not to try again}\label{sec:donotretry}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Do not confuse selected finite programming with complete BFS.}
Compatible selected divisibility/valuation transcripts can be realised in
canonical $h=1$ worlds (Theorems~\ref{thm:facp}, \ref{thm:fbtu}), but this does
not control unprescribed cofactors. Therefore a selected BAD path/cycle is not
a complete BAD neighbourhood. The old blanket finite-local wall is
scope-corrected, not a prohibition on every bounded-depth complete-frontier
theorem.
\item \textbf{Do not restart the programme in new coordinates.} Five successor
theories have already done exactly that (\S\ref{sec:successors}). A new
coordinate system does not change what information is available.
\item \textbf{Do not prove a bound in one functional and use it in another.}
This is the single defect blocking TD, P1$^{\mathrm{br}}$ and K1 simultaneously.
``Morally the same'' and ``dominates on average'' are not the same functional.
\item \textbf{Do not treat canonical failure as Goldbach failure.} Class-D
theorems (upper-half compression, symmetric fracture, forbidden offset band)
require $\Good_N=\varnothing$ and are unusable under canonical failure alone.
\tid{FAIL-UPPERHALF-SCOPE-001}
\item \textbf{Do not quote a count without its domain.} Which roots, which
complements, unit rows included or not. \tid{FAIL-CENSUS-DOMAIN-001},
\tid{FAIL-UNIT-COMPLEMENT-001}
\item \textbf{Do not promote a scan.} $0$ failures to $10^{7}$ is not evidence
for X1; it is the statement that X1 has no small counterexample.
\item \textbf{Do not use the mass of the boundary holes.} $O_k(\log N)$ against
a block mass of order $t_k\log(x/h_k)$. Any argument routed through hole mass
is dead before it starts. \tid{FAIL-P0-ZEROHOLE-ESSENTIAL-001}
\item \textbf{Do not strengthen the reflection gate to activation.} $N=242$ is
final: both lower mirrors are composite and no active reflected row exists.
The phase diagram explains why (Type~I). \tid{FAIL-REFLECTION-ACTIVATION-001}
\item \textbf{Do not widen the reflected block.} The endpoint pair has
difference exactly $2h$ and is not covered by strict non-reuse.
\tid{FAIL-BROADBLOCK-ENDPOINT}
\item \textbf{Do not use the Euler defect in normalisation (N1) or (N2).}
Refuted here: $6\,044$ and $3\,804$ violations respectively for
$N\le6\cdot10^{4}$ (\S\ref{sec:euler}).
\item \textbf{Do not attack X1 or Goldbach directly.} X1 is strictly stronger
than Goldbach for each $N$.
\item \textbf{Do not route around parity by enlarging the graph.} The
obstruction lives in the sieve information, not in the graph
(\S\ref{sec:parity}).
\item \textbf{Do not search for a fixed-rank law in the first mirror alone.}
Every fixed rank realises every odd mirror $m\ge3$, and exact same-$(k,m)$
certificates have opposite eventual verdicts.  Any viable rule must use
ambient $N$-dependent information.
\item \textbf{Do not use a fixed finite valuation/label projection to isolate
$p_0$.}  Run H synchronises arbitrary prescribed finite valuations across
$p_0,\ldots,p_K$ at the same $N$ infinitely often.
\item \textbf{Do not substitute the moving basin $B_N$ into a fixed-$S$
theorem.}  The quantifiers are different; all constants in the
Matveev/BHP separation theorem depend on the fixed alphabet.
\item \textbf{Do not extend the bounded-mirror transplant scan by increasing
only the $N$ cutoff.}  For $m\le3053,k\le74$ the finite-fibre theorem proves
the entire realisation box ends at $N=7324$.
\item \textbf{Do not re-prove what is already \PROVEDs.} Use it by ID from
Chapter~\ref{ch:registry} and the delta registry
\S\ref{sec:postDH-registry}.
\item \textbf{Do not raise a status.} If you prove something, add a row; do not
edit an old one.
\end{enumerate}

\section{What currently looks best}\label{sec:looksbest}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Selector--moving-basin interaction.}  This is the binding target.
Use
\[
 p_k(N)\text{ fails}\iff\rad(N-p_k(N))\mid R_N
\]
together with the fact that $p_0$ is the maximal prime-backed mirror selector.
A useful theorem must constrain $B_N$ in a way that depends on this actual
location, not on a fixed external alphabet.
\item \textbf{Uniform moving-support geometry.}  The strongest analytic
ingredient now available is the Matveev/BHP separation of two complete
$S$-smooth early mirrors.  Search for a bound on the size/height/spacing of
$B_N$ that makes this statement uniform over an admissible moving family.
A contradiction between a lower growth requirement and an upper
rank/mirror-capacity requirement would be genuinely global.
\item \textbf{Construct a new complete failure host.}  The six known hosts
have been mined heavily, and all fixed mirrors $m\le3053$ in the selected
rank box are exhausted.  A new closed BAD basin would provide independent
arithmetic data and immediately test whether the apparent survivor ranks are
accidental.
\item \textbf{Exploit low-gap support disjointness only when coupled to
$B_N$.}  Shared child factors force $2q$-spaced roots; low-gap roots can have
pairwise disjoint initial supports.  By itself this does not imply success,
but a basin-capacity theorem consuming many disjoint supports could.
\item \textbf{Keep the run-D Diophantine branch as a secondary exact target.}
The $q=3,h=1$ three-label branch is killed and monomial returns are more
restricted.  Further exact closure elimination is useful only if it feeds
the moving-basin programme rather than becoming another local invariant.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{warning}[What does \emph{not} look good, despite appearances]
The genealogical layer is the most beautiful part of the project and the most
likely to mislead. It is exact, it has genuine converses, and it does not imply
anything dynamical --- and Warning~\ref{warn:ledger}(2) raises the real
possibility that it cannot, because ``$\kappa_{\mathrm{gen}}(r)=0$'' may carry
exactly the information ``$r$ is the first upper prime'' and nothing more.
Before building on it, decide whether your argument would survive that
equivalence.
\end{warning}

\section{The five most valuable next moves}\label{sec:fivemoves}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Prove a moving-$B_N$ capacity/height inequality with selector
input.}  The desired statement should combine the complete closure equations
for $B_N$ with the fact that $p_0$ is the first upper prime and
$\PF(N-p_0)\subseteq B_N$ under failure.
\item \textbf{Try to uniformise H2.}  Replace ``fixed finite $S$'' in the
early-rank smooth-support separation theorem by a quantitatively controlled
family $S_N$ large enough to contain a hypothetical $B_N$.  Record exactly
where the Matveev constant destroys the argument if it cannot be done.
\item \textbf{Search for a new EAC/BAD-basin host, not for more old-mirror
transplants.}  If one is found, compute the full upper-root spectrum and ask
whether any of $10,14,26,28,30,62,63,71,74$ finally intersects it.
\item \textbf{Develop a simultaneous-failure spacing theorem.}  Combine
$\gcd(N-r,N-s)=\gcd(N-r,s-r)$, the $2q$ shared-factor spacing law, and the
fixed-gap $S$-unit count to bound how many low-rank roots can all be
$B_N$-smooth in one host.
\item \textbf{Only then return to the canonical low-gap Diophantine branch.}
Use the run-D four-label and order-$\ge3$ theorems as exact local inputs to a
complete-basin argument; do not search isolated congruences for their own
sake.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{warning}[Two moves demoted by the v4.81 result]
Anything of the shape ``find new selected storage disjoint from
$\mathscr C_Q$ at fixed positive logarithmic scale'' is now known to be
\emph{insufficient by construction}, not merely unproved
(Corollary~\ref{cor:sizedeath}); and anything of the shape ``exploit an overlap
between the reflected block and the selected family'' is known to be
charge-free (Theorem~\ref{thm:overlapfree}). Do not spend a run on either.
\end{warning}

\begin{summarybox}
\textbf{Final orientation after 2026-09-07H.} Binary Goldbach is \OPENs.
Universal canonical success \textbf{(H-$p_0$)} is \OPENs\ and is strictly
stronger.  The old finite-selected-transcript architecture is \SUPERSEDEDs,
and runs G--H now rule out a much broader family of fixed first-row and fixed
finite-label explanations.  The live object is the incidence between the
actual root selector and the complete moving BAD basin $B_N$.  Fixed $(k,m)$
fibres, bounded old-mirror scans, and fixed-$S$ arguments have sharply defined
limits and must not be extrapolated past them.  Future work should begin at
\S\ref{sec:postDH-frontier}; the raw E/F and D--H sources are preserved
losslessly in the appendices so later models can audit every scope decision.
\end{summarybox}

\section{The data generator}\label{sec:appgen}

The following script reproduces \emph{every} number marked \VERIFCOMP\ in this
file. It has no external dependencies (standard library, Python 3.9+). Blocks
EXP1--EXP8 correspond to the identifiers in the provenance table of
\S\ref{sec:provenance}. Comments are the project's own, transliterated to
ASCII; the executable code is unchanged.

\begin{lstlisting}[style=code,language=Python,
  caption={\texttt{p0\_experiments.py} --- complete self-contained generator
  for every \VERIFCOMP\ number in this file.},
  label={lst:experiments}]
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
p0_experiments.py -- JEDEN samowystarczalny skrypt odtwarzajacy KAZDA liczbe
oznaczona COMPUTATIONAL w dossier p_0 oraz dane wszystkich rysunkow.

Bez zaleznosci zewnetrznych (tylko biblioteka standardowa Pythona 3.9+).

    python3 p0_experiments.py --scan 10000000 --census 20000 --phase 200000 \
                              --fixedpoint 60000 --json dane.json

Domyslne, szybkie ustawienia (kilka minut):
    python3 p0_experiments.py

Kazdy blok EXP wypisuje dokladny zakres, ktory jest czescia twierdzenia
obliczeniowego -- zgodnie z regula "nigdy nie cytuj liczby bez jej domeny".
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from array import array
from collections import Counter, deque


# ===================================================================== sito
def build(limit):
    spf = array('i', range(limit + 1))
    i = 2
    while i * i <= limit:
        if spf[i] == i:
            for j in range(i * i, limit + 1, i):
                if spf[j] == j:
                    spf[j] = i
        i += 1
    isp = bytearray(limit + 1)
    for n in range(2, limit + 1):
        isp[n] = 1 if spf[n] == n else 0
    return spf, isp


def pf(n, spf):
    out = []
    while n > 1:
        q = spf[n]
        out.append(q)
        while n % q == 0:
            n //= q
    return out


def bigomega(n, spf):
    c = 0
    while n > 1:
        q = spf[n]
        while n % q == 0:
            n //= q
            c += 1
    return c


class Env:
    """Sito + selektory kanoniczne + dwa tryby przejscia."""

    def __init__(self, limit):
        self.L = limit
        self.spf, self.isp = build(limit)

    def nextp(self, n):
        m = n + 1
        while m <= self.L and not self.isp[m]:
            m += 1
        return m

    def prevp(self, n):
        m = n - 1
        while m >= 2 and not self.isp[m]:
            m -= 1
        return m if m >= 2 else -1

    def p0(self, N):
        x = N // 2
        return x if self.isp[x] else self.nextp(x)

    def census(self, N, r):
        """tryb census: (sukces, glebokosc, liczba wierzcholkow)"""
        if 2 * r == N:
            return True, 0, 1
        q = deque([(r, 0)])
        seen = {r}
        nodes = 0
        while q:
            p, d = q.popleft()
            nodes += 1
            n = N - p
            if n >= 2 and self.isp[n]:
                return True, d, nodes
            while n > 1:
                f = self.spf[n]
                while n % f == 0:
                    n //= f
                if N % f and f not in seen:
                    seen.add(f)
                    q.append((f, d + 1))
        return False, -1, nodes

    def world(self, N, r):
        """tryb world: (sukces, glebokosc, |R|, liczba krawedzi GOOD)"""
        if 2 * r == N or (N - r >= 2 and self.isp[N - r]):
            return True, 0, 0, 0
        q = deque([(r, 0)])
        queued = {r}
        R, esc, ok, dep = set(), 0, False, None
        while q:
            p, d = q.popleft()
            if p in R:
                continue
            n = N - p
            if n >= 2 and self.isp[n]:
                if not ok:
                    ok, dep = True, d
                continue
            R.add(p)
            while n > 1:
                f = self.spf[n]
                while n % f == 0:
                    n //= f
                if N % f:
                    if N - f >= 2 and self.isp[N - f]:
                        esc += 1
                        if not ok:
                            ok, dep = True, d + 1
                    elif f not in R and f not in queued:
                        queued.add(f)
                        q.append((f, d + 1))
        return ok, dep, len(R), esc


# ============================================ EXP1: wyczerpujacy skan p_0
def exp1_scan(limit):
    """Kazde parzyste 4<=N<=limit, korzen kanoniczny, tryb census."""
    e = Env(limit)
    fails, tot, s = [], 0, 0
    maxn, maxd, hist = (0, 0), (0, 0), Counter()
    for N in range(4, limit + 1, 2):
        r = e.p0(N)
        ok, d, nodes = e.census(N, r)
        tot += 1
        s += nodes
        if not ok:
            fails.append((N, r))
        else:
            hist[d] += 1
            if d > maxd[0]:
                maxd = (d, N)
        if nodes > maxn[0]:
            maxn = (nodes, N)
    return {"limit": limit, "cases": tot, "failures": len(fails),
            "failure_list": fails[:20], "mean_nodes": s / tot,
            "max_nodes": maxn, "max_depth": maxd,
            "depth_hist": {str(k): hist[k] for k in sorted(hist)}}


# ================================== EXP2: ablacja p_0 -> p_k (werdykt roota)
def exp2_ablation(limit, kmax=6):
    e = Env(limit)
    comp = [0] * (kmax + 1)
    unit = [0] * (kmax + 1)
    first = {}
    for N in range(4, limit + 1, 2):
        p = e.p0(N)
        for k in range(kmax + 1):
            if p >= N:
                break
            ok, _, _ = e.census(N, p)
            if not ok:
                if N - p == 1:
                    unit[k] += 1
                else:
                    comp[k] += 1
                    first.setdefault(k, (N, p))
            p = e.nextp(p)
    return {"limit": limit, "kmax": kmax, "composite_complement_failures": comp,
            "unit_row_failures": unit,
            "first": {str(k): v for k, v in sorted(first.items())}}


# ================= EXP3: census WSZYSTKICH zawodzacych gornych korzeni
def exp3_upper_census(limit):
    e = Env(limit)
    rows, unit = [], 0
    for N in range(4, limit + 1, 2):
        r0 = e.p0(N)
        p = r0
        while p < N:
            if e.isp[p] and N % p:
                if N - p == 1:
                    unit += 1
                elif not e.census(N, p)[0]:
                    rows.append((N, p, p == r0))
            p += 1
            while p < N and not e.isp[p]:
                p += 1
    Ns = sorted({r[0] for r in rows})
    return {"limit": limit, "failed_roots": len(rows), "unit_rows": unit,
            "N_values": Ns, "per_N": {str(n): sum(1 for r in rows if r[0] == n)
                                      for n in Ns},
            "canonical_among_them": sum(1 for r in rows if r[2])}


# ================================== EXP4: margines ucieczki G_esc
def exp4_margin(limit):
    e = Env(limit)
    ones, sizes = [], []
    hist = Counter()
    maxW = (0, 0)
    dyad = {}
    for N in range(4, limit + 1, 2):
        r = e.p0(N)
        ok, _, W, esc = e.world(N, r)
        if W == 0:
            continue
        hist[esc] += 1
        sizes.append(W)
        if W > maxW[0]:
            maxW = (W, N)
        if esc == 1:
            ones.append((N, r, W))
        if W >= 3:
            dyad.setdefault(N.bit_length(), []).append(esc)
    return {"limit": limit, "bad_p0_worlds": len(sizes),
            "G_esc_hist_small": {str(k): hist[k] for k in sorted(hist) if k <= 6},
            "margin_one_all": [o[0] for o in ones],
            "margin_one_W_ge_3": [(N, r, W) for N, r, W in ones if W >= 3],
            "max_world": maxW,
            "dyadic_min_G": {str(k): min(v) for k, v in sorted(dyad.items())}}


# ===================== EXP5: trichotomia fazowa i dwukierunkowa ranga rho_0
def exp5_phase(limit):
    e = Env(limit)
    primes = [n for n in range(2, limit + 1) if e.isp[n]]
    idx = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(primes)}
    types = Counter()
    imm = Counter()
    viol = Counter()
    rho_hist = Counter()
    rho_theta = {}
    theta_hist = Counter()
    for N in range(6, limit + 1, 2):
        x = N // 2
        P = e.p0(N)
        h, m0 = P - x, N - P
        Pm = e.prevp(P)
        G = P - Pm
        if m0 - Pm != G - 2 * h:
            viol["identity"] += 1
        t = "diag" if h == 0 else ("I" if 2 * h < G else
                                   ("II" if 2 * h == G else "III"))
        types[t] += 1
        theta_hist[int(20 * h / G)] += 1
        if e.isp[m0] or m0 == 1:
            imm[t] += 1
            if t == "I":
                viol["typeI_prime_m0"] += 1
        if t == "II" and m0 != Pm:
            viol["typeII"] += 1
        if t == "III":
            js, tt = h - G // 2, (h - 1) // 2
            if not (1 <= js <= tt and m0 + 2 * js == Pm):
                viol["typeIII_mirror"] += 1
            if N % Pm == 0:
                viol["typeIII_inactive"] += 1
        if h >= 3:
            tt = (h - 1) // 2
            direct = sum(1 for j in range(1, tt + 1) if e.isp[m0 + 2 * j])
            i0, f, r = idx[P], 0, 1
            while i0 - r >= 0:
                D = P - primes[i0 - r]
                if D >= 2 * h:
                    break
                if D > h:
                    f += 1
                r += 1
            if direct != f:
                viol["rho0"] += 1
            rho_hist[direct] += 1
            rho_theta.setdefault(round(h / G, 2), []).append(direct)
    return {"limit": limit, "type_counts": dict(types),
            "immediate_success_by_type": dict(imm),
            "violations": dict(viol),
            "theta_hist_20": {str(k): theta_hist[k] for k in sorted(theta_hist)},
            "rho0_hist": {str(k): rho_hist[k] for k in sorted(rho_hist)},
            "rho0_mean_by_theta": {str(k): round(sum(v) / len(v), 4)
                                   for k, v in sorted(rho_theta.items())
                                   if len(v) >= 50}}


# ===================================== EXP6: filtracja brzegu (embedding)
def exp6_filtration(limit, kmax=6):
    e = Env(limit)
    checked = viol = 0
    for N in range(50, limit + 1, 2):
        x = N // 2
        roots, p = [], e.p0(N)
        for _ in range(kmax + 1):
            if p >= N:
                break
            roots.append(p)
            p = e.nextp(p)
        for k in range(len(roots) - 1):
            pk, pk1 = roots[k], roots[k + 1]
            s = (pk1 - pk) // 2
            tk, tk1 = (pk - x - 1) // 2, (pk1 - x - 1) // 2
            if tk1 != tk + s:
                viol += 1
            for i in range(1, tk + 1):
                checked += 1
                if pk1 - 2 * (i + s) != pk - 2 * i:
                    viol += 1
    return {"limit": limit, "checked": checked, "violations": viol}


# ===================================== EXP7: fixed point B_N^low
def exp7_fixedpoint(limit):
    e = Env(limit)
    out = []
    for N in range(6, limit + 1, 2):
        cap = N // 3
        B, rows = set(), {}
        for p in range(3, cap + 1, 2):
            if not e.isp[p] or N % p == 0:
                continue
            v = N - p
            if v < 2 or e.isp[v]:
                continue
            B.add(p)
            rows[p] = pf(v, e.spf)
        changed = True
        while changed:
            changed = False
            for p in list(B):
                for q in rows[p]:
                    if N % q and q not in B:
                        B.discard(p)
                        changed = True
                        break
        if B:
            out.append((N, sorted(B)))
    return {"limit": limit, "nonempty_count": len(out),
            "nonempty": [(N, B) for N, B in out]}


# ============================ EXP8: ablacja obserwabli p_0 vs p_1
def exp8_observables(limit):
    e = Env(limit)
    acc = {k: {n: [] for n in ("depth", "world", "esc", "Omega", "ret", "kap")}
           | {"fail": 0, "n": 0, "pp": []} for k in (0, 1)}
    for N in range(50, limit + 1, 2):
        x = N // 2
        r0 = e.p0(N)
        r1 = e.nextp(r0)
        for k, r in ((0, r0), (1, r1)):
            if r >= N or N - r <= 1:
                continue
            m = N - r
            ok, dep, W, esc = e.world(N, r)
            a = acc[k]
            a["n"] += 1
            if not ok:
                a["fail"] += 1
            if dep is not None:
                a["depth"].append(dep)
            a["world"].append(W)
            a["esc"].append(esc)
            a["Omega"].append(bigomega(m, e.spf))
            Q = pf(m, e.spf)
            Qs = set(Q)
            a["pp"].append(max(Q) / m)
            a["ret"].append(sum(1 for q in Q for z in pf(N - q, e.spf) if z in Qs))
            hh = r - x
            tt = (hh - 1) // 2
            a["kap"].append(sum(1 for j in range(1, tt + 1) if e.isp[r - 2 * j]))

    def st(v):
        v = sorted(v)
        return {"mean": round(sum(v) / len(v), 4), "median": v[len(v) // 2],
                "max": v[-1]}
    return {"limit": limit,
            **{f"p{k}": {n: st(acc[k][n]) for n in
                         ("depth", "world", "esc", "Omega", "ret", "kap")}
               | {"fail": acc[k]["fail"], "n": acc[k]["n"],
                  "Pplus_over_m_mean": round(sum(acc[k]["pp"]) / len(acc[k]["pp"]), 5),
                  "Omega_hist": {str(a): b for a, b in
                                 sorted(Counter(acc[k]["Omega"]).items())},
                  "depth_hist": {str(a): b for a, b in
                                 sorted(Counter(acc[k]["depth"]).items())}}
               for k in (0, 1)}}


# ===================================================== pojedynczy swiadkowie
def witnesses(limit=1_100_000):
    """Wszyscy pojedynczy swiadkowie cytowani w dossier."""
    e = Env(limit)

    def fac(n):
        c = Counter(pf(n, e.spf))
        d = Counter()
        m = n
        for q in c:
            while m % q == 0:
                m //= q
                d[q] += 1
        return dict(sorted(d.items()))

    w = {}
    for N in (124, 242, 240, 2200, 103344, 364844, 14198, 11822):
        P = e.p0(N)
        Pm = e.prevp(P)
        h, G, m0 = P - N // 2, P - Pm, N - P
        ok, dep, W, esc = e.world(N, P)
        t = (h - 1) // 2
        w[str(N)] = {"p0": P, "h": h, "G": G, "prev_prime": Pm, "m0": m0,
                     "m0_fac": {str(a): b for a, b in fac(m0).items()},
                     "type": "diag" if h == 0 else
                             ("I" if 2 * h < G else
                              ("II" if 2 * h == G else "III")),
                     "kappa_gen": sum(1 for j in range(1, t + 1)
                                      if e.isp[P - 2 * j]),
                     "rho0": sum(1 for j in range(1, t + 1) if e.isp[m0 + 2 * j]),
                     "verdict": "SUCCESS" if ok else "FAILURE",
                     "depth": dep, "world": W, "escapes": esc}
    w["2200_core"] = {"2200-3": 2200 - 3, "13^3": 13 ** 3,
                      "2200-13": 2200 - 13, "3^7": 3 ** 7,
                      "shift": 3 ** 7 - 3 == 13 ** 3 - 13 == 2184}
    N = 1_000_000
    Q, R = (61, 67, 73), (113, 179, 599)
    w["K33"] = {"N": N, "Q": Q, "R": R,
                "all_entries_prime": all(e.isp[N - q * r] for q in Q for r in R),
                "all_factor_vertices_bad": all(not e.isp[N - v] for v in Q + R)}
    w["cells"] = [{"P": P, "G": P - e.prevp(P),
                   "all_h_have_p0_eq_P": all(e.p0(2 * (P - h)) == P
                                             for h in range(0, P - e.prevp(P)))}
                  for P in (67, 127, 1009, 104729)]
    return w


# ================================================================== driver
def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--scan", type=int, default=1_000_000)
    ap.add_argument("--ablation", type=int, default=200_000)
    ap.add_argument("--census", type=int, default=20_000)
    ap.add_argument("--margin", type=int, default=200_000)
    ap.add_argument("--phase", type=int, default=200_000)
    ap.add_argument("--filtration", type=int, default=20_000)
    ap.add_argument("--fixedpoint", type=int, default=20_000)
    ap.add_argument("--observables", type=int, default=200_000)
    ap.add_argument("--json", default="dane_p0.json")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    out = {
        "EXP1_scan": exp1_scan(a.scan),
        "EXP2_ablation": exp2_ablation(a.ablation),
        "EXP3_upper_census": exp3_upper_census(a.census),
        "EXP4_margin": exp4_margin(a.margin),
        "EXP5_phase": exp5_phase(a.phase),
        "EXP6_filtration": exp6_filtration(a.filtration),
        "EXP7_fixedpoint": exp7_fixedpoint(a.fixedpoint),
        "EXP8_observables": exp8_observables(a.observables),
        "witnesses": witnesses(),
    }
    with open(a.json, "w") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=1)
    print(json.dumps({k: (v if k == "witnesses" else
                          {kk: vv for kk, vv in v.items()
                           if not isinstance(vv, (list, dict)) or len(str(vv)) < 400})
                      for k, v in out.items()}, indent=1)[:6000])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
\end{lstlisting}

\section{The Euler-defect check}\label{sec:appeuler}

This script produced the refutations of normalisations (N1) and (N2) and the
zero-violation results for (N3) and (N4) in \S\ref{sec:euler}. It is new in
this file.

\begin{lstlisting}[style=code,language=Python,
  caption={\texttt{euler\_check.py} --- tests the four candidate normalisations
  of the layered Euler defect on all canonical failed worlds.},
  label={lst:eulercheck}]
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Test the four candidate normalisations of the layered Euler defect
on every canonical failed world with 50 <= N <= LIMIT."""
from collections import deque

LIM = 200001
spf = list(range(LIM))
i = 2
while i * i < LIM:
    if spf[i] == i:
        for j in range(i * i, LIM, i):
            if spf[j] == j:
                spf[j] = i
    i += 1


def fac(n):
    f = {}
    while n > 1:
        p = spf[n]
        e = 0
        while n % p == 0:
            n //= p
            e += 1
        f[p] = e
    return f


def isp(n):
    return n >= 2 and spf[n] == n


def world(N):
    """Canonical stopped traversal, world mode.
    Returns (R, rows, depth, success, root) or None when the root wins
    immediately (diagonal case or N - p0 prime)."""
    x = N // 2
    r = x if isp(x) else None
    if r is None:
        p = x + 1
        while not isp(p):
            p += 1
        r = p
    if 2 * r == N:
        return None
    if isp(N - r):
        return None
    q = deque([(r, 0)])
    seen = {r}
    R, rows, depth = set(), {}, {}
    ok = False
    while q:
        p, d = q.popleft()
        if p in R:
            continue
        if isp(N - p):
            ok = True
            continue
        R.add(p)
        rows[p] = fac(N - p)
        depth[p] = d
        for c in sorted(rows[p]):
            if N % c == 0:
                continue
            if isp(N - c):
                ok = True
                continue
            if c not in R and c not in seen:
                seen.add(c)
                q.append((c, d + 1))
    return (R, rows, depth, ok, r)


bad = [0, 0, 0, 0]
first = [None, None, None, None]
tested = 0
for N in range(50, 60001, 2):
    w = world(N)
    if w is None:
        continue
    R, rows, depth, ok, r = w
    if not R:
        continue
    tested += 1
    nu = len(set(depth.values()))
    # (N1) row-excess form
    eta1 = sum(sum(rows[p].values()) - len([c for c in rows[p] if c in R])
               for p in R)
    # (N2) valuation / reuse split
    d = {}
    kap = {}
    for p in R:
        for q_, e_ in rows[p].items():
            if N % q_ == 0:
                continue
            d[q_] = d.get(q_, 0) + e_
            kap[q_] = kap.get(q_, 0) + 1
    eta2 = sum(d[q_] - kap[q_] for q_ in d)
    nu2 = sum(kap[q_] - 1 for q_ in d)
    # (N3) active-mass form ; (N4) trivial form
    mass = sum(d.values())
    eta4 = sum(sum(rows[p].values()) - 1 for p in R)
    target = len(R) + 1
    for k, val in enumerate((eta1 + nu, eta2 + nu2, mass, eta4 + nu)):
        if val < target:
            bad[k] += 1
            if first[k] is None:
                first[k] = (N, len(R), val, target)
print("worlds tested:", tested)
for k, name in enumerate(("N1", "N2", "N3", "N4")):
    print(name, "violations:", bad[k], "first:", first[k])
\end{lstlisting}
